chapters.title: Chapter 1 -1-Reborn Five Times, Obtaining the Talent: Millionfold Boost
paragraphs: Daniel’s eyes snapped open.
His right hand clenched instinctively, only for the sensation in his grip to feel strangely off.
He lowered his head and looked at the hard object in his hand.
"A... phone!?"
The lock screen lit up instantly:
Sunday, August 30, 2030, 9:00 AM.
Sunlight spilled into the room. From the fast-food place downstairs came the rich smell of Orleans roast chicken...
Upstairs, the neighbor was gaming so hard the floor kept thudding overhead, all while shouting at the top of his lungs.
"Mommy, he’s hacking! Show me your legs and bless me with the Strength to kill a god..."
Daniel quickly came back to himself.
But even so, he remained leaning against the headboard, sitting there for a full ten minutes.
His mind was still replaying what he had just seen.
Invisible tentacles had blotted out the entire sky.
The corpse of the Elven Goddess hung in midair, still clutching a bow broken clean in two.
The Dwarf King had been smashed into the city wall by his own anvil, wedged in so deep no one could pry him back out.
The skeletal remains of the Beast God sprawled hollow-eyed across the land...
Dozens of gods had been slaughtered, enslaved, and strung up in the heavens like trophies.
And on the ground lay countless goblins, beastfolk, seafolk...
These foreign races had willingly degenerated into playthings of the Evil God, taking pleasure in butchering and devouring humanity, their hands drenched in endless blood.
At Daniel’s feet, humanity’s great banner had already fallen, burned down until only a palm-sized scrap remained.
[Lv. 999, Faustus]
[Class: Ancient Forbidden Archmage]
Blood flowed from his left shoulder, staining his clothes red all the way down his ribs.
The flesh on the hand gripping his bow had split open, leaving it a mangled, bloody mess.
Even the Star-Chasing Staff in his hand was covered in cracks, as if it might shatter into pieces at any moment.
And then, the indescribable existence in the sky spoke.
Its voice came from countless dimensions and directions at once, striking directly into Daniel’s mind.
"Hehehe... long ago, your human race produced a fool who tried to tear open godhood with his bare hands."
"So I fed both him and his name to the Void. You will be no exception."
Daniel ignored it.
He lowered his head and glanced at his MP bar, estimating how many forbidden spells he had left in him.
The next instant, he raised a hand and cast Starfall instantly. Nine meteors, trailing blazing tails, crashed down and slammed into the eyelid of that incomprehensible being.
The meteors shattered into dust.
The Evil God did not even blink.
Seeing that, Daniel gritted his teeth and chanted Void Sever. Space split open into a black fissure, tearing toward the Evil God.
But before the attack could even get close, it was forcibly destroyed by some unknown Strength.
Daniel tightened his grip on the staff, his expression complicated.
This staff had been shoved into his hand by a comrade in their final moments. Back then, blood had splattered all over Daniel’s neck, and in the end, his friend had only managed to say one sentence.
"Daniel, I’m leaving that big dumb bastard to you!"
Daniel gave a bitter laugh and poured the last of his mana into the staff.
Crack—!
The staff exploded from the middle, fragments spraying across his face.
Daniel looked at the shattered pieces and merely spat to the side.
Then he raised his head and looked at the gargantuan existence in the sky, so vast it defied imagination, and let both arms fall loosely to his sides.
As casually as if he had just finished a team raid, he said in an easy tone,
"Forget it. Still can’t kill this damn thing."
The next second, a tentacle large enough to blot out the heavens smashed down toward him.
"Damn... this makes four times already."
Daniel jolted upright against the headboard, unexpectedly calm.
He went to the bathroom and splashed water on his face. The face reflected in the mirror was clean and youthful, and his hands were free of even the slightest callus.
Beep! Beep! Beep!
"Cross-era game Stellar will officially begin open beta at 10:00 AM! All game enthusiasts, please prepare to register!"
"Stellar..."
Daniel stared at the unfamiliar yet deeply familiar push notification on his phone screen and froze for a moment.
He had already seen this exact same message four times.
Still, he quickly adjusted his mood, returned to his room, and lay down in the gaming pod that had only been delivered yesterday.
Stellar!
This game had appeared out of nowhere on August 15, occupying the screens of every electronic device in the world.
No teaser.
No press conference.
No official website.
It had even forcefully hijacked the evening news on the Imperial Capital channel.
For a while, countless people guessed that some gaming giant had secretly been cooking up the ultimate bombshell for years.
But Daniel knew better.
It absolutely was not.
Three years later, this game would no longer be just a game.
All those people outside scrambling for jobs, earning baby formula money, or wandering around high out of their minds—they would all be forced into a completely different way of life.
But thinking about that now was pointless.
At this moment, only one thing was on Daniel’s mind:
To seize every single opportunity to grow stronger using his knowledge of the future.
"Login."
[Ding! Connection successful!]
[Welcome to—Stellar!]
Daniel felt a sudden flash before his eyes.
When he opened them again, beneath his feet stretched a dazzling river of stars.
Stellar Plaza.
The place was packed like a wet market, with no end in sight.
Some people craned their necks up at the ceiling in amazement. Some were freaking out in disbelief. Some were even squatting down to touch the floor, checking whether this was really full-dive VR.
Daniel didn’t bother looking.
He strode straight into the towering Stellar Hall ahead of him, and the noise and chaos around him vanished in an instant.
A cold system prompt rang out immediately.
[Please enter your game ID!]
He typed with practiced ease:
"Faustus."
It wasn’t that he was trying to be dramatic. He had just grown used to it after a few hundred years.
He had learned the word back in high school Latin class, even though he had failed that class more than once. Still, the word had stuck with him.
It meant:
"the lucky one."
Back in guild chat, those idiots used to call him things like "Faux-dog," "Faust-ass," and "Faus-tard."
Now that nobody called him that anymore, he actually felt a little unaccustomed to it.
[Ding! ID available. Beginning first Talent draw.]
An animation began spinning above the selection platform, while the draw rates floated at the bottom right.
SSS-rank Talent: 0.00000000001%
SS-rank Talent: 0.000000001%
S-rank Talent: 0.0000003%
A-rank Talent: ...
The probabilities for every Talent, from the highest SSS-rank down to the lowest E-rank, were listed there.
But this time, Daniel did not rush to draw.
Instead, his gaze fell on the tiny, easily overlooked line of text at the very bottom of the wheel.
[Please enter redemption code!]
A complicated look flashed through Daniel’s eyes.
The truth was, he had already gone through four rebirths.
He had spent a full two hundred years in the world of Stellar.
And in all that time, he had never seen a single person use this feature.

The Earth Council had never officially released any code. The forum had argued for thousands of pages without getting anywhere. That input box had basically been nothing more than decoration, sitting there untouched.
The code required exactly twenty-four characters.
And for some reason, four segments of runes surfaced in Daniel’s mind.
They were the bizarre symbols carved into the reward stele each time he had cleared an SSS-rank Forbidden Secret Realm for the first time across his four rebirths.
They were neither Elvish nor Dragon Tongue, nor even the rarest Ancient God script.
He had asked nearly every race he could find about them.
None recognized them.
But Daniel had always felt that these things had to mean something.
So he had memorized them by force.
Four rune segments.
Six symbols each.
Twenty-four in total.
He raised his hand and began writing them stroke by stroke, his fingertip trailing a faint golden light.
As the final rune took shape, the lighting inside the entire Stellar Hall dimmed for three full seconds.
[Ding! Congratulations, player "Faustus," for obtaining the SSS-rank unique hidden Talent — Millionfold Boost!]
[Effect: Anything you sell can be returned to you a millionfold.]
Daniel froze for three seconds.
Then his brain crashed.
"Millionfold Boost??"
"Sell something worth one dollar and get a million back? Wait, that was actually a real redemption code?!"
He stared at the short, simple description in his Talent panel and read it three more times.
Before Daniel could recover from the shock, another cold system prompt interrupted his thoughts.
[Ding! Please choose your base Class!]
Before his eyes flashed five starting Classes:
Mage, Warrior, Priest, Summoner, Archer.
Daniel was already intimately familiar with the first four.
In his previous rebirths, he had experienced every class except Archer, and had even taken each of them to heights beyond the reach of ordinary people.
But no matter how strong he became with his foreknowledge, every time he faced the Evil God, he felt the same crushing sense of powerlessness.
And now, only one class remained untried.
Archer.
Thinking of it, Daniel couldn’t help but recall Archer’s notorious reputation.
A Warrior could buy a sword and use it for half a year.
But an Archer?
A single quiver of good arrows was barely enough for one group battle.
A Mage could spend a few thousand gold coins on a staff and use it for ages.
But an Archer’s bow, arrows, enchanted accessories...
They were all horrifyingly expensive consumables.
Large guilds could afford to raise Archers because they had mines, resources, and money.
But for solo players, choosing Archer meant one of two endings:
Either delete the character and reroll,
or sign away your life to a major guild or financial consortium, working like a slave to pay off your debt.
The overwhelming majority of solo Archers couldn’t even survive the early game, much less grow strong on their own.
It could be said that Archer was absolutely forbidden territory for solo players.
But when Daniel looked at the description of his Talent, the corner of his mouth twitched upward.
Millionfold Boost.
The most gold-hungry class in his previous life.
In this life—
he was a goddamn money printer.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 -2-Selling the Starter Bow Right at the Beginning? Obtaining a Legendary-Grade Weapon!
paragraphs: [Ding! Welcome to Starter Village No. 616!]
Daniel’s vision blurred for a moment.
When he opened his eyes again, he was already standing in a stone-paved plaza.
The buildings around him were all medieval in style—wooden stalls, thatched roofs, and in the distance, a blacksmith’s shop ringing nonstop with clanging metal.
If not for the semi-transparent system panel floating overhead, most people would probably have thought they had been transported straight into the Middle Ages.
Daniel instinctively swept his gaze over the surroundings.

The plaza was packed shoulder to shoulder with newly spawned players. Some were still touching their own faces in disbelief, some were squatting down to pry at the floor tiles, and one guy was hugging the scarecrow at the village entrance while shouting, "Mom, look at me!"
[World Channel]
"Holy crap, this is way too real! It actually hurts when I pinch myself!"
"Anyone want to party up? I’ve got ten years of MMO experience—I can speedrun Starter Village!"
"Forget that, tell me if this game lets you kill people! I wanna see what being red-named feels like!"
"Help! I spawned next to a manure cart! The smell is insane!!!"
Daniel’s mouth twitched as he looked at the flood of messages.
Two hundred years ago, he had been one of these clueless newbies too, yelling at NPCs for half the day and hoping to trigger some hidden quest.
Now, though...
He directly closed the World Channel and opened his character panel.
[Player: Faustus]
[Level: 1]
[Class: Archer]
[Talent: Millionfold Boost (SSS-rank Unique Hidden)]
He opened his inventory.
Inside was the standard starter bow.
[Attack +3, Range: 20 meters, Reload Time: 1.5 seconds]
[Starter Arrows ×10]
As crude as ever.
Daniel stared at the starter bow. The wooden grip looked cheap and fragile.
But as he looked at that piece of junk, his eyes lit up.
Wait.
If he could sell the starter bow and get a millionfold return, then...
Worth a try.
Without another word, Daniel turned and ran toward the small shop at the edge of the plaza.
It was the only NPC-run general store in Starter Village. A sign hung outside the entrance:
We buy all kinds of materials at fair prices!
Behind the counter stood a squinting old man with a line of text floating above his head.
[General Merchant · Grey]
"Boss, I want to sell something!"
Daniel slapped the starter shortbow onto the counter.
"Oh?"
Old Grey narrowed his eyes and looked it over. "A starter bow, huh? Purchase price... 1 copper coin."
"Uh... sold!"
Grey froze for a moment, probably because he had never seen such a bizarre newbie before.
Still, he fished out a single copper coin from under the counter and handed it over.
At that exact moment, a burst of laughter erupted nearby.
Daniel turned his head and saw a circle of players behind him pointing and whispering.
"No way, did I just see that right? This guy sold his starter weapon?"
"He sold his bow right at the beginning? What’s he planning to do, punch monsters to death?"
"Hahahahaha, I’m dying! Has he gone broke already? What can one copper coin even do?"
"He’s probably a total noob who doesn’t know basic game mechanics. An Archer without a weapon is just dead weight."
"Buddy, take it back while you still can. Once the NPC refuses refunds, you’ll be crying."
Daniel swept a glance over them and merely nodded calmly.
[Ding! Detected player has sold an item. SSS-rank Talent — Millionfold Boost activated!]
[Sold Item: Starter Shortbow (Common-grade). Millionfold Boost in progress... Please choose enhancement direction: Quantity or Quality!]
Daniel frowned.
Who the hell would choose to receive one million starter bows?
[Ding! Congratulations, player has obtained: 100 Gold Coins!]
[Ding! Congratulations, player has obtained: Moon Reaper (Legendary-grade)!]
"100 gold coins!"
Daniel took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the shock in his heart.
The exchange rate between copper coins, silver coins, and gold coins was 1:1000.
Which meant...
As long as it was something obtained after a sale, even currency could trigger Millionfold Boost!
"Legendary-grade weapon!!"
But compared to the legendary-grade weapon, those one hundred gold coins suddenly seemed almost insignificant!
In the world of Stellar, weapon grades were divided into:
Common-grade, Bronze-grade, Iron-grade, Silver-grade, Gold-grade, Platinum-grade, Blackgold-grade, Epic-grade, Legendary-grade, Supreme-grade!
All grades below Gold-grade were still within the bounds of ordinary understanding.
But from Gold-grade onward, weapon power became more and more absurd.
Especially Epic-grade and above—those could already be called divine weapons, casually granting attributes on the level of plucking stars and shooting down moons!
At that point, it was no longer a matter of "too valuable to buy."
It was a matter of barely ever seeing one at all.
Even during the final stage of the war against the Evil God, the number of Legendary-grade weapons in the hands of humanity could be counted on one’s fingers.
As for Supreme-grade?
No one had ever even seen one.
And yet now, right at the very start, he had obtained a Legendary-grade weapon.
Even Daniel himself was stunned.
He opened his inventory.
Lying quietly inside was a longbow of pure silver-white, glowing faintly with a soft radiance.
[Moon Reaper (Legendary-grade)]
[Level: 1 (Can Grow)]
[Base Attack Power +500. Each hit additionally deals 5% of the target’s max HP as bonus damage!]
[Skill 1 — Infinite Rapidfire: No reloading required. Draw and shoot instantly. Attack speed depends entirely on the player’s hand speed!]
[Skill 2 — Explosive Arrow: Arrows explode upon hitting the target. Explosion damage equals 100% of the sum of the player’s four core attributes. Explosion radius: 5 meters.]
[Skill 3 — Attribute Amplification: Every point of Strength / Agility / Constitution / Intelligence grants an additional 10 Attack Power.]
[Note: This weapon cannot be dropped, traded, or destroyed.]

[Description: A divine weapon left behind from the age of Ragnarok. Once wielded by the great sage of the Elven Godrace, it pierced through three planes with a single arrow. Later, it was redeemed from a general store by a humble human for 1 copper coin.]
Daniel’s breathing quickened.
He stared at the bow in silence for a full ten seconds.
Then he quietly closed the inventory, his face completely expressionless.
The people at the entrance were still laughing.
"Oh man, this guy’s gone stupid. He’s just staring at his inventory in a daze!"
"He’s probably regretting it now, hahaha! Sold his entire future for one copper coin!"
"Hurry up, screenshot it! Post it in World Channel—Starter Village has produced a true genius!"
Daniel lifted his head and glanced at them.
He was in too good a mood to bother with them.
Instead, he turned back to Old Grey.
"Boss, do you buy arrows too?"
Grey raised a brow. Although surprised, he still nodded.
"Starter arrows are sold in bundles of ten. One bundle buys for 1 copper coin."
Daniel immediately sold all ten arrows in his inventory and got another copper coin.
[Ding! Millionfold Boost activated. Please choose enhancement direction...]
Daniel thought for a moment.
This time, he chose Quantity Boost.
After all, no matter how good arrows were, they were still consumables. He had no interest in wasting one-time divine arrows on trash mobs.
[Item successfully sold: Starter Arrows. Enhancement return in progress...]
[Congratulations, player has obtained: 100 Gold Coins! Standard Arrows ×1,000,000!]
Very quickly, his inventory space was neatly stacked with one million arrows.
The corners of Daniel’s mouth couldn’t help but rise.
One million arrows!
Even if he fired thirty arrows per second, it would still take him nearly ten straight hours to use them all up!
And yet the people beside him were still laughing.
"Hahahaha, this idiot sold his arrows too! He sold all ten starting arrows—what’s he gonna use to kill monsters now? Love?"
"No, wait, look at his expression. Why is he smiling?"
"Hold on... the guy’s actually pretty handsome. He’s not secretly crazy, is he...?"
Daniel completely ignored them.
He tried taking out some of the arrows in his inventory and selling them again.
[Beep! This item cannot be sold!]
As expected.
The system wasn’t about to let him abuse an infinite nesting exploit.
He closed his inventory, turned around, and walked straight out.
"Hey! Bro! Where are you going without a weapon?"
"Seriously, how about this—you call me big bro and I’ll carry you through some small mobs!"
Daniel didn’t even look back.
They weren’t people from the same world at all.
There was no need to waste words.
At the northwest corner of Starter Village, beneath an old scholar tree—
A young man in a gray mage robe was squatting there.
He was holding a book, but his eyes kept drifting toward the passing players. Floating above his head was a line of text.
[Main City Magic Academy Student · Adrian]
Daniel walked over and spoke directly.
"Hello. I’d like to accept a commissioned quest."
Adrian raised his head and looked him over, a trace of disdain flashing through his eyes.
"Get lost. I’m contemplating life."
Daniel pulled out 12 copper coins and handed them over.
Every player started with 10 copper coins in initial funds, plus the 2 he had earned from selling items.
Adrian’s eyes lit up instantly.
No matter how small the money, meat was still meat.

I’ve got ten years of MMO experience—I can speedrun Starter Village!"
"Forget that, tell me if this game lets you kill people!
I wanna see what being red-named feels like!"
"Help!
I spawned next to a manure cart!
The smell is insane!!!"
Daniel’s mouth twitched as he looked at the flood of messages.
Two hundred years ago, he had been one of these clueless newbies too, yelling at NPCs for half the day and hoping to trigger some hidden quest.
Now, though...
He directly closed the World Channel and opened his character panel.
[Player: Faustus]
[Level: 1]
[Class: Archer]
[Talent: Millionfold Boost (SSS-rank Unique Hidden)]
He opened his inventory.
Inside was the standard starter bow.
[Attack +3, Range: 20 meters, Reload Time: 1.5 seconds]
[Starter Arrows ×10]
As crude as ever.
Daniel stared at the starter bow.
The wooden grip looked cheap and fragile.
But as he looked at that piece of junk, his eyes lit up.
Wait.
If he could sell the starter bow and get a millionfold return, then...
Worth a try.
Without another word, Daniel turned and ran toward the small shop at the edge of the plaza.
It was the only NPC-run general store in Starter Village.
A sign hung outside the entrance:
We buy all kinds of materials at fair prices!
Behind the counter stood a squinting old man with a line of text floating above his head.
[General Merchant · Grey]
"Boss, I want to sell something!"
Daniel slapped the starter shortbow onto the counter.
"Oh?"
Old Grey narrowed his eyes and looked it over.
"A starter bow, huh?
Purchase price...
1 copper coin."
"Uh... sold!"
Grey froze for a moment, probably because he had never seen such a bizarre newbie before.
Still, he fished out a single copper coin from under the counter and handed it over.
At that exact moment, a burst of laughter erupted nearby.
Daniel turned his head and saw a circle of players behind him pointing and whispering.
"No way, did I just see that right?
This guy sold his starter weapon?"
"He sold his bow right at the beginning?
What’s he planning to do, punch monsters to death?"
"Hahahahaha, I’m dying!
Has he gone broke already?
What can one copper coin even do?"
"He’s probably a total noob who doesn’t know basic game mechanics.
An Archer without a weapon is just dead weight."
"Buddy, take it back while you still can.
Once the NPC refuses refunds, you’ll be crying."
Daniel swept a glance over them and merely nodded calmly.
[Ding!
Detected player has sold an item.
SSS-rank Talent — Millionfold Boost activated!]
[Sold Item: Starter Shortbow (Common-grade).
Millionfold Boost in progress...
Please choose enhancement direction: Quantity or Quality!]
Daniel frowned.
Who the hell would choose to receive one million starter bows?
[Ding!
Congratulations, player has obtained: 100 Gold Coins!]
[Ding!
Congratulations, player has obtained: Moon Reaper (Legendary-grade)!]
"100 gold coins!"
Daniel took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the shock in his heart.
The exchange rate between copper coins, silver coins, and gold coins was 1:1000.
Which meant...
As long as it was something obtained after a sale, even currency could trigger Millionfold Boost!
"Legendary-grade weapon!!"
But compared to the legendary-grade weapon, those one hundred gold coins suddenly seemed almost insignificant!
In the world of Stellar, weapon grades were divided into:
Common-grade, Bronze-grade, Iron-grade, Silver-grade, Gold-grade, Platinum-grade, Blackgold-grade, Epic-grade, Legendary-grade, Supreme-grade!
All grades below Gold-grade were still within the bounds of ordinary understanding.
But from Gold-grade onward, weapon power became more and more absurd.
Especially Epic-grade and above—those could already be called divine weapons, casually granting attributes on the level of plucking stars and shooting down moons!
At that point, it was no longer a matter of "too valuable to buy."
It was a matter of barely ever seeing one at all.
Even during the final stage of the war against the Evil God, the number of Legendary-grade weapons in the hands of humanity could be counted on one’s fingers.
As for Supreme-grade?
No one had ever even seen one.
And yet now, right at the very start, he had obtained a Legendary-grade weapon.
Even Daniel himself was stunned.
He opened his inventory.
Lying quietly inside was a longbow of pure silver-white, glowing faintly with a soft radiance.
[Moon Reaper (Legendary-grade)]
[Level: 1 (Can Grow)]
[Base Attack Power +500.
Each hit additionally deals 5% of the target’s max HP as bonus damage!]
[Skill 1 — Infinite Rapidfire: No reloading required.
Draw and shoot instantly.
Attack speed depends entirely on the player’s hand speed!]
[Skill 2 — Explosive Arrow: Arrows explode upon hitting the target.
Explosion damage equals 100% of the sum of the player’s four core attributes.
Explosion radius: 5 meters.]
[Skill 3 — Attribute Amplification: Every point of Strength / Agility / Constitution / Intelligence grants an additional 10 Attack Power.]
[Note: This weapon cannot be dropped, traded, or destroyed.]
[Description: A divine weapon left behind from the age of Ragnarok.
Once wielded by the great sage of the Elven Godrace, it pierced through three planes with a single arrow.
Later, it was redeemed from a general store by a humble human for 1 copper coin.]
Daniel’s breathing quickened.
He stared at the bow in silence for a full ten seconds.
Then he quietly closed the inventory, his face completely expressionless.
The people at the entrance were still laughing.
"Oh man, this guy’s gone stupid.
He’s just staring at his inventory in a daze!"
"He’s probably regretting it now, hahaha!
Sold his entire future for one copper coin!"
"Hurry up, screenshot it!
Post it in World Channel—Starter Village has produced a true genius!"
Daniel lifted his head and glanced at them.
He was in too good a mood to bother with them.
Instead, he turned back to Old Grey.
"Boss, do you buy arrows too?"
Grey raised a brow.
Although surprised, he still nodded.
"Starter arrows are sold in bundles of ten.
One bundle buys for 1 copper coin."
Daniel immediately sold all ten arrows in his inventory and got another copper coin.
[Ding!
Millionfold Boost activated.
Please choose enhancement direction...]
Daniel thought for a moment.
This time, he chose Quantity Boost.
After all, no matter how good arrows were, they were still consumables.
He had no interest in wasting one-time divine arrows on trash mobs.
[Item successfully sold: Starter Arrows.
Enhancement return in progress...]
[Congratulations, player has obtained: 100 Gold Coins!
Standard Arrows ×1,000,000!]
Very quickly, his inventory space was neatly stacked with one million arrows.
The corners of Daniel’s mouth couldn’t help but rise.
One million arrows!
Even if he fired thirty arrows per second, it would still take him nearly ten straight hours to use them all up!
And yet the people beside him were still laughing.
"Hahahaha, this idiot sold his arrows too!
He sold all ten starting arrows—what’s he gonna use to kill monsters now?
Love?"
"No, wait, look at his expression.
Why is he smiling?"
"Hold on... the guy’s actually pretty handsome.
He’s not secretly crazy, is he...?"
Daniel completely ignored them.
He tried taking out some of the arrows in his inventory and selling them again.
[Beep!
This item cannot be sold!]
As expected.
The system wasn’t about to let him abuse an infinite nesting exploit.
He closed his inventory, turned around, and walked straight out.
"Hey!
Bro!
Where are you going without a weapon?"
"Seriously, how about this—you call me big bro and I’ll carry you through some small mobs!"
Daniel didn’t even look back.
They weren’t people from the same world at all.
There was no need to waste words.
At the northwest corner of Starter Village, beneath an old scholar tree—
A young man in a gray mage robe was squatting there.
He was holding a book, but his eyes kept drifting toward the passing players.
Floating above his head was a line of text.
[Main City Magic Academy Student · Adrian]
Daniel walked over and spoke directly.
"Hello.
I’d like to accept a commissioned quest."
Adrian raised his head and looked him over, a trace of disdain flashing through his eyes.
"Get lost.
I’m contemplating life."
Daniel pulled out 12 copper coins and handed them over.
Every player started with 10 copper coins in initial funds, plus the 2 he had earned from selling items.
Adrian’s eyes lit up instantly.
No matter how small the money, meat was still meat.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 -3-Hidden Quest, Beast-Turned
paragraphs: "Ahem... well, there is something."
Adrian stuffed the copper coins into his sleeve at lightning speed, then lowered his voice.
"There’s a village not far from Starter Village called Windmill Town. Something strange has been happening there lately. I need someone to investigate what exactly is going on..."
"I’d be happy to help."
Daniel wasn’t surprised in the slightest.
"Just a friendly warning," Adrian said. "The villagers there have been showing signs of beastification."
"Beastification?"

"That’s right. Some people transform into beasts in the middle of the night and attack their neighbors. Those who get attacked soon begin showing the same symptoms as well. It spreads from person to person..."
Adrian’s expression turned grave.
"The Academy sent me here to investigate, but I can’t handle it alone. I need help."
[Ding! Hidden Quest triggered: Investigate the Beastification Mystery of Windmill Town]
[Quest Difficulty: C-rank]
[Quest Objective: Travel to Windmill Town, investigate the source of the beastification phenomenon, and collect at least 3 clues]
[Quest Rewards: EXP +500, Silver Coins +10, Contribution Points +200... ???]
[Accept?]
Daniel accepted immediately.
A few passing players nearby happened to see the scene and froze.
"Holy crap? Isn’t this NPC the one who always squats here ignoring people?"
"I tried talking to him before! He acted all high and mighty and wouldn’t trigger anything no matter what I said!"
"How the hell did this guy activate it?"
Daniel stood up and dusted off his pants.
Of course he knew how to trigger it.

Back in his previous life, he had only discovered it while grinding strategy guides—this Adrian wasn’t some ordinary NPC at all. He was a genius student from the Main City Magic Academy, and also a key figure in the later main storyline involving the beastification plague.
And there was only one requirement to unlock his quest:
Pay him.
At least 10 copper coins was enough.
Unfortunately, most players in the early game saved their copper coins for potions and supplies. By the time they remembered this NPC later, Adrian had long since left Starter Village.
[System Notice: You have accepted an investigation quest for the high-level map Windmill Town!]
[Contribution Points +10]
[Current Contribution Points: 10 (New Arrival)]
Daniel opened the map.
Everything around Starter Village was still gray, except for Windmill Town, where a red exclamation mark had lit up.
That was a high-level map. Under normal circumstances, players needed to be at least Level 20 before they could enter.
But after taking this quest, he could go in right now at Level 1.
Of course, for anyone other than him, even if they somehow took this hidden quest by accident, they’d still have to wait before completing it.
Trying to go there before Level 10 was basically suicide.
Daniel glanced back in the direction of Starter Village Plaza. Most players were still running around trying to find rabbits, chasing chickens and dogs all over the place.
Competing happily as if their lives depended on it.
Daniel looked at the Moon Reaper in his inventory, and the corner of his mouth curled upward.
He took the bow out and lightly pulled the string.
The instant the empty string vibrated, a heavy shockwave burst through the air.
The few players nearby were so startled they dropped onto their asses.
"What the hell was that?!"
"H-He’s got some glowing bow in his hand! Where did that come from?!"
"No way, bro—are you playing a cracked version of the game?!"
Daniel ignored them.
He slung the bow over his back and strode straight out of Starter Village.
Behind him, the World Channel exploded.
[World Channel]
"By the gods, there’s a hacker in Starter Village 616! Some player got a glowing bow from who knows where!"
"A glowing bow? Stop joking around. Only weapons above Gold-grade glow. Are you blind or what?!"
"No way that’s real. Does this game actually have planted accounts?"
"Where’s the screenshot? Post the screenshot!"
"Didn’t get one. The light was too blinding..."
Daniel chuckled at the messages and closed the channel.
A planted account?
Well, in a certain sense, he really was a closed-beta veteran.
He lifted his head.
In the distance, he could already see the windmills of Windmill Town turning slowly.
Daniel stepped into Windmill Town, and a dense fog immediately rushed at his face, reducing visibility to less than ten meters.
A foul odor slammed straight into his brain.
Daniel frowned and took the Moon Reaper off his back.
The surroundings were deathly quiet.
Every now and then, a low beastly growl drifted out from the depths of the mist—sounding part wolf, part human.
Daniel lightened his footsteps and moved along the wall.
No matter how much combat experience he had, it couldn’t change the fact that right now he was only a fragile Level 1 player.
In a high-level map like this, even getting grazed could injure him badly—getting hit head-on could mean instant death.
He had walked about fifty meters when he suddenly stopped.
It was too quiet.
According to his memories from his previous life, the monster density in Windmill Town was extremely high. There was no way he should have gone this long without encountering one...
And just then, a rustling sound suddenly came from the alley to his right.
Daniel pivoted sideways and raised his bow, his eyes locked on the alley entrance.
The next second, a pair of green glowing eyes lit up in the fog.
Then came a second pair. A third.
"ROAR—!"
A monster covered in gray fur lunged out of the mist.
It had a human face and a beast’s body. Its mouth stretched all the way to its ears, filled with jagged teeth still hanging with scraps of flesh.
With one swipe of its claw, the stone door beside it shattered like wet paper.
[Iron-grade Beast-Turned · LV15]
Daniel’s pupils contracted.
What the hell? The first one I meet is already an Iron-grade template?
He didn’t hesitate for even a second and leapt backward on the spot.
In barely the blink of an eye, the monster had already rushed in front of him and slammed one claw down where he had just been standing.
Boom!
The stone pavement was smashed open into a crater the size of a washbasin. Flying gravel struck Daniel’s legs hard enough to sting.
"What the hell? My total HP is only 100! This is insane!"
Daniel spun his bow around and loosed an arrow in one smooth motion!
Bang!
A streak of silver flashed through the air as the arrow buried itself deep in the monster’s chest.
And then—
BOOM!!!
A crimson damage number floated above the monster’s head.
By sheer terrible luck, the creature had instantly triggered both the critical hit and explosion effects, and was killed on the spot.
The blast rang through Daniel’s ears, and the shockwave blew away all the surrounding fog.
Half the monster’s upper body was blown clean off, rotten flesh and shattered bone spraying across the ground while the remaining half of its corpse flew five or six meters backward.
Daniel stood there in a daze, still holding the bow without lowering it.
He looked down at the Moon Reaper in his hand, then at the smoking hole blasted into the wall nearby.
What.
The.
Hell.
He knew that shot would hit hard.
But he hadn’t expected it to hit this hard.
A Level 15 Iron-grade monster got one-shot by a single arrow?
[Ding! You have slain Beast-Turned (LV15). Gained 1500 EXP!]
[Level Up! Current Level: 2]
[Gained 10 Attribute Points]
[Level Up! Current Level: 3]
[Gained 10 Attribute Points]
[Level Up! Current Level: 5]
[Gained 10 Attribute Points]
A string of notifications flooded his screen.
Before Daniel could even recover, his level had already jumped straight to Level 5.
He took a deep breath and dumped all of his attribute points into Agility.
Agility +50!
Originally, he had only wanted to test the bow’s power.
Now, though, he was starting to understand what it meant to be a walking humanoid cannon.
The remaining Beast-Turned in the alley had already been halfway through lunging out.
But after seeing their companion get blown into chunks, they actually skidded to a halt on the spot.
They exchanged uneasy looks, low whimpers rumbling in their throats.
Daniel bared his teeth in a grin.
"Why run?"
"Since you’re already here, don’t be shy."

chapters.title: Chapter 4 -4-Unique Hidden Class — Burstshot God
paragraphs: Under the terrified gazes of the remaining Beast-Turned, Daniel slowly raised his bow.
Whoosh!
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh...!
Arrows poured out like they cost nothing at all. And among that endless barrage, every now and then, one would strike a monster with perfect precision.
Boom!
Boom boom boom...!
The explosions came one after another without end, lighting up the entire street with fire.
By the time the smoke cleared, the alley was left with nothing but chunks of flesh and a few smoking craters.
[Ding! You have slain Beast-Turned ×7... Your level has risen to: Level 10]
Daniel glanced at his EXP bar, then at the wreckage all over the ground. Scattered here and there were three pieces of white- and green-grade equipment.
He couldn’t help but whistle.
This efficiency...
In his previous life, he wouldn’t have dared dream of something like this.
[Ding! Obtained Common-grade Weapon: Greatsword ×1, Bronze-grade Magic Staff ×1, Bronze-grade Gauntlets ×1]
Daniel picked up the dropped equipment.
At this stage of the game, Bronze-grade gear was still hard currency. There was no need to worry about selling it.
He opened the map to confirm his direction, then carried his bow deeper into town.
The explosions never stopped along the way.
If he ran into a lone monster, one arrow was enough, no matter what level it was.
If he ran into groups of three or five, a single shot could blast through the whole pack. Ten arrows later, both monsters and walls alike would be reduced to rubble.
The more Daniel fought, the smoother it felt.
Once he got into rhythm, he even started showing off a little.
One arrow pierced through three monsters, making all three explode together.
Or he would deliberately use ground blasts to launch clusters of monsters into the air.
Half an hour later, he was already standing beside the fountain in the center of town.
[Level: 20]
He evenly distributed the newly gained 150 attribute points among Strength, Intelligence, Constitution, and Agility.
Including the base ten points in each stat, his four core attributes now looked like this:
[Strength: 45]
[Intelligence: 45]
[Agility: 105]
[Constitution: 45]
Aside from Agility, the exclusive primary stat for Archers, Daniel did not underestimate the other three at all.
Knowing how the future would unfold, he understood perfectly well that every stat had an important role to play.
After all, in the future, these attribute points would affect his real body as well.
Daniel checked the time.
Ten minutes left.
That was right—one of the reasons he had accepted this quest was to claim Adrian’s hidden questline and rewards.
But there was another purpose as well.
A Wandering Merchant would spawn here!
The items sold by this kind of merchant were mostly basic supplies, but on very rare occasions, they could carry truly valuable goods.
Some people had even once found Legendary-grade items in a Wandering Merchant’s stock!
Normally, merchants like these did not spawn at any fixed location.
But during the current newbie period, this one was guaranteed to appear in Windmill Town.
Once the number of players entering Windmill Town exceeded one hundred, his spawn point would no longer remain fixed.
And the reason Daniel was waiting for him...
Was because there was a very high chance the merchant would be selling a Class Awakening Scroll.
In his previous life, Daniel had come here specifically to verify this, and sure enough, he had indeed found that Class Awakening Scroll in the merchant’s inventory.
Roar!
Right then, a series of low growls rose from the fog.
Daniel swept his gaze around the fountain.
Shadows of monsters loomed everywhere in the mist.
The nearest few had already noticed him, baring their fangs as they crept closer.
Daniel rolled his neck, then raised his bow.
Whoosh whoosh whoosh!
Whoosh whoosh whoosh whoosh...
For the next ten minutes, the center of Windmill Town sounded like a warzone. Explosions came wave after wave, and flames shot into the sky.
If nearby players could have seen this scene, they probably would have suspected the game had bugged out.
As the final monster fell, Daniel put away his bow and looked toward the fountain.
The next second, the air suddenly warped.
A middle-aged man in a tattered cloak appeared out of nowhere.
He pushed a small cart piled high with assorted goods and stood smiling beside the fountain.
[Wandering Merchant · Marcus]
"Heh, looks like you came right on time, friend."
Marcus narrowed his eyes as he sized Daniel up.
"A little guy at Level 20, and you managed to stay alive here? Not bad."
Daniel didn’t waste words with him and directly opened the shop list.
Inside were stacks of potions and materials, all with unlimited purchase quantities.
In the limited-purchase section, he saw an Iron-grade Warrior Armor, a bottle of Rare MP Potion, and even a Silver-grade Arcane Staff.
If he could buy and resell those, he didn’t even dare imagine what kind of return he might get.
But unfortunately, the limited-purchase section allowed him to buy only one item.
And his real target was not the staff.
At the very end of that section, he saw a roll of parchment.
[Universal Class Awakening Scroll · B-rank]
Price: 100 Gold Coins
Description: An utterly ordinary Class Awakening Scroll. Upon use, it will randomly Class Change the user into a special Class corresponding to their current Class.]
Utterly ordinary.
Daniel said nothing, but this item only looked random on the surface.
In truth, it was the only item in the early game that had a chance of producing a top-tier Class.
The catch was that the probability was absurdly low—99.99% of the time, it would only turn into some ordinary special class.
Rather than waste that much money on such terrible odds, most players would rather just go to the village chief in Starter Village and get a free class advancement.
That was why nobody ever bought it.
But Daniel...
Didn’t need probability.
He directly clicked Purchase.
[Gold Coins -100]
Marcus’s eyes lit up.
"Oh? A decisive customer!"
Daniel took the scroll, but instead of using it immediately, he looked up and asked,
"Boss, do you buy things too?"
Marcus froze for a second, then nodded.
"Sure. What, you’ve got something good?"
Daniel handed the scroll he had just bought right back over.
"This."
Marcus looked at it, and his expression turned a little strange.
"Items sold here can’t be refunded."
"Of course. I’m not asking for a refund. I’m selling it to you."
"You bought it just to sell it?"
Seeing Daniel nod without hesitation, Marcus’s mind went into chaos.
This guy...
Was he mentally ill?
"...Fine. Buyback price: 10 Gold Coins."
The transaction was completed.
[Ding! Detected sold item: Universal Class Awakening Scroll. Sale price: 10 Gold Coins. Millionfold Boost activated!]
[Ding! Obtained: Gold Coins ×10,000,000!]
[Player selected Quality Boost. Returned corresponding item: Burstshot God Class Awakening Scroll (Unique)]
A red scroll instantly appeared in his inventory.
Marcus stared at the scroll in his own hand, then at Daniel, his face full of disbelief.
Daniel had no mood to pay attention to him. He impatiently opened the red scroll in his inventory.
In the world of Stellar, Classes were clearly ranked in strength:
F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, SSS!
But beyond those, there existed even rarer Classes:
Unique, Supreme-grade, and God-grade Classes!
Each of those three categories was unique in existence, impossible to seek by force, and every single one possessed overwhelming power.
Just thinking about how a B-rank Universal Scroll had turned into a Unique-grade Class Awakening Scroll simply by reselling it made Daniel’s heart surge with joy.
[Ding! You have used Burstshot God Class Awakening Scroll (Unique)]
[Beginning Class Change...]
[Congratulations! You have Class Changed into Unique Hidden Class: Burstshot God!]
[Class Traits:]
[- All bow skill damage +1000%]
[- Critical Rate +300%]
[- Arrows can ignore armor and resistance, piercing through targets]
[- All arrows gain explosive effects, Explosion Core Damage +1000%]
[- Attribute points gained per level: 10 → 20]
Daniel’s eyelid twitched as he read the last line.
20 attribute points per level?
So if other people gained 10 points per level, then every level-up for him was equal to two levels for everyone else?
Nearby, Marcus the Wandering Merchant was still muttering to himself.
"How strange... where the hell did this nouveau riche come from..."
Shaking his head, he pushed his cart onward and quickly disappeared into the fog.
Daniel took a deep breath and felt power surging through his body.
He looked up and saw a monster crouched on a rooftop in the distance, looking around warily.
He raised his hand and fired a single arrow.
The arrow turned into a streak of light, pierced straight through the monster’s chest, then buried itself into the head of the second monster behind it—
And then two explosions rang out almost at the same time.
Boom! Boom!
The two monsters were blasted directly into pieces!
[Ding! You have slain Wolf-type Beast-Turned ×2. Gained 1800 EXP!]

Normally, merchants like these did not spawn at any fixed location.
But during the current newbie period, this one was guaranteed to appear in Windmill Town.
Once the number of players entering Windmill Town exceeded one hundred, his spawn point would no longer remain fixed.

Was because there was a very high chance the merchant would be selling a Class Awakening Scroll.

Marcus narrowed his eyes as he sized Daniel up.

Not bad."

Description: An utterly ordinary Class Awakening Scroll.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 -5-Deeper into the Mine, Breaking Through to Level 45!
paragraphs: [Ding! You have obtained: Murky Crystal Fragment ×1]
Daniel bent down and picked up the thumb-sized crystal from beside the monster’s corpse, holding it up to the light for a closer look.
The grayish-white crystal was covered in cracks, and within it, faint black threads seemed to writhe as if alive.
Even in his hand, it gave off a slight, almost imperceptible warmth.
The next moment, the system description unfolded before his eyes.
[Murky Crystal Fragment (Quest Item)]
Description: A crystal fragment containing strange energy. It seems to point toward the source of some kind of infection. Collect 3 to complete this investigation quest! (1/3)
A faint smile curled at Daniel’s lips.
He remembered it clearly—this kind of fragment was actually the core byproduct of the beastification infection. Any monster that had been deeply infected would condense one inside its body.
The more he collected, the more the NPC’s favorability would rise when he turned in the quest at the end.
And that money-grubbing scholar Adrian?
If you maxed out his favorability, he could cough up some truly good stuff.
Daniel tossed the fragment into his inventory and continued deeper into Windmill Town.
For the rest of the day, the monsters of Windmill Town were in for absolute misery.

From East Street to West Street, anything that could still breathe—whether it was an ordinary Level 15 Beast-Turned, a Level 20 Iron-grade monster, or even those little mobs that had just respawned in the corners of walls and hadn’t even had time to open their eyes yet...
The moment a thunderous blast rang out, they vanished.
Daniel was like a walking harvester. Everywhere he passed, explosions linked together into an endless chain, flames soaring into the sky.
Every now and then, players in the distance would catch sight of the flashes and hear the explosions from afar. Terrified, they would turn and run, thinking the game had glitched out somehow.
By evening, in the center of Windmill Town—
Daniel opened his inventory.
[Murky Crystal Fragment ×97!]
Level: 35!
He put all 300 newly gained attribute points into Agility, preparing for the battle ahead.
Daniel enlarged the map.
Two kilometers north of Windmill Town, there was a small mine icon. Beside it was a tiny label:
Windmill Town Mining Cooperative (Abandoned)
Familiar memories surged into his mind instantly.
The mine!
The root of Windmill Town’s beastification lay inside that mine!
He still remembered that, in his first life, one of the major guilds had pushed their exploration all the way here and unearthed a buried piece of history.
The miners of Windmill Town had dug too deep while mining. In the process, they broke through a layer of rock and discovered an ancient church buried deep underground.
That place was the source of the villagers’ beastification. After the miners were infected, they returned to town and passed it on to the villagers...
One infected ten, ten infected a hundred, and just like that, all of Windmill Town was doomed.
And most importantly—
That mine had a fixed drop: a universal movement skill book.
Daniel’s thoughts sharpened.
A movement skill!
Having reincarnated four times, he understood better than anyone how important movement skills were.
Especially when fighting bosses.
Whether you had a movement skill or not made it feel like two entirely different games.
One version was getting chased all over the map by the boss.
The other was kiting the boss around like you were walking a dog.
Without another word, Daniel grabbed his bow and headed north.
The two-kilometer journey took only ten minutes.
The entrance to the mine was halfway up a hill, concealed behind a dense mass of vines. If it hadn’t been marked on the map, there would have been no way to discover it.
A crooked wooden sign stood at the entrance. The writing on it had long since faded, but a few words could still barely be made out:
Windmill Town Mining... No Unauthorized Entry
A rotten stench ten times stronger than the one in town drifted out from the cave, making Daniel frown deeply.
He took out a torch and lit it, then inhaled deeply before stepping into the entrance.
[Ding! You have discovered a new map: Abandoned Mine, Floor 1]
[Recommended Level: 20–30]
[Current Exploration: 0%]
The mine was extremely dark. The torch only illuminated a radius of two or three meters around him.
The ground was littered with overturned mine carts, rusted pickaxes, and scattered ore.
There were shallow mining marks on the walls, but even more than that, there was black moss everywhere, slick and slimy to the touch.
Daniel lightened his steps and moved forward slowly.
He hadn’t gone fifty meters before a rustling sound came from up ahead.
He planted the torch into the wall, then raised the Moon Reaper and aimed toward the source of the sound.
Very soon, three humanoid monsters staggered out from around the corner.
They were still wearing tattered miner uniforms, with rusted pickaxes hanging at their waists.
Their skin was an unnatural grayish-black, and parts of their bodies bulged with fist-sized lumps, as though something inside them was writhing beneath the skin.
Their eyes were completely clouded over, and low, unconscious rasping noises came from their throats.
[Beast-Turned Miner · LV22]
[Beast-Turned Miner · LV22]
[Beast-Turned Miner · LV23]
"Tch. What a miserable sight."
Daniel shook his head, drew his bow, and fired.
Whoosh—
One arrow pierced through the chest of the first miner. The arrowhead exited from its back and buried itself into the belly of the second.
Boom! Boom!
The two explosions went off almost simultaneously. The three closely packed miners were blasted into the air together, chunks of flesh splattering all over the wall.
But the next instant, a cracking sound came from overhead.
Daniel looked up, and his expression changed slightly.
The explosion had shaken several cracks loose in the ceiling of the mine, and bits of rock were already falling down in a shower.
"WTF—I forgot this is a mine!"
He immediately ran forward. Behind him came a thunderous boom, and the spot where he had been standing was buried under a pile of rubble in the blink of an eye.
Daniel wiped cold sweat from his forehead.
Looks like I’ll need to control the blast radius.
I can’t just go wild inside a mine. If a cave-in buried me alive, that’d be one hell of a joke.

After all, Stellar’s freedom level was absurdly high. He had personally seen players embezzle quest items after accepting a mission, only to end up being put on a wanted list by the NPC who gave them the quest.
From there on, Daniel fought much more cautiously.
Whenever possible, he avoided triggering explosions.
Although pure piercing damage from arrows had limited effect against these half-dead things, quantity made up for everything.
After all, how was a monster supposed to survive when its entire body was full of arrows?
Whenever he ran into large groups of monsters, Daniel would fire one arrow and immediately reposition to avoid getting crushed by falling rocks.
By the time he cleared the first floor, his level had risen to 40, and the loot wasn’t bad either.
[Obtained: Rusted Pickaxe ×5 (Common-grade)]
[Obtained: Durable Warrior Armor (Bronze-grade)]
[Obtained: Rare Longsword (Bronze-grade)]
[Obtained: Murky Crystal Fragment ×12]
[Obtained: Copper Coins...]
Then he continued down to the second floor.
And there, Beast-Turned Overseers · LV25 appeared!
These monsters were a head taller than ordinary miners. They held whips in their hands and wore slightly more presentable clothing, suggesting that they had managed others while alive.
Their attack patterns had changed too—they would lash out with their whips first, then blow whistles to summon smaller mobs.

Back in his first life, Daniel had nearly suffered at the hands of these things. The moment he killed an overseer, several miners had rushed out from the side and cornered him, hammering away until his HP dropped by a third before he barely managed to survive.
"But this time?"
"If you can even touch me, I lose."
The moment Daniel encountered a monster, the arrows in his hands flew like they were free.
The entire group of monsters barely managed a few steps before they were turned into human pincushions!
[Ding! You have slain Beast-Turned Overseer · LV30. Gained 23,950 EXP! Current Level: 45!]
[Obtained: Hardened Shield (Bronze-grade)]
Rumble—!
As a thunderous roar echoed through the mine, the gate to the third floor slowly opened!

chapters.title: Chapter 6 -6-An A-Rank Skill Book, Earning a Massive 100 Million Gold Coins!
paragraphs: The environment on the third floor was extremely eerie.
The walls were covered in black crystalline veins, spreading out like blood vessels.
Large numbers of [Crystallized Miners · LV35] poured out from around the corners.
The bulges on these monsters’ bodies had burst open, sprouting black crystals that covered them like hedgehog spines.
These monsters had incredibly high defense. Ordinary attacks dealt only single-digit damage.
But Daniel had explosive arrows that ignored armor, and on top of that, the walls here were already covered in those strange crystal membranes, making the structure exceptionally sturdy.
A streak of red arrow-light shot forward.
Rumble—!
Entire groups of crystallized monsters were blasted into pieces!
"What a dull and tedious process," he muttered, while his harvesting speed only grew faster and faster.
He had no idea how long he had been killing when the space ahead of him suddenly opened up.
It was a naturally formed underground hall, about half the size of a football field.
At the far end of the hall stood a massive iron gate, carved with twisted symbols that glowed faintly red.
In front of the gate stood a hulking monster.
It was nearly three meters tall, its entire body covered in thick black crystals, and in its hand it gripped a massive pickaxe.
No—not quite.
That pickaxe had already fused with its arm, becoming part of its body.
Its eyes glowed with two crimson lights, fixed directly on Daniel.
[Beast-Turned Guard · LV40 (Iron-grade)]
Daniel sucked in a breath.
This thing looked a lot fiercer than the Iron-grade monsters in Windmill Town.
He instinctively took a step back—and crushed a piece of gravel underfoot.
Crack—
At the same time, the Beast-Turned Guard moved.
It gave no roar, no warning. It simply raised its pickaxe and brought it smashing down toward Daniel’s head!
BOOM!!!
Shattered stone flew everywhere, and the ground was smashed into a crater the size of a washbasin.
Daniel dodged quickly and fired an arrow in return.
The arrow sank into the guard’s chest, then exploded—
Boom!
A bowl-sized hole was blown open in the guard’s chest, and black crystal shards scattered all over the floor.
The black explosion damage was shockingly eye-catching.
But its HP had only dropped by around one-tenth.
Daniel’s pupils contracted.
That HP...
This thing should make a decent target dummy for a while.
To be honest, Daniel felt that his biggest weakness right now was that his archery accuracy was pretty average.
If five out of ten arrows hit the enemy, that already counted as a high hit rate.
And now, with such a durable moving monster standing right in front of him, it was the perfect chance to practice.
The battle lasted a full five minutes.
Daniel had never enjoyed a fight this much.
This Beast-Turned Guard’s HP was absurdly thick—at least ten times that of an ordinary Iron-grade monster.
Its attack range was also enormous. Once that giant pickaxe started swinging, everything within ten meters became a death zone.
More interestingly, it could even hurl mineral fragments like a machine gun, sending them flying with rapid-fire whoosh whoosh whoosh sounds!
Daniel dodged while shooting, and his explosive arrows never stopped for even a moment.
Thankfully, he had maxed out Agility in advance. Facing those whistling attacks, a stream of MISS notifications kept popping above his head.
One arrow, two arrows, three arrows...
The monster’s HP rapidly fell.

He kept kiting it, making full use of his Agility advantage as he circled through the wide-open hall.
Several times, he almost got smashed by the pickaxe, barely dodging in the nick of time.

It let out one final furious roar, and all the crystals on its body suddenly exploded—
A self-destruct!
Daniel had already been prepared. He leapt backward, dodging the shockwave.
BOOM!!!
The explosion blasted broken rocks all over him, dropping his HP by 10%.
But the guard finally fell, its huge body crashing to the floor and kicking up a cloud of dust.

[Obtained: Iron-grade Standard Armor ×1]

[Shadow Step (A-rank)]
Type: Active Skill
Effect: Instantly dash 5 meters in a chosen direction
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Mana/Stamina Cost: 100
Class Restriction: None
Description: A high-level movement technique that keeps enemies from so much as touching your clothes!
Daniel’s eyes brightened.
An A-rank movement skill!
Even if it was just a basic version with a range of five meters, movement skills were god-tier in the early game!
Especially for fragile classes like Archer and Mage—once enemies got into melee range, death was practically guaranteed.
Having a movement skill was like having an extra life.
Suddenly, Daniel thought of something and opened the communication channel.
At this moment, the World Channel was as lively as a marketplace.
"WTF, I finally hit Level 5! Anyone wanna party up?"
"The free market is open! Brothers, charge!"
"Selling White Rabbit Dagger, 1 silver coin each, PM me if you want one!"
"Need a carry! I’m a girl, nice voice!"
"The guy above is definitely a dude, right? Yesterday you were saying you wanted to go red-name from PKing people..."
Daniel smiled faintly as he read the scrolling messages.
The market had opened.
With the experience of several lifetimes, he knew exactly what would happen next.
The major guilds and financial groups would rush in like sharks smelling blood,疯狂扫货.
sweeping up goods in a frenzy.
Anything valuable would find a buyer, no matter the price!
He lowered his head and looked at the skill book in his hand.
A movement skill—in the early game, this was the kind of rare treasure you couldn’t buy even if you had money.
If he sold it to players...
Daniel opened the market interface, clicked List Item, and placed [Shadow Step] up for sale.
Price: 100 Gold Coins.
Note: A-rank universal movement skill. Usable by all classes. One fixed price. If you can’t afford it, don’t yap.
He clicked confirm.
The next second, the World Channel exploded.
"Holy shit?!!! Check the market!!!"
"What are you freaking out about—... WTF?! An A-rank skill book??? A movement skill???"
"100 gold coins? Where the hell would anyone get 100 gold coins on day one? Is this guy insane?"
"Faustus—where the hell did this guy get something this good? His luck is insane!"
"A movement skill! If I had that while getting chased down by monsters, I’d be flying!"
"100 gold coins is way too expensive, isn’t it? Normal players could never afford that..."
"If you can’t afford it, stop yapping. He’s obviously not selling it to normal players."
"That said... I still think anyone who buys it at this stage is making a profit. An A-rank movement skill probably won’t even be outdated in the late game..."
Daniel watched the flood of messages in World Channel and said nothing, only smiling.
Of course he knew that 100 gold coins was expensive.
But he also knew that, to those wealthy guilds, 100 gold coins was pocket change.
What they wanted was the initiative.
They were using money to buy time.
And sure enough, in less than three minutes—
[Ding! Your listed item, Shadow Step Skill Book (A-rank), has been purchased.]
Daniel’s eyes lit up.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 -7-Millionfold Boost Activates — SSS-Rank Skill, God Speed
paragraphs: [Buyer: Dragon Slayer · Rhine]
The moment he saw that name, a faint gleam flashed through Daniel’s eyes.
"Someone from Rhine Guild."
Rhine Guild—one of the top five major guilds from his previous life.
Behind it stood the Rhine River Consortium, with assets worth hundreds of billions.
Their guild leader, Rhine Watcher, was a ruthless man who acted swiftly and decisively. But some of his subordinates were far from clean, bullying solo players by relying on the guild’s power.
But none of that mattered to Daniel right now.
What mattered was this—
[Ding! Detected sold item: Shadow Step Skill Book (A-rank), sale price: 100 Gold Coins. Millionfold Boost activated!]
[Obtained Gold Coins: 100,000,000]
[Sold item is a skill book. Quality Boost triggered!]
[Congratulations, player has obtained skill book: God Speed (SSS-rank)]
One hundred million Gold Coins, plus an SSS-rank skill book!
Daniel took a deep breath and opened his inventory.
A golden skill book lay quietly inside one of the slots.
[God Speed (SSS-rank)]
Type: Active Skill
Effect: Instantly teleport in a designated direction, up to a maximum distance of 1,000,000 meters
Cooldown: None (MP cost increases with distance)
MP Cost: Base 10 points + additional cost per meter
(No extra distance cost within 1 kilometer. Beyond 1 kilometer, consumes 1 additional MP per kilometer.)
Special Effects:

1 — Afterimage Clone: When the skill is used, afterimage clones are created. Clones last for 30 seconds, inherit 100% of the user’s Attack Power, and can act independently. The number of clones depends on MP consumed: one clone is created for every 100 MP spent (maximum 10 clones).
2 — Divine Perception: When using this skill, you can sense the locations of all living beings within a 1-kilometer radius centered on yourself.**
Description: A divine spatial skill from the Age of Gods. One step forward, and the ends of the earth lie within reach.
Daniel stared at the description.
After the initial shock passed, he couldn’t help but laugh.
A one-million-meter teleport?
The straight-line distance from Starter Village to the main city was only about eight hundred kilometers.
With this skill, he could take one step from Starter Village straight to the gates of the main city!
And as long as he had enough MP, he could even chain teleports and cross the entire continent!
Then there was the clone effect.
Ten clones, each inheriting 100% of his Attack Power, lasting for 30 seconds—
That meant he alone could unleash the firepower of eleven people.
It was absurdly overpowered.
And most importantly—
Divine Perception!
Every living creature within a radius of one kilometer would be exposed to him. Any ambushing players would have nowhere to hide.
Without question, it was a god-tier skill.
If he really had to name a flaw, it was that it could only detect the existence and location of living beings, not every detail about them.
But that hardly mattered.
Daniel took a deep breath and clicked Learn without hesitation.
[Ding! You have learned skill: God Speed (SSS-rank)]
A golden icon appeared in his skill bar.
He tried activating the skill.
His vision blurred for an instant, and the next second he was already standing at the other end of the mine, at least five hundred meters away from where he had just been.
And his MP had only dropped by 10 points.
Daniel couldn’t help but curse under his breath.
This skill was simply too broken.
At a stage when everyone else was still crawling like turtles, he was already driving a top-tier supercar.
He was just about to continue testing it when his private message channel suddenly chimed.
He opened it.
[Rhine Watcher (Private Message)]
"Lord Faustus, would you be interested in having a chat?"
"Rhine Guild sincerely invites you to join us. The待遇 is excellent—starting salary of 100,000 Earth Credits per month, full equipment reimbursement, plus profit-sharing!"
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
He hadn’t expected Rhine Guild’s leader to really notice him so soon.
A salary of 100,000?
In his previous life, he remembered that when Rhine River Consortium tried to recruit top-tier experts, the opening offer had been 200,000, minimum.
Offering him only 100,000 now...
Did they think he was easy to buy off?
A few seconds later, another private message came through.
[Rhine Watcher]
"The price is negotiable! Feel free to name your terms. Rhine Guild is more than sincere..."
Daniel still didn’t reply.
Soon after, friend requests and private messages from several other guilds came flooding in as well, but the contents were all more or less the same.
Without the slightest hesitation, he blocked every single one of them.
He had seen the true face of these guilds long ago in his previous life.
When they wanted to recruit you, they smiled and flattered you.
The moment recruitment failed, they turned hostile.
Rhine Guild, in particular, was especially disgusting.
On the surface they acted fair and righteous, but behind the scenes they suppressed solo players, monopolized resources, and even colluded with players from foreign servers to sell intelligence.
There was nothing they wouldn’t do.
Across four reincarnations, Daniel had watched these resource-hoarding conglomerates drag humanity into the abyss for their own selfish profit.
Cooperate with them?
In their dreams.
Still...
Daniel glanced at the 100 million Gold Coins in his inventory, then at the God Speed icon in his skill bar.
Disgust was one thing.
But emotions shouldn’t interfere with business.
"Alright. Time to get back to work."
He stretched his body and walked toward the iron gate deeper in the mine.
Beyond that gate...
Lay the underground church.
And inside that church, a boss called [Beast-Turned Father] was waiting for him.
This boss was incredibly fast, had wide attack coverage, enormous HP, and could summon crystal spikes to attack!

Under normal circumstances, it required a full party to clear—at least a twenty-man team around Level 50, all equipped with Iron-grade gear or above, plus strong coordination, to have any chance of success.
Because the difficulty of clearing it was so absurdly high, it had once earned the nickname:
The Newbie Butcher.
But now...
Daniel looked at the newly learned God Speed, then at the Moon Reaper in his hand.
Fast, are you?
Then let me show you what it means to be a man made of lightning.
Daniel took a slow breath.
He could already feel a faint but unmistakable pressure behind the gate, like a needle pricking the center of his forehead.
This was Divine Perception, the passive sensing effect granted by God Speed, already taking effect.
Behind the door was a gigantic life signature.
Far stronger than the Beast-Turned Guard from earlier.
"A Gold-grade Boss."
Monster tiers were divided into:
Common-grade, Bronze-grade, Iron-grade, Silver-grade, Gold-grade, Platinum-grade, Blackgold-grade, Epic-grade, Legendary-grade!
A Gold-grade Boss had already crossed a critical threshold.
In terms of raw strength alone, it could crush all ordinary players of the same level.
Daniel licked his lips and tightened his grip on the Moon Reaper.
Behind the iron gate stretched a stone staircase descending downward.
On both sides of the walls, glowing crystals had been embedded, casting the whole passage in a dim, sickly green light.
Daniel lightened his steps and descended one level at a time.
At the end of the stairs, the view suddenly opened up.
It was a naturally formed underground hall.
At the center of the hall stood a church.
A Gothic spire. Stained glass windows. Even a rusted iron cross planted outside the entrance.
The church was surrounded on all sides by dense masses of black crystal, like thorny brambles encircling it at the center.
Those crystals emitted light, illuminating the underground space with an eerie radiance.
Daniel frowned.
This place was just as unsettling as ever.
He followed the narrow path winding through the crystal growths toward the church.
He had only just reached the entrance when a low growl came from inside.
It didn’t sound like a beast.
It sounded more like...
A human.
Inside the church, more than a dozen pews lay overturned in disarray.
The pulpit was covered in dust.
More than half the stained-glass windows had shattered, and that ghastly green light streamed through the broken openings.
Standing before the pulpit was a gigantic figure.
It wore a tattered black robe, and around its neck still hung a silver cross.
The figure stood nearly four meters tall.
Its entire right half was covered in thick black crystal.
The left half barely retained a human shape, but its skin was a lifeless ash-gray, crisscrossed by black vein-like patterns.
Half of its face was human.
The other half was crystal.
One eye was murky gray-white.
The other burned with a dark crimson glow.
From its back grew three tentacles, each as thick as a bowl, ending in bony spikes.
A blood-red prompt appeared above the figure’s head.
[Beast-Turned Father · LV45 (Gold-grade Boss)]

chapters.title: Chapter 8 -8-Soloing a Level 45 Gold-Grade Boss!
paragraphs: The moment Daniel stepped one foot into the church—
The boss’s three grotesque tentacles lashed toward him at the same time, moving at terrifying speed!
Daniel activated God Speed almost instinctively.
His vision blurred, and in the next instant, he was already standing behind a pillar on the left side of the church.
Boom!
The tentacles slammed into the place where he had just been standing, instantly smashing three rows of pews into splinters and sending rubble flying everywhere.
Daniel sucked in a breath.
That speed...
If he hadn’t had God Speed, that hit probably would have buried him into the ground.
Having missed its first strike, the Father Boss turned its head and looked toward the pillar where Daniel had taken cover.
The three tentacles rose again.
But this time, Daniel didn’t dodge.
He directly drew his bow and fired!
Whoosh!
The arrow shot straight for the Father’s face!
The Father raised his left arm to block. The explosive arrow detonated on impact with his arm.
With a deafening boom, black crystal shards exploded across the floor.
A red critical hit number popped up, but its total HP only dropped by around 2%.
Daniel’s eye twitched.
One hundred thousand HP!
That arrow of his would have dealt at least 80% to an elite monster outside the mine.
And against this thing, it only shaved off 2%?
This bastard had at least 100,000 HP, minimum!
Enraged by the arrow, the Father Boss threw back its head and roared. Its three tentacles whipped wildly through the air, making the entire church tremble.
Then, all of a sudden, more than a dozen black crystal spikes burst from the ground, stabbing toward Daniel from every direction!
Daniel chain-blinked with God Speed, darting back and forth through the forest of spikes.
The spikes kept chasing after him, stabbing the ground until it looked like a giant hedgehog.
"Holy shit—this damn AoE skill again!"
This ultra-wide-range attack from the Beast-Turned Father had slaughtered countless players in his previous lives.
Even Daniel himself had been wrecked by it more than once.
He kept dodging while shooting, explosions echoing without end, and the Father’s HP slowly began to drop.
But it was too slow.
At this pace, he’d need to fire at least a hundred arrows to kill it.
One hundred arrows meant about five minutes of combat.
And during those five minutes, he’d have to maintain nonstop dodging. One slip-up and he’d be flattened by a tentacle.
Daniel kept fighting while calculating his MP.
His current Intelligence was 45, giving him a total of 3450 MP.
Creating one clone required 100 MP, so ten clones would cost 1000 MP, leaving him with 2450 MP to cast skills and blink.
But the problem was—
He had never tried controlling ten clones at once before.
He had no idea how effective it would be.
"Screw it. Let’s try."
At this stage, he still had no chance to learn dedicated Archer skills yet, so he could only rely on Class skills and equipment skills for damage output.
That meant every detail had to be calculated carefully.
Spotting an opening, he immediately activated the God Speed clone effect!
With a thought, four afterimages appeared behind him out of thin air.
Each one looked exactly like him, holding a Moon Reaper, moving in perfect sync.
Daniel froze.
Why are there only four?
Then he immediately understood.
He had used a lot of MP fighting all the way here. Right now, he only had a little over 400 MP, just enough to create four clones.
"Damn it. Forgot about that."
He hurriedly retreated, dodging tentacles while chugging MP potions.
The Father kept pursuing him, whip after whip coming from its tentacles, several of them nearly grazing him.
Thirty seconds later, the clones vanished.
Fortunately, Daniel had already finished drinking his potions, and his MP had climbed back up to 3000.
He took a deep breath and used the skill again.
This time, ten afterimages appeared behind him at once, standing neatly in a row, all raising their bows together.
A smile curved at Daniel’s lips.
"Come on, let this freak taste what saturation firepower feels like."
He drew his bow.
The ten afterimages behind him did the same.
Eleven bows were aimed at the Father at the same time.
The Father seemed to sense the danger. Its three tentacles whipped wildly as it lunged toward Daniel.
Eleven arrows left the strings at once!
Whoosh whoosh whoosh whoosh whoosh—!
It was like a rain of arrows pouring down!
Before the Father’s tentacles had even finished lashing forward, the first wave of arrows had already hit.
A thunderous explosion erupted, followed by the second wave, then the third...
Its enormous body was basically a giant living target. All eleven arrows landed cleanly.
Boom boom boom boom boom—!
The explosions blended into one continuous roar, illuminating the entire church with firelight.
The shockwaves shattered what remained of the stained glass and even shook stalactites loose from the ceiling outside.
By the time the smoke cleared, the Father’s HP had dropped to 50%.
Daniel’s eyes widened.
One volley took off 30%?!
Before he could even celebrate, the Father let out an earth-shaking roar.
The entire church began to quake.
The ground cracked open, and countless black crystals burst out from the fissures, growing madly.
Those crystals writhed as if alive, spreading toward Daniel!
[Ding! Beast-Turned Father has entered Phase Two: Berserk State]
[Attack Speed +50%, Movement Speed +50%, Defense +50%, New Skill: Crystal Spread]
Daniel’s face changed instantly, and he hurried backward.
But the crystal spread was fast too—within the blink of an eye, it had already covered half the church.
He could only keep using God Speed to evade, jumping onto pews, onto the pulpit, onto pillars.
The Father fought like a maniac, its tentacles thrashing, crystal spikes stabbing everywhere, tearing the entire church apart piece by piece.
Daniel kept dodging while sniping whenever he found an opening.
The moment the clone skill came off cooldown, he unleashed another synchronized volley.
Finally, after the third full barrage, the Father’s HP dropped to 5%.
And at that exact moment, the Beast-Turned Father went completely berserk.
It threw back its head with a long howl, and all the crystals on its body suddenly exploded, turning into countless fragments that shot outward in every direction!
Daniel’s pupils shrank.
This was a full-map AoE!
He had been prepared for this move all along.
But now the crystal fragments covered the entire church.
There was nowhere to dodge!
At the last possible instant, he activated God Speed.
His vision blurred, and the next second, he was already standing at the iron gate on this floor, while a storm of crackling impacts rang out behind him.
He looked back.
The church was in complete ruin. Everything inside had been riddled full of holes by the crystal fragments.
Inside the church, the Father’s HP remained frozen at 5%.
It was breathing heavily, its three tentacles hanging limply against the floor.
But its eyes were still locked onto Daniel with murderous hatred.
Daniel raised his bow and aimed at the Father’s head.
The Father seemed to sense that this would be the final blow.
It struggled to force itself upright, and its three tentacles lashed toward Daniel with the last of their strength.
Fire!
Eleven arrows left the strings at once.
Before the Father’s tentacles had even finished reaching forward, the first wave of arrows had already arrived.
The explosions detonated in a deafening chain, followed by the second wave, then the third...
Boom boom boom boom boom—!
This time the distance was much shorter.
The shockwaves from the blasts directly tore the church roof apart, and broken stone came crashing down in a cascade.
Daniel was blasted backward three meters, slamming hard into the ground and losing another 5% HP.
Then the smoke cleared.
The Father was still standing.
But only barely.
A washbasin-sized hole had been blasted through the Beast-Turned Father’s chest. Through it, Daniel could see the shattered pulpit behind him.
All three tentacles had been blown off at the roots, lying on the ground and still twitching weakly.
The crimson glow in its eyes dimmed little by little.
Daniel stared at the longbow in his hands in disbelief, his heart pounding with excitement.
The Beast-Turned Father—
The monster once known as the Newbie Butcher—
Had actually been solo-killed by him?
