chapters.title: Chapter 16 -16-Fifty Billion Dollars, Doom Guild
paragraphs: Daniel looked at the little stone dragon and then at its ridiculously powerful skills, nearly laughing out loud with excitement.
Especially the last skill: Immortal!
This meant that as long as the dragon touched the ground, it could never die!
The little stone dragon nuzzled his hand, making a friendly cooing sound.
Then, it turned around and began chomping on its dragon egg, flapping its little wings up and down, clearly overjoyed!
Meanwhile, in Starter Village,
Crimson Soul held the blackgold-grade companion egg in her hands, looking utterly stunned.
"Did I really buy it...?"
"Is this a dream? But why me?"
Crimson Soul’s expression was complicated.
She couldn’t understand why Daniel would sell her this companion egg.
After all, she knew her own worth, and this companion egg was definitely worth more than 10,000 gold coins—there was no doubt that someone else would offer a higher price!
She had even seen on the World Channel that a large guild was offering a million gold coins to buy it!
So, why her?
After hesitating, she couldn’t help but send a message.
"Lord Faustus, why did you sell it to me?"
"I heard Rhine Guild offered a million gold coins, but I only offered 10,000..."
She waited for quite a while before a message finally popped up.
"It’s nothing, just thought your name sounded nice!"
Huh?
Crimson Soul froze.
This reason... was way too casual, wasn’t it?
For Daniel, since the companion egg wasn’t bound to him, it was always going to be sold.
Who he sold it to wasn’t particularly important; he simply chose someone trustworthy.
Crimson Soul would eventually become one of the top human fighters, always at the frontlines against the evil gods!
Helping her—and even Daniel selling those items to players at a cheap price—was in a way helping humanity rise!
Crimson Soul wasn’t a pretentious person. Since she couldn’t figure it out, she didn’t waste time thinking more about it.
She looked at the companion egg in her hand, excitement flashing in her eyes.
"No matter what, I owe you one."
"If you ever need anything, feel free to ask me!"
She sent a friend request.
Daniel accepted.
Then, his profile picture completely grayed out.
Crimson Soul stood there, softly muttering to herself.
"Faustus, huh?"
"This game god... interesting!"
Leaving the east gate, Daniel headed straight for the Luminara Trading Company!
The [Luminara Trading Company] was the largest free trading market in Luminara, offering a wide variety of goods.
As soon as he entered, he casually walked up to one of the shops, and on the shelves, he immediately spotted what he was looking for.
[Money Bag Exchange]
He walked over and opened the product details.
[Money Bag (Special Item)]
Price: 10 coins
Effect: Stores gold coins in the bag, which will not drop upon death.
Description: Hide your coins so they can’t be stolen!
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
He remembered from his previous life that this was an item unlocked only after the main city opened, designed to reduce losses upon death.
In the game, players would drop all their gold coins upon death,
but the coins in the money bag wouldn’t drop.
Moreover, the money bag was an equipment item!
What did this mean?
It meant that it could be traded!
This meant he could store gold coins in the money bag and then sell the money bag.
This way, the gold coins would become a tradeable item, allowing both the buyer and seller to bypass some of the system’s restrictions.
More importantly...
Daniel suddenly had a brilliant idea.
He could sell the money bags to players, triggering the Millionfold Boost.
Then, the game’s gold coins would multiply!
He took a deep breath and immediately bought 100 money bags.
[Ding! You’ve reached today’s purchase limit for money bags!]
Then, he anonymously listed one item in the player marketplace, taking a "let’s try it" approach.
[Item: Money Bag (contains 10,000 gold coins)]
[Price: 1 copper coin]
[Purchase Method: Seller must agree!]
[Seller’s Note: Cash transaction, 5 dollars = 1 gold coin... Interested parties can add the bank account: XXXX-XXXX... Pay first, then ship!]
He listed the money bag and began to wait.
Soon, someone on the World Channel noticed the bizarre listing.
"HOLY SHIT! Look at the marketplace, someone is selling a money bag containing 10,000 gold coins for 1 copper coin, but it’s a cash transaction!"
"5 dollars per gold coin? The black market price is only 3.5 dollars, right?"
"But the money bag is a good item, it prevents gold coins from dropping upon death!"
"Crap, if everyone starts selling these money bags, where will we get old items to drop gold coins..."
"This person must be crazy, only a fool would buy..."
Daniel knew someone would buy it.
Since the game had just opened, gold coins were extremely scarce.
Those big guilds, desperate to secure resources, were willing to pay high prices to buy gold coins.
Although 5-1 was expensive, to them, it was pocket change.
Sure enough, within ten minutes, he received a private message.
[Anonymous Player (Private Message)]: I’ll take the 10,000 gold coins, 50,000 dollars have been transferred to your account, please check.
Daniel opened his phone (the game pod had real-world communication functions), and sure enough, there was a bank text message.
[Your account ending in XXXX has received a transfer of 50,000 dollars...]
He immediately moved the funds through a dozen accounts to ensure it couldn’t be traced back.
Once the money was secure, he returned to the marketplace, found the buyer, and clicked [Agree to Sell].
[Ding! Item sold: Money Bag (contains 10,000 gold coins), Price: 1 copper coin, Millionfold Boost triggered!]
[Received 1 gold coin!]
[Detected that the item has no quality attributes, automatic quantity increase, received 10,000,000,000 gold coins!]
[Detected that the transaction involves real currency, triggering real-world amplification!]
[Received 50,000,000,000 dollars!]
The next second, his phone vibrated wildly.
[Your account ending in XXXX has received fifty billion dollars...]
A series of transaction notifications flooded in, and his balance instantly reached a jaw-dropping number:
50 billion dollars.
Daniel’s hand holding the phone trembled slightly.
He knew the system was insane, but he didn’t expect it to be this insane—it even amplified real-world currency!
He took several deep breaths to quickly calm himself down.
No matter how much money he had, it was just a tool. The true goal was that final, apocalyptic disaster!
After confirming his suspicions, Daniel quickly returned to the game.
He didn’t need the money—getting massive wealth so quickly was too risky for the shadow account.
He decided to slowly unload the goods in batches.
But now, he had more important things to do.
He headed straight for the guild registration NPC at the main city guild management hall.
"Hello, I would like to register a guild."
The NPC nodded politely: "Please provide your ID and 500,000 gold coins as registration fees."
Daniel pulled out the Apprentice Merit Medal—this item gave him certain privileges with official organizations.
When the NPC saw the medal, their attitude immediately became more respectful.
"Ah, a meritorious person! You have priority handling rights."
"To register a guild, you need 500,000 gold coins and at least 3 members. Do you have members?"
Daniel shook his head.
"Just me for now."
"Just one person? That requires special permission."
The NPC thought for a moment and continued.
"However, with your Merit Medal, we can make an exception. Are you sure you want to register the guild?"
"Confirmed."
[Ding! You are registering a guild. Please enter the guild name.]
Daniel thought for a moment and entered a word: Doom!

She had even seen on the World Channel that a large guild was offering a million gold coins to buy it!
So, why her?
After hesitating, she couldn’t help but send a message.
"Lord Faustus, why did you sell it to me?"
"I heard Rhine Guild offered a million gold coins, but I only offered 10,000..."
She waited for quite a while before a message finally popped up.
"It’s nothing, just thought your name sounded nice!"
Huh?
Crimson Soul froze.
This reason... was way too casual, wasn’t it?
For Daniel, since the companion egg wasn’t bound to him, it was always going to be sold.
Who he sold it to wasn’t particularly important; he simply chose someone trustworthy.
Crimson Soul would eventually become one of the top human fighters, always at the frontlines against the evil gods!
Helping her—and even Daniel selling those items to players at a cheap price—was in a way helping humanity rise!
Crimson Soul wasn’t a pretentious person.
Since she couldn’t figure it out, she didn’t waste time thinking more about it.
She looked at the companion egg in her hand, excitement flashing in her eyes.
"No matter what, I owe you one."
"If you ever need anything, feel free to ask me!"
She sent a friend request.
Daniel accepted.
Then, his profile picture completely grayed out.
Crimson Soul stood there, softly muttering to herself.
"Faustus, huh?"
"This game god... interesting!"
Leaving the east gate, Daniel headed straight for the Luminara Trading Company!
The [Luminara Trading Company] was the largest free trading market in Luminara, offering a wide variety of goods.
As soon as he entered, he casually walked up to one of the shops, and on the shelves, he immediately spotted what he was looking for.
[Money Bag Exchange]
He walked over and opened the product details.
[Money Bag (Special Item)]
Price: 10 coins
Effect: Stores gold coins in the bag, which will not drop upon death.
Description: Hide your coins so they can’t be stolen!
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
He remembered from his previous life that this was an item unlocked only after the main city opened, designed to reduce losses upon death.
In the game, players would drop all their gold coins upon death,
but the coins in the money bag wouldn’t drop.
Moreover, the money bag was an equipment item!
What did this mean?
It meant that it could be traded!
This meant he could store gold coins in the money bag and then sell the money bag.
This way, the gold coins would become a tradeable item, allowing both the buyer and seller to bypass some of the system’s restrictions.
More importantly...
Daniel suddenly had a brilliant idea.
He could sell the money bags to players, triggering the Millionfold Boost.
Then, the game’s gold coins would multiply!
He took a deep breath and immediately bought 100 money bags.
[Ding!
You’ve reached today’s purchase limit for money bags!]
Then, he anonymously listed one item in the player marketplace, taking a "let’s try it" approach.
[Item: Money Bag (contains 10,000 gold coins)]
[Price: 1 copper coin]
[Purchase Method: Seller must agree!]
[Seller’s Note: Cash transaction, 5 dollars = 1 gold coin...
Interested parties can add the bank account: XXXX-XXXX...
Pay first, then ship!]
He listed the money bag and began to wait.
Soon, someone on the World Channel noticed the bizarre listing.
"HOLY SHIT!
Look at the marketplace, someone is selling a money bag containing 10,000 gold coins for 1 copper coin, but it’s a cash transaction!"
"5 dollars per gold coin?
The black market price is only 3.5 dollars, right?"
"But the money bag is a good item, it prevents gold coins from dropping upon death!"
"Crap, if everyone starts selling these money bags, where will we get old items to drop gold coins..."
"This person must be crazy, only a fool would buy..."
Daniel knew someone would buy it.
Since the game had just opened, gold coins were extremely scarce.
Those big guilds, desperate to secure resources, were willing to pay high prices to buy gold coins.
Although 5-1 was expensive, to them, it was pocket change.
Sure enough, within ten minutes, he received a private message.
[Anonymous Player (Private Message)]: I’ll take the 10,000 gold coins, 50,000 dollars have been transferred to your account, please check.
Daniel opened his phone (the game pod had real-world communication functions), and sure enough, there was a bank text message.
[Your account ending in XXXX has received a transfer of 50,000 dollars...]
He immediately moved the funds through a dozen accounts to ensure it couldn’t be traced back.
Once the money was secure, he returned to the marketplace, found the buyer, and clicked [Agree to Sell].
[Ding!
Item sold: Money Bag (contains 10,000 gold coins), Price: 1 copper coin, Millionfold Boost triggered!]
[Received 1 gold coin!]
[Detected that the item has no quality attributes, automatic quantity increase, received 10,000,000,000 gold coins!]
[Detected that the transaction involves real currency, triggering real-world amplification!]
[Received 50,000,000,000 dollars!]
The next second, his phone vibrated wildly.
[Your account ending in XXXX has received fifty billion dollars...]
A series of transaction notifications flooded in, and his balance instantly reached a jaw-dropping number:
50 billion dollars.
Daniel’s hand holding the phone trembled slightly.
He knew the system was insane, but he didn’t expect it to be this insane—it even amplified real-world currency!
He took several deep breaths to quickly calm himself down.
No matter how much money he had, it was just a tool.
The true goal was that final, apocalyptic disaster!
After confirming his suspicions, Daniel quickly returned to the game.
He didn’t need the money—getting massive wealth so quickly was too risky for the shadow account.
He decided to slowly unload the goods in batches.
But now, he had more important things to do.
He headed straight for the guild registration NPC at the main city guild management hall.
"Hello, I would like to register a guild."
The NPC nodded politely: "Please provide your ID and 500,000 gold coins as registration fees."
Daniel pulled out the Apprentice Merit Medal—this item gave him certain privileges with official organizations.
When the NPC saw the medal, their attitude immediately became more respectful.
"Ah, a meritorious person!
You have priority handling rights."
"To register a guild, you need 500,000 gold coins and at least 3 members.
Do you have members?"
Daniel shook his head.
"Just me for now."
"Just one person?
That requires special permission."
The NPC thought for a moment and continued.
"However, with your Merit Medal, we can make an exception.
Are you sure you want to register the guild?"
"Confirmed."
[Ding!
You are registering a guild.
Please enter the guild name.]
Daniel thought for a moment and entered a word: Doom!

chapters.title: Chapter 17 -17-Second Class, Legendary-Grade Engineer
paragraphs: [Ding! The guild name "Doom" is available, would you like to confirm?]
[Confirm.]
[Guild registration successful! 500,000 gold coins deducted, congratulations on successfully founding Doom Guild!]
[Ding! Doom Guild has been established. You may recruit members for business, mercenary, employment, and other activities. The guild has independent assets.]
Daniel looked at this system notification and couldn’t help but smile.
Guilds in the Stellar world could operate just like real-world companies, with their own independent accounts and assets.
Guilds, much like independent corporations in the real world, were individual entities.
As the guild leader, Daniel could directly inject funds into the guild, completing the initial funding, or he could "sell" things he acquired to the guild.
If he wanted to withdraw assets from the guild, he only needed to pay a very low fee, similar to personal income tax in the real world.
Simply put, he was the only shareholder of the guild, with unlimited funding, internal transactions, and unrestricted rights to withdraw dividends!
This setup would allow him to trigger Millionfold Boost while keeping the resources within his own faction, preventing them from leaking!

For example, if he acquired a blackgold-grade weapon, he could first sell it to the guild to trigger Millionfold Boost and receive the weapon back, while the original blackgold-grade weapon would belong to the guild.
The guild could then use it to arm its members or sell it to designated players!
This was simply the perfect resource loop!
After all, the world was full of all sorts of creatures, and there were those among other races willing to fall into the clutches of evil gods. Similarly, humanity wouldn’t lack such individuals!
Though Daniel needed to strengthen humanity’s overall power, it was also necessary to remove the traitors within the human faction!
Fortunately, over the course of four lifetimes, he had recorded the information of the traitor guilds and human powerhouses.
Once he had the time, they would be the first targets he dealt with!
Just then, a system notification spammed the World Channel.
[Ding! Server-wide announcement: Player "Faustus" has established the "Doom Guild." As the first guild ever created, Doom Guild will go down in Stellar history!]
[As the first player to create a guild, the following exclusive rewards have been granted:]
[1 Guild Name: Guild level automatically upgraded to Lv.3, member limit increased by 4000, guild warehouse expanded to 10,000 slots.]
[2 Gift of Prosperity: All guild members receive +5% experience gain and +5% drop rate when in a group.]
[3 Growth Pact: Guild shop unlocked early, members can exchange contributions for experience potions, enhancement stones, rare materials, refreshed weekly!]
[4 Flag of Summoning: Receive the unique item "Doom Flag." When used, all members’ attack power is increased by 15% for 2 hours, with a 7-day cooldown.]
[5 Heart of the Territory: Guild base automatically unlocks Lv.2, with training dummies included. Members can practice skills here, increasing proficiency speed by +10%.]
The World Channel exploded.
"WTF! Experience and gold coin bonuses? This is insane!"
"Does Doom Guild recruit? I’m a level 20 warrior, I can fight and tank!"
"Faustus, look at me! I’ll bring my own supplies!"
"This reward is better than working a job! I want to join..."
"Don’t run ahead, let’s team up and apply together!"
Daniel watched the system spam with application messages, a smile playing on his lips.
There was no rush—he had many things to handle first, and he could recruit slowly once he got everything in order.
He opened the guild panel.
[Doom Guild (Lv.3)]
Leader: Faustus
Members: 1/10000
Assets: gold coins
Guild Warehouse: Empty
Guild Skills: None
Daniel transferred 1 billion gold coins into the guild as initial funding.
Then, he began to think about the next steps.
Now that he had money, top-tier equipment, a legendary-grade pet, and his own guild, the next move was to expand and seize the initiative.
He was going to break the monopoly that the big guilds had on resources this time around!
Daniel turned and headed towards the east district of the main city.
There was a nondescript building there, with a brass plaque hanging at the door.
[Engineer Guild]
He pushed the door open and entered, finding the place eerily quiet with only a few NPCs dozing off.
He walked up to the counter and tapped the table.
"Hello, I’d like to buy an Engineer Scroll."
The old man behind the counter lazily looked up at him and said,
"E-grade Engineer Scroll for 100 silver coins, F-grade for 10 silver coins..."
"I want to buy an A-grade scroll. Here’s 10,000 gold coins!"
At the old man’s surprised gaze, Daniel pulled out a money bag.
"A, A-grade?"
The old man’s laziness instantly vanished.
You see, the engineer sub-class was not popular in the early game, and few people were willing to spend 10,000 gold coins on a profession scroll.
He had assumed Daniel was just a newbie from Starter Village, but the man casually pulled out 10,000 gold coins!
The A-grade Engineer Scroll was the highest-level scroll available for sale. Anything higher required passing stringent exams and completing tasks to level up.
"Well, well, honored guest, here is the item you requested. Please take it!"
[Ding! You have obtained: Engineer Scroll (A-grade)]
Daniel didn’t use the scroll immediately. Instead, he opened the guild panel and found the [Guild Trade] option.
[You are trading items with Doom Guild: Engineer Scroll (A-grade)]
[Ding! Trade successful!]
[Detected that you are selling an item to your own guild. Triggering trade determination...]
[Ding! Sold item: Engineer Scroll (A-grade), price 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[The item sold is a sub-class level scroll. Player chooses quality boost!]
[Congratulations, player, you have obtained: Engineer Scroll (legendary-grade)]
Daniel took a deep breath.
Legendary-grade!
The sub-class levels in Stellar world ranged from F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, SSS, legendary-grade, to supreme-grade!
Legendary-grade engineers were rare, and SSS-grade was already a rare breed.
He had heard that only a few players had reached legendary-grade in previous lives!
Without hesitation, he used the scroll.
[Ding! You have changed your class to: Legendary-grade Engineer]
[Ding! Legendary-grade class features unlocked!]
[Building Modification Permission: You may alter and change existing buildings in the game world, including but not limited to Starter Village, main city, fortresses, and other areas.]
[Terrain Editing Permission: You may make limited edits to the terrain in the game world (using resources).]
[Portal Network Construction: You may build and connect portals to create a private teleportation network.]
[Building Upgrade and Enhancement: You may upgrade existing buildings to improve their functions and attributes.]
Daniel stared at the string of descriptions and couldn’t help but smile.
Modify main city buildings, edit terrain, build a teleportation network?
It seemed his guess had been correct—these permissions gave him a huge advantage in making continuous profits!
Without further hesitation, he turned around and walked out.
His next target: the main city portal!
The portal in Luminara was located in the central square of the city, the only passage between major cities and Starter Village.
At that moment, only a few NPCs were coming and going near the portal.
Daniel quickly spotted a figure standing next to the portal!

chapters.title: Chapter 18 -18-Build Portals All Over Main City!
paragraphs: In front of Daniel stood a plump middle-aged man.
He was wearing greasy work clothes and holding a wrench, leaning against a pillar while dozing off.
[Main City Portal Administrator · Harold (LV220)]
Daniel approached, but the fat man didn’t even lift his eyelids, mumbling,
"One silver coin per teleportation."
Daniel didn’t move: "I’m not here to teleport."
Only then did Harold open his eyes, glancing at him impatiently.
"A level 50 kid? What are you here for if you’re not teleporting? Causing trouble?"
"I heard the portal has been experiencing aging and malfunctions, I’d like to try repairing it."
Harold froze for a moment, then burst into loud laughter.
"Hahahaha... You?"
"A level 50 kid trying to rebuild a portal? Do you even know who built this portal?"
"This was built by me! I’m an SSS-level engineer! I couldn’t even find the issue, who do you think you are?"
Ignoring his mockery, Daniel walked straight up to the portal and placed his hand on its frame.
Harold watched his movements, his expression turning to one of anger and disdain.
This was his life’s work! If this kid actually managed to fix it, he would drink three barrels of rum!
"Shit, stop!"
As Daniel suddenly stepped back and drew his longbow, Harold felt something was wrong.
He instantly charged, unleashing the full force of his level 220 warrior class, the air around him seemingly freezing.
His right hand shot out to grab Daniel by the neck.
If he caught him, this level 50 archer would probably be sent back to the city to respawn!
But just as his fingers were about to make contact with Daniel’s neck,
Daniel disappeared.
He reappeared on the other side of the portal, raised his hand, and fired an arrow at the portal!
Harold’s claw grabbed nothing, and he froze for half a second.
Half a second was enough for him to launch a second attack.
But in that half second, he witnessed a scene that he would never forget.
The arrow split into twelve beams of light in midair, accurately hitting twelve key nodes of the portal.
But it wasn’t destruction, as Harold had expected. Instead, it was... deconstruction!
With each beam of light that landed, a rune stone automatically detached and floated in the air.
Energy conduits broke apart automatically.
The whole process was smooth as flowing water, as if an invisible engineering team was working in unison.
Harold’s hand froze in midair, his mouth hanging open, as if he could fit a fist in.
What had he just seen?
This was a monster capable of performing twelve precise operations in mere fractions of a second!
"My gods, you... you are..."
Daniel turned his head, giving him a casual glance.
"Can I continue?"
Harold silently withdrew his hand.
[Ding! Do you wish to deconstruct this portal?]
[Confirm.]
The next second, a miracle happened.
The massive portal began to break down into countless tiny light particles, with rune stones automatically detaching and floating in the air, and energy conduits hovering in place...
The entire deconstruction process was orderly, as if an invisible hand were performing a delicate operation.
"What?!"
Harold’s wrench fell to the ground with a clatter.
"This... this can’t be!"
In just thirty seconds, the once complete portal turned into a neat pile of materials on the ground.
[Deconstruction successful!]
[Obtained: Spatial Stone (Core Material) ×1, Spatial Runes ×12, Energy Conduits ×8, Base Stone ×Several]
Daniel glanced at the materials, a plan forming in his mind.
He opened the guild panel and sold all the materials to Doom Guild.
[Ding! You are selling items to Doom Guild: Full portal materials, price 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[Boost option: Quantity boost/Quality boost]
Daniel selected quantity boost.
[Congratulations! You have obtained: Teleportation Stones (Core Material) ×1,000,000, Spatial Runes ×12,000,000, Energy Conduits ×8,000,000, Base Stones...]
A massive amount of materials instantly appeared in the guild warehouse, piling up into small mountains.
Daniel took a set of complete materials and began to rebuild the portal.
His hands moved quickly through the air, drawing energy lines that interwove, with runes automatically embedding and energy conduits precisely connecting...
Five minutes later, a brand-new portal appeared in the same spot.
It was bigger, more refined, and its energy fluctuations were more stable than the original!
Harold stood there with his mouth agape, his eyes nearly popping out.
"Legendary-grade... You must be a legendary-grade engineer, at the very least?!"
"But... but how is this possible? You’re only level 50!"
Daniel patted his hands and turned to look at him.
"Do you believe me now?"
But to Daniel’s surprise, the next moment Harold suddenly dropped to his knees!
"Master!"
"I’ve been stuck at the SSS-level for twenty years, how did you do this? Can you teach me?"
Daniel pulled him up.
"Get up first. I have business to attend to."
He pointed to the newly built portal.
"I want to build a teleportation network all over Luminara!"
"Major districts, important instance entrances, business areas, quest hubs... all covered with portals."
Harold’s eyes widened.
"How many materials and energy will this take? Plus, the main city council would never approve..."
Daniel interrupted him.
"I have the materials, as for the approval..."
He stared at Harold.
"You’re the main city portal administrator. Isn’t that your job?"
Harold paused for a moment, then slapped his thigh.
"Right! I’m the administrator!"
"I can approve it! Those old fools at the main city council don’t know anything about engineering!"
He rubbed his hands excitedly.
"So, how do you want to build it?"
Daniel opened the map and quickly marked the locations.

"One main station in the central square, one in the east district shopping street, one in the west district instance area, one in the south district quest hall, one in the north district residential area..."
"Also, at the entrances of major guilds, several popular instance entrances, and city gates... a total of thirty-seven points."
Harold gasped.
"Thirty-seven? The workload..."
"Don’t worry, I’ll provide the materials."
Daniel said calmly, "Also, once all the portals are built, you’ll get 20% of the income, Luminara gets 1%."
Harold’s eyes instantly lit up.
"Deal!"
In the next few hours, NPCs all over Luminara witnessed a spectacular scene.
A figure with a silver bow was flying across the city, followed by Harold, who was eagerly trailing behind him.
Every time Daniel landed at a spot, he would tinker with it for a while, and then a brand-new portal would appear there.
"John, I’m not seeing things, right? There’s suddenly a portal in the shopping street?"
"There’s one in the quest hall too!"
"There’s one at the city gate!"
"What’s going on? Is Luminara developing?"
"I just saw Harold over there messing with it. Could he have built this?"
"Don’t joke, Harold’s portals start malfunctioning after a while, how could he build so many, and with so much material waste, how could the city lord approve this?"
"So what’s the explanation for this then?"

Harold’s hand froze in midair, his mouth hanging open, as if he could fit a fist in.
What had he just seen?
This was a monster capable of performing twelve precise operations in mere fractions of a second!
"My gods, you... you are..."
Daniel turned his head, giving him a casual glance.
"Can I continue?"
Harold silently withdrew his hand.
[Ding!
Do you wish to deconstruct this portal?]
[Confirm.]
The next second, a miracle happened.
The massive portal began to break down into countless tiny light particles, with rune stones automatically detaching and floating in the air, and energy conduits hovering in place...
The entire deconstruction process was orderly, as if an invisible hand were performing a delicate operation.
"What?!"
Harold’s wrench fell to the ground with a clatter.
"This... this can’t be!"
In just thirty seconds, the once complete portal turned into a neat pile of materials on the ground.
[Deconstruction successful!]
[Obtained: Spatial Stone (Core Material) ×1, Spatial Runes ×12, Energy Conduits ×8, Base Stone ×Several]
Daniel glanced at the materials, a plan forming in his mind.
He opened the guild panel and sold all the materials to Doom Guild.
[Ding!
You are selling items to Doom Guild: Full portal materials, price 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[Boost option: Quantity boost/Quality boost]
Daniel selected quantity boost.
[Congratulations!
You have obtained: Teleportation Stones (Core Material) ×1,000,000, Spatial Runes ×12,000,000, Energy Conduits ×8,000,000, Base Stones...]
A massive amount of materials instantly appeared in the guild warehouse, piling up into small mountains.
Daniel took a set of complete materials and began to rebuild the portal.
His hands moved quickly through the air, drawing energy lines that interwove, with runes automatically embedding and energy conduits precisely connecting...
Five minutes later, a brand-new portal appeared in the same spot.
It was bigger, more refined, and its energy fluctuations were more stable than the original!
Harold stood there with his mouth agape, his eyes nearly popping out.
"Legendary-grade...
You must be a legendary-grade engineer, at the very least?!"
"But... but how is this possible?
You’re only level 50!"
Daniel patted his hands and turned to look at him.
"Do you believe me now?"
But to Daniel’s surprise, the next moment Harold suddenly dropped to his knees!
"Master!"
"I’ve been stuck at the SSS-level for twenty years, how did you do this?
Can you teach me?"
Daniel pulled him up.
"Get up first.
I have business to attend to."
He pointed to the newly built portal.
"I want to build a teleportation network all over Luminara!"
"Major districts, important instance entrances, business areas, quest hubs... all covered with portals."
Harold’s eyes widened.
"How many materials and energy will this take?
Plus, the main city council would never approve..."
Daniel interrupted him.
"I have the materials, as for the approval..."
He stared at Harold.
"You’re the main city portal administrator.
Isn’t that your job?"
Harold paused for a moment, then slapped his thigh.
"Right!
I’m the administrator!"
"I can approve it!
Those old fools at the main city council don’t know anything about engineering!"
He rubbed his hands excitedly.
"So, how do you want to build it?"
Daniel opened the map and quickly marked the locations.

"One main station in the central square, one in the east district shopping street, one in the west district instance area, one in the south district quest hall, one in the north district residential area..."
"Also, at the entrances of major guilds, several popular instance entrances, and city gates... a total of thirty-seven points."
Harold gasped.
"Thirty-seven?
The workload..."
"Don’t worry, I’ll provide the materials."
Daniel said calmly, "Also, once all the portals are built, you’ll get 20% of the income, Luminara gets 1%."
Harold’s eyes instantly lit up.
"Deal!"
In the next few hours, NPCs all over Luminara witnessed a spectacular scene.
A figure with a silver bow was flying across the city, followed by Harold, who was eagerly trailing behind him.
Every time Daniel landed at a spot, he would tinker with it for a while, and then a brand-new portal would appear there.
"John, I’m not seeing things, right?
There’s suddenly a portal in the shopping street?"
"There’s one in the quest hall too!"
"There’s one at the city gate!"
"What’s going on?
Is Luminara developing?"
"I just saw Harold over there messing with it.
Could he have built this?"
"Don’t joke, Harold’s portals start malfunctioning after a while, how could he build so many, and with so much material waste, how could the city lord approve this?"
"So what’s the explanation for this then?"

chapters.title: Chapter 19 -19-Setting Up the Plan, Big Harvest
paragraphs: At 10 PM, the last portal was completed.
Daniel stood in front of the central square, looking at his masterpiece with satisfaction.
Thirty-seven portals now covered the entire city.
Each portal had its usage permissions set.
Apart from NPCs, only players from World 616 could use them, at a cost of 1 copper coin per use.
This meant that starting tomorrow, all players from World 616 could teleport to any corner of Luminara for just 1 copper coin.
Doing quests? No need to run around.
Going to an instance? Simply teleport right to the entrance.
Returning to town to turn in a quest? A one-second trip.
This would completely change the gameplay efficiency for players from World 616.
1 copper coin was practically nothing for both players and NPCs!
Hearing this pricing, Harold was stunned.
The materials and cost for building a single portal were astronomical!
And now, a copper coin per use?
It would take forever to break even!
He thought Daniel was here to monopolize the business, but he didn’t expect him to be running a charity!
Harold stood by, watching Daniel’s back, deep in thought.
After finishing everything, Daniel checked the time—10:30 PM!
It was time to log off and rest!
Daniel sat up from the game pod, stretching his neck.
The room felt familiar, and the night view outside the window was just as it always was.
But this time, his feelings were completely different!
He picked up his phone and opened social media.
The top trending topic!
[All players are born in Starter Village 616, what does this mean?]
Clicking on it, he found expert analyses flooding the feed.
"Based on current data, all players worldwide are born in Starter Village 616... Does this mean our world has been labeled as World 616 by the game system?"
"More worryingly, we’ve made contact with players from other parallel worlds, but the results suggest that these other worlds’ inhabitants might not be so friendly..."
Daniel furrowed his brow.
His memories from previous lives resurfaced—the World War indeed broke out during the mid-game.
Human factions from different numbered worlds fought brutally for resources.
He kept scrolling down.
Second trending topic!
[Who is the great player Faustus? What’s his mindset?]
The comments below were all over the place.
"I’ll start, he’s definitely a professional gamer!"
"Even professional gamers aren’t this crazy. He hit level 50 in a day and soloed a boss!"
"I think he’s an insider from the game company."
"An insider wouldn’t dare do this, aren’t they afraid of being banned?"
"Banned? The GM would probably be too scared of him to ban him, hahaha..."
"I think he’s a reincarnator. Do you believe it?"
"A reincarnator? Why don’t you just say he’s a god descended from the heavens?"
"Forget everything else, just the fact that Faustus is selling gear at a low price, I’m totally for him!"
"Yeah, I’m a fan now. Faustus, take me to the top!"
Daniel smiled and was about to put his phone down when he suddenly remembered something.
He opened his phone’s banking app and stared at the fifty billion dollars in his account.
This was the real-world currency transferred to him by the system after selling the money bags and triggering the Millionfold Boost.
At the time, he was so excited that he hadn’t thought much about what this meant.
But now, staring at the number, a cold sweat started to form.
The game’s system was influencing the real world!
In his previous lives, nothing like this had ever happened.
But this time...
Daniel stared at the phone screen, his mind racing.
If Millionfold Boost could affect real-world currency, could it also affect other things?
If the boundaries between the game and the real world were blurring, what did that mean?
It meant that the disaster of the game turning into reality could have already started, three years earlier than expected!
Daniel took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down.
No matter what, he needed to prepare.
He opened his computer and set up a carefully prepared virtual bank account.
This account was routed through a dozen overseas banks, making it impossible to trace back to him.
Then, he started the transfers.
One billion dollars to a real estate company in Country A to purchase a large plot of land in the Alar District.
One hundred billion dollars to a construction company in Country B, commissioning the building of an underground fortress.
Requirements: nuclear-proof, biohazard-proof, self-sustaining, able to house a thousand people for a hundred years.
Next, he contacted a supplier in Country C to order the highest-quality game pods and top-tier nutritional solutions for three years.
One transfer after another, the complex orders were quickly confirmed amidst a flurry of banknotes.
By 3 AM, all arrangements were in place.
Daniel lay back on his bed, staring at the ceiling.

The construction of the fortress would take time. Even though he had offered far more than expected, with the promise of gathering the world’s top building firms for the job, it would still take at least three months!
The nutritional solutions and game pods would probably arrive tomorrow.
Over the next three months, he had to continue getting stronger in the game while closely monitoring the changes in the real world!
The next morning, when Daniel woke up, the game pods and nutritional solutions had already arrived at his door!
After assembling everything, Daniel logged into the game at 9 AM.
A flash of light, and he appeared in Luminara’s central square.
The portals around him were already in use, with players coming in and out, all wearing expressions of excitement.
"Holy Shit! This portal really only costs 1 copper coin!"
"I just teleported from the shopping street to the instance entrance. I got there in one second!"
"Luminara’s transport system is so convenient now?!"
"Does Doom Guild still recruit? I’ve applied for 3 hours!"
"Who knows? I applied last night!"
Daniel smiled and didn’t respond. Instead, he opened the message panel.
The next moment, the system notifications exploded like firecrackers!
[Ding! You have 999+ private messages!]
[Ding! You have 999+ friend requests!]
[Ding! Your trade market order has been completed, please check!]
[Ding! Your...]
Daniel was stunned by the barrage of notifications.
He quickly silenced all the message alerts temporarily.
Then, he opened the trade market backend.
Before he logged off last night, he had listed all the gear he obtained from the event.
He set the items to be sold after 3 hours, exactly when he was offline.
But now that he logged back in, the expected orders were flooding in...
[Trade market order settlement]
[Items sold: 3,847]
[Trigger Millionfold Boost!]
[Total income in gold coins: 4,524,673,892]
[Congratulations! You obtained: Legendary-grade gear/materials × 3,847!]
[Congratulations! You obtained: Supreme-grade items × 2!]
Daniel froze.
Over 3,000 legendary-grade items?
He took a deep breath and opened his backpack.
The entire backpack space was packed full with various gleaming items.
There were over two thousand pieces of legendary-grade gear.
The rest were legendary-grade materials, including dragon scales, dragon blood, silver-grade ores, arcane crystals...
At the most prominent spot in the backpack, two items emitted a unique red-gold glow!
These were the two supreme-grade pieces of gear and materials!

chapters.title: Chapter 20 -20-Mass Sale Settlement! SSS-level Star Ascension Quest
paragraphs: The first item was a pair of miniature wings!
They were entirely black, with red-black glowing patterns on the edges, and just looking at them made Daniel feel the terrifying energy within.
[Black Dragon King’s Protection (Supreme-grade)]
Magical Defense: +2000
Physical Defense: +2000
Skill 1 - Dark Dragon Wings:
Flying speed +8000%, immune to all magic damage while flying.
Skill 2 - Dragon King’s Pressure:
Passive effect, applies pressure to legendary-grade and below creatures, reducing all attributes by 30%!
Can be activated to stun all enemies within 100 meters, inducing fear for 3 seconds (cooldown 5 minutes).
Skill 3 - Shadow Shelter:
When attacked, automatically triggers a shadow shield, absorbing 20,000 damage and rebounding 100% of the damage to the attacker. The shield lasts for 10 seconds, cooldown 5 minutes.
Skill 4 - Black Dragon Bloodline:
All four core attributes +500, HP +10,000, MP +10,000, all attribute resistances +50%!
Equipment Requirement: Level 50 or higher, Constitution 500+.
Description: Forged using the Black Dragon Wing as the core, combined with supreme-grade Strength from the Dragon Clan. When you spread your wings, you are the ruler of the dark sky.
Daniel’s breath slowed for a moment.
All four core attributes +500!
HP and MP both +10,000!
Flying speed 8000%, immunity to magic damage?
Without a second thought, he equipped the Black Dragon Wings.
Strangely, he didn’t feel any weight, nor could he see any equipment on his back.
With a thought, two enormous black dragon wings instantly unfolded from his back!
They spanned over ten meters, and every feather glimmered with a cold metallic sheen, with red arcs of lightning dancing on the edges.
With a thought, he shot into the sky, soaring to a height of one kilometer in an instant!
Fast!
Too fast!
He tried performing a roll in mid-air, and the movement was so fluid it felt like he had always been a flying creature.
The surrounding players only saw a shadow flash by, and then nothing.
"HOLY SHIT, what just flew past?"
"A bird?"
"Does your bird have ten-meter wings?"
"This is a game, are you an idiot..."
Daniel landed back on the ground, retracting his wings.
Then he looked at the second item.
It was a crystal core the size of a fist, shining brilliantly like a diamond, with a golden dragon silhouette faintly visible swimming inside.
[Sacred Dragon Core (Supreme-grade/Special Material)]
Type: Pet Evolution Material
Effect: A supreme-grade crystal core containing the essence of the Sacred Dragon Clan’s bloodline, can be used for pet evolution.
Feeding it to a dragon-type pet will evolve it into a higher-grade dragon species, unlocking new forms and skills.
Currently compatible: Earthmount Dragon (Ancient Dragon) → After evolution, can advance to Supreme-grade!
Note: The higher the pet’s level, the higher the evolution success rate. It’s recommended to use it on pets level 100 or higher.
Description: Awakened unexpectedly by supreme-grade Strength, this crystal core can change the fate of a dragon descendant.
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
He quickly opened the pet space.
The little stone dragon was curled up and fast asleep.
After finishing off its egg shell last night, it had fallen into a deep sleep.
[Earthmount Dragon (Ancient Dragon·LV15)]
Status: Sleeping (digesting energy), estimated awakening time: 23 hours.
Daniel smiled and closed the pet space.
No rush, he would wait for it to wake up.
By then, the [Sacred Dragon Core] would be for it.
He focused on his attribute panel.
[Player: Faustus]
[Level: 50 (Experience pool overflow)]
[Intelligence: 755 → +500 = 1255]
[Constitution: 755 → +500 = 1255]
Daniel stared at the numbers, silent for a full five seconds.
All attributes at 1255!
And with the various broken skills of the Black Dragon Wings.
If he stood still and let a level 50 monster attack him, it would probably take them quite a while to break his defenses.
And this was only the first day since the game started!
He took a deep breath and closed the panel.
It was time to head to the archer guild to do the Star Ascension Quest!
Soon, Daniel arrived at the archer guild in Main City.
The most luxurious building on the entire street, it was made entirely of white jade, with two elven archer statues at the entrance and exquisitely elegant interiors.
In contrast, the warrior guild next door looked like a few large stones stacked together—rough and simple.
Daniel walked into the lobby, where many NPC archers were active.
They all had different levels and task difficulties displayed above their heads.
[Junior Instructor: Provides F-C level Star Ascension Quests]
[Intermediate Instructor: Provides B-A level Star Ascension Quests]
[Advanced Instructor: Provides S-SS level Star Ascension Quests]
[Secret Instructor: Provides SSS-level and above Star Ascension Quests]
Daniel walked straight to the innermost area, where a mysterious figure, cloaked and with an indistinguishable face, stood.
[Secret Instructor · Shadow Song]
"I want to take the Star Ascension Quest, the hardest one!"
Shadow Song raised her head, revealing deep eyes.
She gave Daniel a once-over, a faint smile curling her lips.
"A level 50 Burstshot God... Interesting."
She handed him a scroll.
[Star Ascension Quest: Shadow of the Dark God (SSS-level)]

[Quest Description: The southern town of Grayvale has been occupied by a group of cultists who worship an extradimensional evil god. They have activated an altar, tearing the earth apart and summoning the projection of the evil god. The most elite warriors are needed to go to Grayvale, destroy the altar, and kill the cult’s high priest.]
[Quest Objective: Kill the cult’s high priest (LV55 blackgold-grade BOSS), destroy the evil god’s altar.]
[Quest Rewards: +1 class star, +100 attributes, unlock upgrade permissions, unlock new class skills.]
After accepting the quest, Daniel was immediately teleported away!
His vision blurred, and he found himself standing under a dim sky.
The town ahead was shrouded in thick black mist, and through the mist, he could vaguely make out twisted building outlines.
The air was filled with the stench of decay and sulfur, the ground cracked, and black slime seeped out from the fissures.
[Ding! You have entered the special area: Grayvale Town.]
[Area Effect: Continuously affected by the Evil God’s whispers, losing 1% HP per second.]
Daniel glanced at his HP and smiled.
Infinite Grail—during combat, it restores 1% HP per second.
Since he was already in combat mode as he entered the map, the 1% HP loss and the 1% HP recovery perfectly balanced out.
He walked boldly into the black mist.
The town was eerily silent.
The houses along the streets had broken windows and doors, and various debris littered the ground.
But what was most bizarre were the wandering creatures!
They still had human bodies, but their heads had transformed into various animals—wolf heads, deer heads... and even pig heads!
They crawled on all fours like beasts, growling lowly.
[Aberration · LV35 (common-grade)]
Daniel raised his hand and shot an arrow.
The arrow pierced through a wolf-headed creature’s chest, exploding it into pieces.
The surrounding Aberrations were alerted and rushed towards him with a growl.
Daniel fired several more arrows, instantly clearing the wave.
He pressed on.
The further he went towards the town center, the stronger the monsters became.
LV40 Fused Ones—human bodies with multiple animal heads, with bizarre attack patterns.
LV45 Twisted Ones—bodies completely deformed, like piles of rotten flesh growing countless arms and legs, slowly crawling.
Daniel looked at these grotesque humanoids, feeling disgusted.
While these monsters were weak and couldn’t even break his defenses, the sight of them was repulsive!

It was time to head to the archer guild to do the Star Ascension Quest!
Soon, Daniel arrived at the archer guild in Main City.
The most luxurious building on the entire street, it was made entirely of white jade, with two elven archer statues at the entrance and exquisitely elegant interiors.
In contrast, the warrior guild next door looked like a few large stones stacked together—rough and simple.
Daniel walked into the lobby, where many NPC archers were active.
They all had different levels and task difficulties displayed above their heads.
[Junior Instructor: Provides F-C level Star Ascension Quests]
[Intermediate Instructor: Provides B-A level Star Ascension Quests]
[Advanced Instructor: Provides S-SS level Star Ascension Quests]
[Secret Instructor: Provides SSS-level and above Star Ascension Quests]
Daniel walked straight to the innermost area, where a mysterious figure, cloaked and with an indistinguishable face, stood.
[Secret Instructor · Shadow Song]
"I want to take the Star Ascension Quest, the hardest one!"
Shadow Song raised her head, revealing deep eyes.
She gave Daniel a once-over, a faint smile curling her lips.
"A level 50 Burstshot God...
Interesting."
She handed him a scroll.
[Star Ascension Quest: Shadow of the Dark God (SSS-level)]
[Quest Description: The southern town of Grayvale has been occupied by a group of cultists who worship an extradimensional evil god.
They have activated an altar, tearing the earth apart and summoning the projection of the evil god.
The most elite warriors are needed to go to Grayvale, destroy the altar, and kill the cult’s high priest.]
[Quest Objective: Kill the cult’s high priest (LV55 blackgold-grade BOSS), destroy the evil god’s altar.]
[Quest Rewards: +1 class star, +100 attributes, unlock upgrade permissions, unlock new class skills.]
After accepting the quest, Daniel was immediately teleported away!
His vision blurred, and he found himself standing under a dim sky.
The town ahead was shrouded in thick black mist, and through the mist, he could vaguely make out twisted building outlines.
The air was filled with the stench of decay and sulfur, the ground cracked, and black slime seeped out from the fissures.
[Ding!
You have entered the special area: Grayvale Town.]
[Area Effect: Continuously affected by the Evil God’s whispers, losing 1% HP per second.]
Daniel glanced at his HP and smiled.
Infinite Grail—during combat, it restores 1% HP per second.
Since he was already in combat mode as he entered the map, the 1% HP loss and the 1% HP recovery perfectly balanced out.
He walked boldly into the black mist.
The town was eerily silent.
The houses along the streets had broken windows and doors, and various debris littered the ground.
But what was most bizarre were the wandering creatures!
They still had human bodies, but their heads had transformed into various animals—wolf heads, deer heads... and even pig heads!
They crawled on all fours like beasts, growling lowly.
[Aberration · LV35 (common-grade)]
Daniel raised his hand and shot an arrow.
The arrow pierced through a wolf-headed creature’s chest, exploding it into pieces.
The surrounding Aberrations were alerted and rushed towards him with a growl.
Daniel fired several more arrows, instantly clearing the wave.
He pressed on.
The further he went towards the town center, the stronger the monsters became.
LV40 Fused Ones—human bodies with multiple animal heads, with bizarre attack patterns.
LV45 Twisted Ones—bodies completely deformed, like piles of rotten flesh growing countless arms and legs, slowly crawling.
Daniel looked at these grotesque humanoids, feeling disgusted.
While these monsters were weak and couldn’t even break his defenses, the sight of them was repulsive!

chapters.title: Chapter 21 -21-Altar of the Dark God
paragraphs: Boom!
Rumbling violently...!
In a flash faster than the ear could catch, Daniel obliterated every low-level monster into scraps, feeling a rush of satisfaction as he approached the town’s central square.
The mist here was even thicker than at the outskirts, pressing down like a dark, suffocating blanket. Visibility was barely ten meters.
The outlines of buildings loomed faintly in the fog, like dormant beasts waiting to strike.
The air was thick with the stench of decay and sulfur, making Daniel’s stomach churn.
Beneath his feet, the ground was cracked in a web-like pattern, black viscous liquid oozing from the fissures, bubbling with a gurgling sound.
The streams of this liquid converged, flowing in a single direction—toward the center of the square.
There, a massive altar had been constructed.
Black monoliths were arranged in a circle, each stone engraved with twisted runes that faintly glowed dark red.
At the center of the altar, a gaping chasm split the ground, from which black mist surged continuously, writhing as if alive.
Around the altar stood a dozen or so figures, clad in black robes and wearing grotesque masks.
The masks bore twisted faces, the eyeholes appearing as nothing but two dark voids, seemingly capable of swallowing the soul.
[Cultist · LV50 (Iron-Grade Monster)] (Iron-grade = Elite-grade)
They were performing some kind of ritual, gesticulating wildly, muttering incantations under their breath.
The whispers overlapped into a chorus, as though countless voices murmured directly into Daniel’s ears.
Without hesitation, Daniel nocked an arrow and drew his bow.
Explosive Rain of Arrows!
Swish! Swish! Swish...!
A torrent of arrows descended from the sky, covering the entire altar.
The cultists felt a sudden chill above their heads, and when they looked up, a sky full of glowing points rained down like a shower of light.
"Could it be... the Dark God has heard our call?"
One cultist cried in ecstatic joy, arms raised to the sky.
"No... no, this is an attack!"
The lead cultist shouted in panic, but it was already too late.
Whoosh... whoosh... whoosh...
Boom!
Boom! Boom! Boom...!
The earth shook and mountains quivered; dust and smoke roiled everywhere!
The black stones of the altar shattered into fragments. The cultists barely had time to scream before they were swallowed by the flames of the explosion.
The iron-grade monsters, frozen in shock, were reduced to fragments under the barrage.
As the smoke gradually cleared, Daniel sheathed his bow and stepped toward the ruined altar.
Severed limbs littered the ground, black blood seeping into the cracked earth.
The cultists’ masks lay broken in pieces, revealing the twisted faces beneath.
Some were young, some lined with age, yet all shared the same final expression: madness, fanaticism, and a hint of bizarre release.
Daniel crouched and used the tip of his arrow to pull aside the robe of one corpse.
A twisted sigil was etched onto its chest—a downward-facing eye encircled by tentacle-like lines.
His pupils contracted slightly.
He had seen this symbol before.
During his fourth reincarnation, he had encountered similar tattoos on the bodies of fallen aberrant races.
Though the details differed, the twisted style and the innate sense of unease it inspired were unmistakable.
Daniel rose and scanned his surroundings.
The altar, the chasm, the black mist, the cultists...
These deformed creatures reminded him of the Beast-Turned he had seen in Windmill Town.
Could all of this be connected to that underground church?
Fragments of memories from his previous four lives flickered rapidly through his mind.
In his first life, he focused solely on leveling, indifferent to the world, knowing only that monsters existed to be slain for experience.
In his second, he vowed to defeat the Dark God and save all beings, delving into hidden quests and gradually realizing that Stellar’s worldview was far more complex than it appeared.
Magic, gods, the Dark God, racial wars, and countless hidden conspiracies—all interwoven.

In his third life, he joined a major guild, gaining access to secret intelligence: the existence of parallel world wars, humans clashing across worlds, and the ever-looming threat of the Dark God over humanity.
By his fourth life, he had reached unparalleled heights, yet could only watch as the Dark God descended, seeing the alien races submit or be slain, witnessing humanity’s banners burn to ashes.
How had those corrupted goblins, beastfolk, and seafarers fallen under the Dark God’s control?
Daniel’s gaze landed on the black mist swirling above the altar’s chasm.
In Windmill Town, the Anti-Holy Grail of the Dark God had infected the miners, spreading throughout the town.
Here, the cultists performed rituals to summon the Dark God’s Strength, birthing deformed monsters.
Both phenomena seemed to stem from the same source.
The Dark God’s Strength could infect living beings and corrupt the mind.
In Windmill Town, the miners were passively infected; these cultists, however, had approached it willingly.
Daniel frowned.
Who were these people? Why did they worship the Dark God?
For Strength? Immortality? Or had they been simply bewitched?
Was there a greater organization behind them?
Memories from his previous lives began to assemble.
He recalled tales of how, before descending, the Dark God sent emissaries to various worlds to spread faith, cultivate followers, and build altars.
These disciples would attempt to tear the world’s barriers, paving the way for the Dark God’s arrival.
And this altar, this chasm, this black mist...
Wasn’t it doing exactly that—ripping the barriers apart?
Daniel’s eyes narrowed.
If so, the cultists’ purpose was clear.
Even as mere projections, if left unchecked, any corner of this world could become a stronghold of the Dark God.
Then, it wouldn’t just be small-scale transformations like Beastification; it would be a full-scale...
Roar!
Ho-ho!
At that moment, deep, guttural howls erupted from the chasm, snapping Daniel out of his thoughts.
The black mist began to surge violently, boiling like a cauldron of water.
"Heh-heh... ke-ke-ke-ke..."
A grating voice echoed from the depths, carrying a subtle psychic assault that made Daniel’s vision waver.
He stepped back instinctively, nocking an arrow in readiness.
A massive figure slowly rose from the chasm.
First, Daniel saw a cluster of eyes.
The enormous head was bald, covered with dozens of eyes crowded together, each rotating to survey all directions.
Within each pupil was a reflection of a different scene—burning villages, crying children, mountains of corpses.
The pale human face was almost entirely consumed by eyes, leaving only a mouth that remained normal.
Its grin stretched to the ears, revealing jagged black teeth, emitting a horrifying, otherworldly laughter.
[Dark Acolyte · LV55 (Blackgold-Grade Boss)]

chapters.title: Chapter 22 -22-Dark God? Still Using Such an Outdated Concept?
paragraphs: The Dark Acolyte hovered in midair, dozens of eyes simultaneously fixated on Daniel, each burning with rage and hatred.
"You... destroyed my altar... killed my followers..."
His voice emanated as if from countless throats at once—shrill, eerie, and unnatural.
"Do you... know what you’re doing?!"
Daniel stared at him without expression.
The Dark Acolyte spread his arms, and the eyes began to spin wildly.
"We devote ourselves here, we pray here, we await the arrival of the Great One!"
"How dare you... how dare you, wretched insect..."
His voice grew higher, more frenzied with every word.
"You don’t even understand! You don’t comprehend!"
"The Great Being is about to descend, and you ants... you pitiful ants shall kneel before its feet!"
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
"The Great Being? You mean... the Dark God?"
The Dark Acolyte froze for a moment, then let out a cold, sinister laugh.
"Dark God? Hahahaha..."
"You mortals, using your meager words and limited comprehension to define that which cannot be understood!"
"Dark God? No! That is a law that existed at the dawn of the universe! You are the intruders! You are the heretics!"
His agitation grew, and the eyes began to redden, bloodshot and furious.
"You will never understand! Ants like you can only kneel and tremble when the Great Being descends, begging for its mercy!"
A faint smile curled on Daniel’s lips.
"Sorry, I’ve seen it. It’s nothing but a giant worm, isn’t it?"
The Dark Acolyte’s laughter abruptly stopped.
"What?"
"I said I’ve seen your so-called Great Being."
Daniel’s tone was calm. "I’ve seen it more than once. Yes, it’s powerful—powerful enough to make anyone despair. But in the end... it’s just a big worm, isn’t it?"
The Dark Acolyte froze for a second, then let out a roar of fury.
"Damn ant! Arrogant! Ignorant! Pathetic!"
"You saw the Great Being and lived? Do you take me for a three-year-old child?! Die, you foolish blasphemer!!"
In the next moment, Daniel felt a sharp pain strike his mind.
Countless illusions flooded his brain—failures from past lives, the deaths of comrades, the Dark God’s mockery...
[Ding! You have been targeted by a Mind-Type skill. Due to special equipment Demon’s Whisper, you are immune to all negative status effects!]
Every hallucination vanished instantly.
Daniel’s head throbbed faintly; although he was immune to the illusions, the mental attack itself was real.
But his eyes were clear, and a smile tugged at the corner of his mouth.
This guy’s only real difficulty was psychic illusions, but fortunately, Daniel could shrug off all negative states.
As for mental attacks... he had endured far worse through four cycles of rebirth—pain beyond this fool’s imagination!
Whoosh!
An arrow shot straight for the Dark Acolyte’s face!
Boom!
The explosion erupted across the Dark Acolyte’s face, forcing him several steps back. Pain and rage flickered simultaneously in his eyes.
"How dare you...!"
Daniel activated God Speed, creating distance, and fired another arrow.
"You talk too much."
The battle turned into a one-sided massacre.
The Dark Acolyte’s psychic interference was completely useless. Daniel ignored mental attacks entirely. All he could do was swing his staff and cast spells.
But with Daniel’s Agility 755 and God Speed, none of the attacks could touch him.
After just one rapid volley, the Dark Acolyte’s HP dropped to 60%.
Two volleys later, it fell to 20%!
"Cursed human! How dare you desecrate the will of the Dark God!"
The Dark Acolyte shrieked, dozens of eyes simultaneously bloodshot, glowing crimson.
Just as Daniel prepared the final strike, the Dark Acolyte let out a painful roar and his body began to swell violently.
Then, to Daniel’s stunned gaze... it self-destructed!
Boom!
Its lower body exploded, and the enormous eyes on its head shattered, black blood splattering everywhere.
A foul stench assaulted Daniel’s nose, forcing him to retreat several meters.
But the decayed flesh and blood didn’t fall—they seemed pulled by some unnatural strength, sliding entirely into the abyss!
Seconds later, the abyss shook violently.
A slimy tentacle emerged, resting on the edge of the altar.
It was as thick as a bucket, covered in countless sharp teeth, wriggling continuously.
Then a second, a third...
A completely different monster crawled from the depths.
Its lower body was all tentacles, dozens of them supporting a massive torso.
Its upper body barely retained human shape, but the flesh was blood-red, slimy, as if skinned and soaked in blood.
Viscous fluid oozed from the surface, dripping onto the floor, corroding pits into the ground.
Most terrifying was its head... or rather, it had no head.
In its hands, it held a perfectly intact human head, face twisted in agony, mouth opening and closing—it was the Dark Acolyte’s face!
[Dark God’s Plaything · LV55 (Blackgold-Grade BOSS) — Phase Two!]
Daniel frowned.
Disgusting... but disgusting or not, it had to die.
He raised his hand and unleashed another volley.
This Dark God’s Plaything was tougher than the first phase, HP at least double—at least 150,000!
The tentacles swung, blocking arrows, almost hitting him a few times.
But to Daniel, that HP was already brittle.
He created distance and activated Arrowstorm.
A stream of golden arrows shot into the sky, splitting into dozens of falling bolts, trailing golden flames like a meteor shower.
Boom... Boom... Boom...
Explosions tore across the battlefield. Two tentacles were severed. The creature shrieked in pain, swinging the remaining ones in an attempt to reach him.
Daniel activated God Speed, dodging to the other side, then unleashed another volley of explosive arrows.
Arrow after arrow pierced the twisted flesh, pinning it to the floor.
It struggled to rise, but the raining arrows forced it back down again and again.
Boom... Boom... Boom...
Explosions rocked the ground, making it sink half a meter.
Daniel had remained tens of meters away the entire time—the foul Dark God’s creation never came within twenty meters of him.
Finally, under the relentless storm of arrows, it was annihilated, twitching its tentacles a few last times before falling still.
The human head it had clutched rolled onto the ground, a bizarre serenity on its face.
[Ding! You have slain Dark God’s Plaything (Blackgold-Grade BOSS)]
[Rewards: Luck +20, Elven Pendant (Blackgold-Grade) ×1, Windrunner Ring (Blackgold-Grade) ×1]
[Quest Complete! Return to Archer Guild to submit!]
Daniel examined the two items.
[Elven Pendant (Blackgold-Grade / Accessory)]
Effect: Agility +100, Critical Damage +30%, All Arrows Pierce +1
Description: A masterpiece crafted by elven artisans, as light as the wind.
[Windrunner Ring (Blackgold-Grade / Accessory)]
Effect: Attack Speed +25%, Movement Speed +25%, Evasion +15%
Description: Wearing it, you become the embodiment of wind.
Seeing both were bound items, Daniel immediately equipped them.
His Agility rose from 1,255 to 1,355, Critical Damage jumped to 530%, and Attack Speed increased further!
Ah... satisfying.
He gave the ruined town one last glance before vanishing from sight.
Behind him, only the shattered altar and dissipating black mist remained.

[Rewards: Luck +20, Elven Pendant (Blackgold-Grade) ×1, Windrunner Ring (Blackgold-Grade) ×1]
[Quest Complete!
Return to Archer Guild to submit!]
Daniel examined the two items.
[Elven Pendant (Blackgold-Grade / Accessory)]
Effect: Agility +100, Critical Damage +30%, All Arrows Pierce +1
Description: A masterpiece crafted by elven artisans, as light as the wind.
[Windrunner Ring (Blackgold-Grade / Accessory)]
Effect: Attack Speed +25%, Movement Speed +25%, Evasion +15%
Description: Wearing it, you become the embodiment of wind.
Seeing both were bound items, Daniel immediately equipped them.
His Agility rose from 1,255 to 1,355, Critical Damage jumped to 530%, and Attack Speed increased further!
Ah... satisfying.
He gave the ruined town one last glance before vanishing from sight.
Behind him, only the shattered altar and dissipating black mist remained.

chapters.title: Chapter 23 -23-New SSS-Class Skill: Shattering Comet
paragraphs: Archer Guild.
Shadow Song stood in the guild hall, watching as Daniel’s figure materialized via teleportation.
"I didn’t expect you to complete the quest so quickly!"
"Piece of cake," Daniel replied as he submitted the quest items—the Dark Acolyte’s necklace and a shard of the altar.
Shadow Song accepted the items, eyes flickering with surprise.
"They were completely destroyed... what exactly did you do there?"
"Uh... it was raining heavily, and there was lightning too!"
Daniel scratched his nose.
Shadow Song studied him thoughtfully.
"After enduring that level of psychic assault, your mental state is surprisingly stable... very strange."
[Ding! Congratulations! You have completed the SSS‐rank Star Ascension Quest: Shadow of the Dark God.]
[Class Star Level: ★ → ★★]
[Max Level Cap unlocked: 70]
[Attribute Points +100 (freely assignable)]
[New Class Skill Unlocked: Shattering Comet]
[Shattering Comet (SSS‐Rank)]
Effect: Fired arrows split into multiple branching arrows, each dealing 200% damage with armor‐breaking effect.
Cooldown: 5 minutes
MP Cost: 1000
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
200% damage, and armor break?
Combined with Arrowstorm for clearing crowds, this skill was practically unstoppable.
He allocated all 100 points to Agility, bringing his four core attributes to 1,455!
A terrifying stat—each individual attribute rivaled that of a player over a hundred levels higher.
Extreme, yes—but he was aiming for full development.
It was clear just how powerful the Heart of Balance (supreme-grade) had been in amplifying him.
Along with Demon’s Whisper, Infinite Grail, and Black Dragon King’s Protection, all supreme-grade equipment contributed unmatched bonuses.
At this point, Daniel was virtually untouchable, even if surrounded by players.
At that moment, the system alert sounded.
[Ding! Excess experience detected in your EXP pool. Auto-leveling initiated...]
Golden light burst from Daniel, one wave after another.
The golden light flashed twenty times, illuminating the entire Archer Guild hall.
Nearby NPCs turned their heads; several players holding quest scrolls were dumbfounded, letting the scrolls drop without noticing.
Shadow Song stood to the side, eyes widening more and more.
When the light finally faded, Daniel opened his character panel.
[Current Level: 70 (Max Level)]
[Next Star Ascension Quest required to continue leveling.]
Shadow Song was silent for three seconds, then spoke slowly:
"How... much experience have you accumulated?"
Daniel thought for a moment.
"Overflowed from level 50, killed several bosses, cleared a map... before I knew it..."
"Before you knew it?"
Shadow Song’s mouth twitched in disbelief.
"Do you realize how long it normally takes a player to go from level 50 to 70?"
"At least a month! You did it in thirty seconds!"
Daniel smiled.
"Just got lucky."
Shadow Song took a deep breath, trying to calm herself.
"By the way, do you need to start the next Star Ascension Quest?"
"Not for now."
To continue leveling, he would need the next stage of Star Ascension Quests—but he suddenly remembered something he hadn’t done.
Players were already streaming into the main city, and his layout had to be finalized immediately.
Daniel stepped out of the Archer Guild, observing the bustling streets.
Players trained, ran quests, and cleared instances with fervor.
Some had just stepped out of the Starter Village portal, eyes wide at the splendor of Luminara.
Some grouped together, rushing outside the city, shouting, "Still need one healer!"
Some set up stalls by the roadside, hawking items cheaply—until fully armored city guards dragged them off for "education."
No one knew that three years later, this place would become a real battlefield.
No one knew threats from other worlds were approaching.
No one even realized the boundaries between game and reality were beginning to blur.
Daniel inhaled deeply.
There was still much to do:
Increase his power
Secure resources
Develop the human race’s overall strength
Monitor otherworldly movements
And prepare a real-world fortress...
[Ding! New gold coin received: +1 gold coin!]
[Ding! New gold coin received: +1 gold coin!]
[Ding! New gold coin received: +1 gold coin!]
Daniel opened his mailbox to a flood of notifications.
He checked the message logs:
[Player "Sword to the Sky" used Luminara portal, consumed 1 copper coin, triggered Millionfold Boost. You gained 1 gold coin.]
[Player "Nightingale" used Luminara portal, consumed 1 copper coin, triggered Millionfold Boost. You gained 1 gold coin.]
[Player "Rhine Watcher" used Luminara portal, consumed 1 copper coin, triggered Millionfold Boost. You gained 1 gold coin.]
[Player ...]
The notifications were countless—roughly several thousand.
Daniel realized that the thirty-seven portals he built in Luminara last night were now active.
[World Channel]
"Holy shit! Look at Luminara! These buildings are insane!"
"Quick, record a video for the forums! Gothic, Baroque, and Romanesque elements combined—it’s magical!"
"Unbelievable... these portals only cost 1 copper coin each? What’s the difference from free?!"
"Wait, 1 copper coin? Are you kidding? Our world #58 portals cost 1 silver coin each!"
"Exactly, and our main city only has one portal, and it’s ridiculously expensive!"
"No way, the players in world #616 must be hacking!"
Daniel smiled at the cheers in World Channel.
This was only the beginning.
He was about to close the messages and focus on business when he noticed a pile of unread emails.
Opening them, he saw:
[Ding! You have 99 trade mails pending!]
[Item: Money Bag (contains 10,000 gold coins) ×99, Status: Sold, awaiting your confirmation to deliver.]
Daniel slapped his forehead—almost forgot!
After successfully selling the first Money Bag last night, he had listed the remaining 99 with free purchase permissions at 1 copper coin each, noting cash transaction required.
He had expected it would take days, but they were all bought immediately.
He checked the transaction record:
[Sold Quantity: 99 Money Bags]
[Total Price: 99 copper coins]
Daniel opened his phone.
Bank notifications instantly poured in:
[Your account ending XXXX received a transfer of 4,900,000 dollars.]
In just seconds, nearly 5 million dollars had entered his account.
He quickly reviewed it, then pressed [One-Click Confirm Delivery].
[Ding! You sold 99 Money Bags for 99 copper coins, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[Received: 99 gold coins, 990,000,000,000 gold coins!]
[Ding! Transaction involves real-world currency, triggering Real-World Boost!]
[Real-World Boost: 4,950,000 dollars × 1,000,000 = 4,950,000,000,000 dollars!]
His phone vibrated wildly again.
This time, Daniel didn’t even look.
He silenced it and tossed it aside.
Money?
At this point, money had no meaning to him.
Billions or trillions—what’s the difference?
None.
His only goal now: get stronger, and kill that damn octopus Dark God!
Daniel inhaled deeply, focusing back on the game.
He activated God Speed.
The next second, he was already standing beside the main city central portal.
