chapters.title: Chapter 24 -24-Linking All Portals in the Nine Main Cities
paragraphs: Harold was leaning against a portal, hands fiddling with parts here and there.
Seeing Daniel suddenly appear, he quickly withdrew his hands and coughed.
"Cough cough cough... Can you walk normally or what?! You scared the hell out of me!"
Daniel didn’t waste words.
"Take me to the other eight main cities."
Harold froze. "Why?"
"To build portals."
Harold’s eyes nearly popped out, his wrench almost falling to the ground.
"You’re insane! You don’t mean... you want to build portals in all eight other main cities, do you? Do you know how much material that would cost?!"
"And those stingy administrators would never approve that kind of expense!"
Daniel said calmly, "I’ll cover the materials. The profits remain the same—20% for you, 10% for each main city."
Harold straightened immediately, his face full of righteous resolve.
"Let’s go! Right now!"
First stop: Galehold.
This main city was built on sheer cliffs, where fierce winds howled year-round. The buildings were low, sturdy, and made of stone.
The city lord, Robert Stormrider, a balding middle-aged man, sat in his office, troubled.
Recently, beastfolk had been causing problems at the border, and city defense funds were tight.
He looked at Harold with a mix of resignation and suspicion.
Not again... is he here to beg for money?
Harold was one of the three SSS-grade engineers specially employed by the nine main cities. His position was unusually authoritative.
Robert treated him with casual respect, but Galehold’s defenses were already strained. If the portals malfunctioned, he’d have to pay—willingly or not.
"Hehe, my lord, I bring you tremendous news today!"
"Go ahead. How much do you want?"
Robert didn’t even look at him.
"Hey! What are you talking about?" Harold said.
"I’ll just put it simply, old man. Want me to build a portal for you... for free?"
"No... wait, what? Free?"
The introduction went astonishingly smoothly.
After Harold’s explanation, Robert looked at Daniel, bewildered.
"Is... is this person insane?"
He whispered to Harold, "Harold, what’s going on? You’re one of the three SSS-grade engineers, yet you bring this kid to do... this? Is he your new apprentice?"
Harold chuckled without answering.
Daniel stepped forward calmly.
"I will personally provide all construction materials. After completion, Galehold will receive 10% of the profits."
Robert froze.
"You’re providing the materials yourself? And we only get 10%?"
"Yes."
Robert immediately nodded. "Build it! Build anywhere in the city!"
A joke—so long as he wasn’t paying for materials, they could build a thousand portals if they wanted.
This guy must have more money than he knows what to do with.
[Ding! Harold has issued you a special quest on behalf of the nine main city lords: Main Cities Hub Construction!]
[Quest Reward: ???]
Harold shot Daniel a mischievous wink.
"Don’t worry, Daniel. Since you’re building portals for the nine main cities, I won’t let you be shortchanged!"
"I’ll negotiate with each lord to get you a satisfactory reward!"
Harold patted Daniel on the shoulder.
"Much obliged!"
Daniel silently added Harold to his friendship list.
Soon, thanks to Harold’s introductions, all nine main city lords agreed to the portal constructions.
Daniel immediately began the build. Throughout, he combined his skills and experience, explaining every step to Harold.
From rune arrangements to energy conduit layouts, from foundation stone choices to spatial node positioning—he revealed every detail.
Harold’s eyes sparkled as he scribbled notes feverishly, muttering to himself.
Second stop: Pyrehaven.
The entire city lay at the foot of a volcano, the air thick with sulfur.
When building the portal, lava zones had to be avoided. Daniel flew over the area, selected the optimal location, and finished in ten minutes.
Third stop: Snowspire.
A frigid, icy land where breath froze instantly.
Harold shivered in the tavern, refusing to come out. Daniel braved the blizzard alone, completing three portals in half an hour.
Returning to the tavern, he found Harold surrounded—two gorgeous women pouring drink after drink into him.
"Tavern master, today’s bill for Lord Harold is 78,250 gold coins. As a VIP guest, you only need to pay 78,000 gold coins!"
"Ha! No problem, keep it all!"
Harold casually tossed a Money Bag.
The tavern staff squeezed it, a strange expression on his face.
"Lord Harold, this Money Bag only contains 20,000 gold coins. This... is a bit of a problem."
"What? A problem?" Harold flushed, looking embarrassed at Daniel.
"Well, Daniel..."
Daniel rolled his eyes but stepped forward.
"Fine, I’ll cover it."
[Ding! Current friendship with NPC Harold has increased to Best Friend!]
Daniel shook his head.
Old man only raises friendship when he benefits, huh?
In a single day, Daniel and Harold traveled to the eight main cities.
At least thirty portals were built in each city—covering major commercial zones, instance entrances, quest halls, and guild districts.
Money flowed like water, yet Daniel didn’t bat an eye. Money was the least of his concerns now.
By seven o’clock that evening, the portal network in the final main city, Skyhold, was completed.
Skyhold floated above the clouds, all-white buildings shimmering in mist, resembling a divine realm.
The moment the final portal was built, all portals activated simultaneously, forming a network linking all nine cities. A beam of light shot skyward.
[Ding! Congratulations! You have completed the special quest: "Nine Main Cities Portal Network Construction"]
[Quest Rating: SSS]
[Rewards: 500,000 gold coins, 5 Legendary Material Boxes, Military Merit +1000, Contribution Points +4000]
[Honorary Title jointly awarded by the nine main cities: Pioneer of Creation!]
[Pioneer of Creation (Unique Title)]: Luck +20, Contribution Points +5000, 20% discount for buying or selling with all main city NPCs.
Harold’s face flushed with excitement.
"Done! I didn’t expect it to be completed so fast!"
At the same time, a system notification rang throughout the Stellar World:
[Ding! Global Announcement!!!]
[Player "Faustus" has completed the nine main cities portal network, becoming the first player to link all nine main cities!]
[As the first to achieve this feat, his name will forever be engraved on the portal monuments of the nine main cities!]
The golden announcement flashed three times before every player, each character shimmering with blinding golden light.

chapters.title: Chapter 25 -25-Progress Far Ahead, Real-World Guilds Stunned
paragraphs: [World Channel]
"The portal network across the nine main cities?? Does that mean he built the portals??"
"No way... we’re still struggling in Starter Village, and he’s already doing infrastructure?"
"Faustus is the project manager of this game, right?"
"Project manager? Does he have that authority? He’s basically the boss!"
"I give up... I seriously give up. Is this guy a GM? If so, can he drop some perks?"
"Hey, Faustus, need any trinkets? The clingy kind..."
"I suspect he’s an alien vacationing on Earth."
"Alien: Not our fault, we’re not this insane."
Crimson Soul stood beside the Luminara portal, staring at the dreamlike main city before her, her expression complicated.
She had just reached level 15 and arrived via portal with the crowd.
She hadn’t even gotten a proper look at the city’s grandeur before this server-wide announcement hit.
"Established a portal network across all nine main cities..."
She muttered to herself, looking up at the sky.
This is absurd.
How far has this game god gone?
She clenched her fists.
No, she had to level up fast!
She had a strong premonition—a massive wave of new players would soon flood the game.
And that man was already far ahead of everyone.
"I must convince my family to focus on Stellar as soon as possible. This is definitely more than just a game!"
[Rhine Guild · Core Meeting Room]
In the encrypted channel, projections of a dozen figures sat around a round table.
Guildmaster Rhine Watcher sat at the head, a screen in front of him repeatedly playing recordings of Daniel building portals.
The footage had been captured by other players in the main city.
"Let’s hear your thoughts," his voice low and serious.
Vice President North Wind spoke first:
"Without a doubt, all 37 portals in Luminara were built by him."
"Today he completed the remaining eight main cities, at least 30 portals in each. This efficiency... no normal player could achieve it."
"So you’re saying he’s a GM?" someone asked.
"GMs don’t trigger server-wide announcements."
Rhine Watcher shook his head.
"We’ve checked the forums. No internal accounts or staff records. All posts analyzing him are from regular players."
After a few seconds of silence, Prospector, sitting in the corner, spoke slowly.
"Have you considered another possibility?"
Everyone turned to him.
Compared to the Watcher, Prospector was the true mastermind of Rhine Guild, one of the top-tier figures of Blue Star.
He rarely spoke, but when he did, his words often determined the final decision.
"This game..." he paused, eyes deep, "might be a real-world environment."
"Could it be?"
Everyone exchanged glances, recalling recent heated forum discussions.
Some players had reportedly contacted players from other worlds—their Starter Village IDs didn’t match theirs.
"Yes, the reports about contacting other-world players are true!"
"I’ve also had people check—the IP addresses of those posts are untraceable, and the timestamps are strange."
The meeting room fell silent.
After a long moment, Rhine Watcher asked solemnly:
"What do you think Faustus... has to do with this?"
Prospector shook his head, then nodded slightly.
"I don’t know."
"But his leveling speed and understanding of this game far exceed normal boundaries. Either he has insider information we don’t know, or..."
He didn’t finish the sentence, but everyone understood.
Either he’s not a normal player.
"Keep engaging him," Prospector concluded.
"On favorable terms. You can’t afford to offend someone like this—at least superficially, keep appearances!"
[Ragnarok Guild · Voice Channel]
Compared to Rhine Guild’s seriousness, Ragnarok was far more chaotic.
"Hahaha! Did you guys see World Channel? Someone said Faustus is his dad!"
"Pfft, just a player, yet people worship him now. He’s only completed a few hidden tasks we haven’t found yet. Wait, I’ll surpass him in no time!"
"You? You haven’t even left Starter Village."
"Shut up!"
Guildmaster Duskfang cleared his throat to suppress the chatter.
"Let’s get serious. What do you think about Faustus?"
"Pervert."
Someone summed up succinctly.
"Cut the nonsense, give me useful info."
An analyst handed over a report:
"We analyzed all public data on Faustus. His leveling speed is over 100 times that of a normal player."
"His gear is at least two tiers above current players. His accumulated wealth is preliminarily estimated at over a million gold coins."
Duskfang narrowed his eyes.
"You’re saying he’s cheating?"
"Not necessarily," another analyst said.
"This game has no traceable network endpoints; we don’t know where the servers are. Even if he wanted to cheat, he couldn’t do it."
"So how is he achieving this?"
No one had an answer.
Duskfang fell silent for a moment, then smiled.
"Interesting... just like this game world, mysterious as hell!"
He stood, pacing in the virtual meeting room.
"Keep observing him."
"Also, prepare an invitation—invite him to join our guild."
"Anything money can solve... is nothing!"
He paused, a glint of coldness in his eyes.
"If money can’t solve it... then we’ll use other means."
[Stormbound Guild · Encrypted Channel]
Compared to other guilds’ caution, Stormbound Guild’s discussion was far more direct.
Guildmaster Vantheon, gold rings on his fingers, a chain of gold around his neck, exuded a nouveau-riche arrogance.
A subordinate spoke cautiously:
"Guildmaster, this person is not ordinary..."
"Not ordinary?" Vantheon interrupted, disdainful.
"I’ve seen plenty of ’not ordinary’ people. And the outcome?"
"They either became our servants or disappeared. A lone wolf, lucky enough to pick up some gear, thinking he’s special?"
Vantheon stood, a sharp gleam in his eyes.
"Send him a message—demand he transfer portal profits to us. We, Stormbound Guild, will ensure his safety in the main cities. Otherwise..."
"Guildmaster, isn’t that too direct? Other guilds are trying to court him."
"Direct? Do we, in the Ganges server, need to be polite to a solo player?"
Vantheon sneered.
His subordinate didn’t dare speak further, sending the message silently.
Seconds later, Vantheon’s expression changed.
"Guildmaster... he blocked me."
Vantheon froze, then erupted in fury.
"Good! Excellent!"
He sent another message in the guild channel:
[Attention all Stormbound Guild members: From today, Faustus is our enemy! Share coordinates immediately if encountered in the field! Whoever kills him will receive a 1,000,000 dollar reward!]
The channel erupted in cheers, though some muttered privately:
"Guild master’s lost it? That’s a god-level player who can solo Blackgold-grade BOSSes. Even sending all of Stormbound after him, they might not win..."

chapters.title: Chapter 26 -26-Buying All Real Estate in the Nine Main Cities
paragraphs: Beside the Skyhold portal.
Daniel scrolled through a string of messages in the private chat channel.
Rhine Guild’s probing messages? Ignored.
Ragnarok’s friendly overtures? Ignored.
As for the staggering offer from the Morgan Consortium, he chuckled.
For the Morgans, money was never an issue.
This attitude matched his current mindset perfectly. Without the system, he probably would have been buried under all that wealth and confused!
As for Stormbound Guild’s threats...
He glanced at the message, a faint smile curling on his lips.
"A bunch of idiots," he muttered softly, then blocked them.
Threaten him?
He had seen plenty of this kind of trash in his past life.
Those who screamed the loudest usually died the fastest.
Now, every major guild had begun to notice him, study him, and plan against him...
But he had been mentally prepared for this.
And at his current level, he feared no threat. It wouldn’t be long before these guilds realized exactly how formidable he was.
"Snap!"
At that moment, Harold grabbed Daniel’s arm, his face red with excitement.
"I get it! I finally get it!!"
Daniel felt dizzy from the shaking.
"What do you get?" he asked.
Harold’s eyes glimmered, his face flushed and neck thick, speaking incoherently.
"I’ve been stuck at SSS rank for twenty years and never understood what I was missing!"
"Watching you build so many portals today, I finally understand!"
He released Daniel’s arm, spinning excitedly in place.
"I’ve been building with an engineer’s mindset—pursuing perfection, stability, and absolute safety."
"But you use the Creator’s mindset! You don’t think about how to build a portal—you think about what kind of portal I want, and build that!"
He stopped abruptly, staring Daniel down.
"This is what I was missing!"
He solemnly took a badge from his chest and handed it to Daniel.
His hands trembled slightly, as if entrusting something precious.
[Received: Level 2 Honor Medal (Universal in Human Cities)]
"This is for you! From now on, in all human territories, you’re one of us!"
Daniel accepted the medal, barely speaking, when Harold grabbed his shoulder again.
"I have business to attend to. I’ll try my promotion now!"
"When I succeed, I’ll definitely buy you a drink. You don’t know... the girls in Snowspire are wild, hehe!"
With that, Harold disappeared in a flash.
Daniel smiled at the medal in his hand.
No wonder Harold had been studying hard in the eight main cities... until Snowspire, where he ran straight to the tavern!
He stowed the medal and turned toward Skyhold’s Commercial Management Office.
There was one important task left.
Skyhold Commercial Management Office was located beside the Lord’s Mansion, a building entirely of white jade.
The sunset bathed the building in warm golden light, making it breathtakingly beautiful.
Two guards in ornate armor stood at the entrance, holding long halberds, eyes unwavering.
Daniel stepped inside. The interior was spacious and bright, with marble floors and exquisite oil paintings on the walls.
At the front desk stood a professional attendant, smiling politely.
"Honored hero, how may I assist you?"
"I want to buy real estate."
The attendant nodded, smiling.
"Very well... which plot are you interested in? I can recommend the best locations..."
"All of them."
The attendant’s smile froze.
"All available commercial properties in Skyhold? You want them all?"
The quill in the attendant’s hand fell to the desk, mouth forming an O, frozen for three seconds before reacting.
"Please... wait, I need to report this to my superiors..."
A cool, clear voice spoke from behind.
"Honored hero, are you serious?"
Daniel turned.
A woman in a deep blue gown stood at the doorway. Her silver hair fell to her waist, her features delicate as a work of art.
Her eyes were a rare pale violet, assessing Daniel carefully.
Two assistants stood behind her, faces full of respect.
[Skyhold Chief of Commercial Management · Alicia (Epic-grade NPC)]
Daniel nodded. "Of course."
Alicia approached, scanning him from head to toe.
"Pioneer of Creation, Honorary Citizen of Nine Cities, Apprentice Merit Medal holder... and a Level 2 Honor Medal!"
As she recited his titles, her eyes shifted slightly at the last one.
"You indeed have the qualification and authority to make this purchase."
She paused, taking the documents from the attendant and quickly reviewing them.
"Skyhold has 57 vacant commercial properties, spread across commercial streets, residential areas, and near instance entrances. The total cost..."
She looked up directly at Daniel.
"Exceeds 10 billion gold coins. Are you sure?"
Daniel didn’t hesitate, opening the transaction interface to transfer the funds.
[Transferred to Skyhold Official Account: 10,000,000,000 gold coins!]
A stream of zeros flashed across the screen, taking several moments to fully display.
Alicia’s pupils contracted slightly at the number.
She was silent for a few seconds, then spoke softly:
"Please wait while I report to the Lord..."
She turned and walked away, her high heels clicking crisply on the marble floor.
Daniel leisurely moved to the wall, admiring the paintings.
One depicted Skyhold’s initial construction—scaffolds floating in the clouds, craftsmen working midair—fascinating to observe.
Five minutes later, Alicia returned.
"The Lord has approved."
She handed Daniel a thick stack of contracts, each stamped with the Lord’s official seal.
"All 57 properties are now yours."
[Received: Skyhold Real Estate Contracts ×57!]
Daniel stowed the contracts in his backpack and turned to leave.
Alicia asked suddenly:
"Why are you buying so much property?"
Daniel looked at her.
Why? Monopoly, of course.
Monopoly sounded simple, but required a full chain to execute.
He moved to the window, pointing to the bustling commercial street below.
A few players wandered the streets; most shops were empty, with "For Sale" signs.
"How many adventurers are in Skyhold currently?"
Alicia considered. "About a thousand, I’d say."
"And in a month... two months?"
Alicia said nothing.
Daniel continued:
"When most adventurers reach level 30–40, the main city will become the true core area."
"Daily traffic will be hundreds or thousands of times higher than now. What will they need? Equipment, potions, materials, all sorts of supplies."
He turned to Alicia.
"All those needs will be fulfilled through shops, and the shops accessible to adventurers are exactly what I just bought."
Alicia thought for a moment.
"So you intend to..."
"Monopolize the trade channels among adventurers."

chapters.title: Chapter 27 -27-Fallen Mountain God
paragraphs: Daniel spoke calmly.
He deliberately emphasized the key point: between adventurers.

The NPC shops in the nine main cities would remain unaffected. Official channels—main city shops, guild shops, and military supply offices—would continue operating normally, prices set by the system, untouchable by anyone.
But the real estate he purchased was different.
These were commercial properties adventurers could freely operate.
Once adventurers rented or bought these shops, they could open their own stores, sell the equipment, materials, or potions they obtained, set their own prices, and keep the profits.
This was Daniel’s true goal.
"Adventurers want to open a shop? They’ll have to rent or buy the stores I own," he said.
Seeing Alicia’s puzzled look, he continued:
"If adventurers want to buy something, aside from the main city shops, they’ll have to come to the stores I operate."
"My prices are lower, and the stock comes from adventurers themselves. Those who don’t want to open shops but want to liquidate their goods—those goods will eventually flow into these stores."
Alicia’s eyes widened slightly.
"So what you want to control is..."
"The capillaries of the adventurer economy," Daniel said.
"Don’t worry," he added. "I won’t touch what I shouldn’t. I won’t take a cent from main city profits. I only control the portion between adventurers."
Unless he achieved certain merits or earned a noble title, acquiring NPC-held properties would be impossible.
He picked up a contract on the table, scanning the location details.
Alicia nodded, then asked suddenly:
"How will you set the pricing? If the rent is too high, many adventurers won’t be able to afford it."
Daniel shook his head.
"The rent won’t be high—at least for ordinary adventurers."
He paused, eyes cooling slightly.
"But for the big guilds, it’s a different story."
Alicia’s eyes widened, then she understood.
"You mean..."
"They’re rich, aren’t they? Big wallets, big egos?"
Daniel’s lips curved in a small smile.
"Want to open a guild shop in the main city?"
"Fine—rent is ten times that of a regular adventurer. Want to monopolize a specific material? Sure—first check with me if I approve the pricing."
What he didn’t say:
In his previous life, the big guilds had used wealth and influence to dominate the adventurer economy.
Solo players who wanted to sell something valuable had to undercut themselves.
And when solo players wanted to buy good items, the guilds skimmed them dry.
This time, he would let those guilds experience being throttled instead.
Alicia looked at Daniel, her expression complicated.
Honestly, if Daniel hadn’t had the Level 2 Honor Medal, she wouldn’t have approved this deal.
Even though the Lord had agreed, she still had the right to reject it.
After a moment of silence, she spoke:
"Actually, what you’re doing benefits most adventurers."
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
"Oh?"
"If you really keep rent low, ordinary adventurers will have the chance to open stores."
"Big guilds monopolized resources for too long. Ordinary adventurers had to sell good items cheaply."
"Now they can open their own stores, set their own prices, and keep their profits."
Daniel nodded slightly.
That was exactly his intention.
Monopoly could be used for personal gain, or for balance.
In his previous life, he had seen too many players quit the game due to unequal resource distribution. He had seen potential solo players forced into dead ends by big guilds.
This time, with the system in hand, he wanted to try a different approach.
Give ordinary adventurers more opportunities, prevent guilds from having total control.
After all, when a disaster arrives, the ones who step up will be every single player.

"But..." Alicia said after a pause, "the nine main cities cover an enormous area. Even if you control adventurer resources in Skyhold, with the other eight cities regulating theirs, it will be difficult to achieve exactly what you intend."
Daniel smiled calmly.
"Not hard at all."
"I’ve bought all nine main cities. Any adventurer wanting to open a shop in a main city has to go through me."
"What!"
Alicia gasped. All nine main cities... bought?
What kind of scale is this?
The total assets must be at least ten trillion gold coins!
Skyhold’s annual revenue couldn’t even reach a fraction of that. This adventurer is only level 70—where did he get this kind of capital?!
If he really has this level of backing, any major guild wanting a foothold in the main cities will have to play by his rules.
And as Skyhold’s Chief of Commercial Management, Alicia knew exactly what this meant for a main city.
If Daniel really builds the system he described, it would greatly stabilize and promote economic growth.
More transactions would happen here, more taxes flowing into the Lord’s Treasury, and the more prosperous the city, the greater the benefit.
It’s a win-win scenario.
Of course, the biggest winner is the man himself.
"You..." Alicia opened her mouth, unsure what to say.
Daniel stowed the contracts and turned to leave.
At the door, he paused.
"By the way, beautiful lady, if anyone from Doom Guild comes to rent a shop, give them a friendly discount, okay?"
Alicia paused, then a slight smile appeared.
"Of course!"
Daniel nodded and disappeared outside.
Next, he would need to move quickly through the remaining eight main cities, repeating the same process.

Once he controlled all adventurer-run shops in all nine main cities, he could supply 616 World Line players with reasonably priced goods, supporting solo players while using economic means to counterbalance big guilds.
Of course, he’d also earn a little profit along the way—it was only natural.
Night fell, and Skyhold’s lights gradually turned on.
Daniel’s figure flashed between one main city and another, one contract after another falling into his backpack.
His commercial empire was taking root.
Luminara, Archer Guild.
Daniel walked into the guild hall once more.
He headed straight to the hidden instructor, Shadow Song, at the very back.
"Hello, I’m here to accept the Star Ascension Quest."
Shadow Song looked at him, a hint of curiosity in her eyes.
"Pioneer of Creation, Honorary Citizen of Nine Cities... you’ve accomplished quite a lot today."
Daniel smiled.
"Not much, just handled it while passing by."
Shadow Song’s mouth twitched.
"’Passing by’? You call this passing by?"
She shook her head and handed him a scroll.
[Star Ascension Quest: Fallen Mountain God (SSS-Rank)]

[Quest Description: The Northern Mountains’ Broken Spine Range produces a variety of rare herbs, vital for alchemists and gatherers in the nine main cities. Recently, the Mountain God has gone berserk, annihilating any life entering the mountains. The most capable hero is required to subdue the Fallen Mountain God and restore the herb-producing region.]
[Quest Objective: Defeat the Fallen Mountain God and uncover the root cause of its corruption (LV75 Blackgold-grade BOSS)]
[Quest Rewards: Class Star Level +1, Attribute Points +150, Unlock a new class skill!]
Daniel read the quest description, his brows furrowing involuntarily.

sentences.text: Daniel spoke calmly.
He deliberately emphasized the key point: between adventurers.
The NPC shops in the nine main cities would remain unaffected.
Official channels—main city shops, guild shops, and military supply offices—would continue operating normally, prices set by the system, untouchable by anyone.
But the real estate he purchased was different.
These were commercial properties adventurers could freely operate.
Once adventurers rented or bought these shops, they could open their own stores, sell the equipment, materials, or potions they obtained, set their own prices, and keep the profits.
This was Daniel’s true goal.
"Adventurers want to open a shop?
They’ll have to rent or buy the stores I own," he said.
Seeing Alicia’s puzzled look, he continued:
"If adventurers want to buy something, aside from the main city shops, they’ll have to come to the stores I operate."
"My prices are lower, and the stock comes from adventurers themselves.
Those who don’t want to open shops but want to liquidate their goods—those goods will eventually flow into these stores."
Alicia’s eyes widened slightly.
"So what you want to control is..."
"The capillaries of the adventurer economy," Daniel said.
"Don’t worry," he added.
"I won’t touch what I shouldn’t.
I won’t take a cent from main city profits.
I only control the portion between adventurers."
Unless he achieved certain merits or earned a noble title, acquiring NPC-held properties would be impossible.
He picked up a contract on the table, scanning the location details.
Alicia nodded, then asked suddenly:
"How will you set the pricing?
If the rent is too high, many adventurers won’t be able to afford it."
Daniel shook his head.
"The rent won’t be high—at least for ordinary adventurers."
He paused, eyes cooling slightly.
"But for the big guilds, it’s a different story."
Alicia’s eyes widened, then she understood.
"You mean..."
"They’re rich, aren’t they?
Big wallets, big egos?"
Daniel’s lips curved in a small smile.
"Want to open a guild shop in the main city?"
"Fine—rent is ten times that of a regular adventurer.
Want to monopolize a specific material?
Sure—first check with me if I approve the pricing."
What he didn’t say:
In his previous life, the big guilds had used wealth and influence to dominate the adventurer economy.
Solo players who wanted to sell something valuable had to undercut themselves.
And when solo players wanted to buy good items, the guilds skimmed them dry.
This time, he would let those guilds experience being throttled instead.
Alicia looked at Daniel, her expression complicated.
Honestly, if Daniel hadn’t had the Level 2 Honor Medal, she wouldn’t have approved this deal.
Even though the Lord had agreed, she still had the right to reject it.
After a moment of silence, she spoke:
"Actually, what you’re doing benefits most adventurers."
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
"Oh?"
"If you really keep rent low, ordinary adventurers will have the chance to open stores."
"Big guilds monopolized resources for too long.
Ordinary adventurers had to sell good items cheaply."
"Now they can open their own stores, set their own prices, and keep their profits."
Daniel nodded slightly.
That was exactly his intention.
Monopoly could be used for personal gain, or for balance.
In his previous life, he had seen too many players quit the game due to unequal resource distribution.
He had seen potential solo players forced into dead ends by big guilds.
This time, with the system in hand, he wanted to try a different approach.
Give ordinary adventurers more opportunities, prevent guilds from having total control.
After all, when a disaster arrives, the ones who step up will be every single player.
"But..." Alicia said after a pause, "the nine main cities cover an enormous area.
Even if you control adventurer resources in Skyhold, with the other eight cities regulating theirs, it will be difficult to achieve exactly what you intend."
Daniel smiled calmly.
"Not hard at all."
"I’ve bought all nine main cities.
Any adventurer wanting to open a shop in a main city has to go through me."
"What!"
Alicia gasped.
All nine main cities... bought?
What kind of scale is this?
The total assets must be at least ten trillion gold coins!
Skyhold’s annual revenue couldn’t even reach a fraction of that.
This adventurer is only level 70—where did he get this kind of capital?!
If he really has this level of backing, any major guild wanting a foothold in the main cities will have to play by his rules.
And as Skyhold’s Chief of Commercial Management, Alicia knew exactly what this meant for a main city.
If Daniel really builds the system he described, it would greatly stabilize and promote economic growth.
More transactions would happen here, more taxes flowing into the Lord’s Treasury, and the more prosperous the city, the greater the benefit.
It’s a win-win scenario.
Of course, the biggest winner is the man himself.
"You..." Alicia opened her mouth, unsure what to say.
Daniel stowed the contracts and turned to leave.
At the door, he paused.
"By the way, beautiful lady, if anyone from Doom Guild comes to rent a shop, give them a friendly discount, okay?"
Alicia paused, then a slight smile appeared.
"Of course!"
Daniel nodded and disappeared outside.
Next, he would need to move quickly through the remaining eight main cities, repeating the same process.

Once he controlled all adventurer-run shops in all nine main cities, he could supply 616 World Line players with reasonably priced goods, supporting solo players while using economic means to counterbalance big guilds.
Of course, he’d also earn a little profit along the way—it was only natural.
Night fell, and Skyhold’s lights gradually turned on.
Daniel’s figure flashed between one main city and another, one contract after another falling into his backpack.
His commercial empire was taking root.
Luminara, Archer Guild.
Daniel walked into the guild hall once more.
He headed straight to the hidden instructor, Shadow Song, at the very back.
"Hello, I’m here to accept the Star Ascension Quest."
Shadow Song looked at him, a hint of curiosity in her eyes.
"Pioneer of Creation, Honorary Citizen of Nine Cities... you’ve accomplished quite a lot today."
Daniel smiled.
"Not much, just handled it while passing by."
Shadow Song’s mouth twitched.
"’Passing by’?
You call this passing by?"
She shook her head and handed him a scroll.
[Star Ascension Quest: Fallen Mountain God (SSS-Rank)]
[Quest Description: The Northern Mountains’ Broken Spine Range produces a variety of rare herbs, vital for alchemists and gatherers in the nine main cities.
Recently, the Mountain God has gone berserk, annihilating any life entering the mountains.
The most capable hero is required to subdue the Fallen Mountain God and restore the herb-producing region.]
[Quest Objective: Defeat the Fallen Mountain God and uncover the root cause of its corruption (LV75 Blackgold-grade BOSS)]
[Quest Rewards: Class Star Level +1, Attribute Points +150, Unlock a new class skill!]
Daniel read the quest description, his brows furrowing involuntarily.

chapters.title: Chapter 28 -28-SSS Skills: Aetherlance
paragraphs: Mountain God?
In his previous lives, Daniel had rarely encountered such creatures.
They were scarce, nearly extinct, and usually gentle, never involving themselves in interspecies conflicts.
These special beings had mountain-like bodies, with absurdly high defenses. No one bothered them.
So why had it suddenly gone berserk?
Suppressing his doubt, he turned to Shadow Song.
"By the way, do you have any suitable skill recommendations?"
Shadow Song glanced at him and flipped through a skill book.
"This quest is actually cross-class. As an archer, taking it is a bit of a disadvantage. This might help you."
[Eagle Pierce (A-Rank)]
Effect: Fires a high-penetration arrow that ignores 30% of target’s defense and resistances.
Cooldown: 1 minute
Class Restriction: Special archer class
Price: 10 gold coins
Daniel’s eyes lit up. He immediately purchased it.
He then opened the guild warehouse and sold the skill book to his own guild.
[Ding! You sold item to Doom Guild: Eagle Pierce Skill Book (A-Rank), 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[Sold item is skill book type; player selects Quality Boost!]
[Congratulations! You received 1 gold coin and obtained skill book: Aetherlance (SSS-Rank)]
[Aetherlance (SSS-Rank)]
Effect: Fires an arrow imbued with absolute penetration power. Ignores all defenses, shields, and damage mitigation, dealing 1000% damage to the target. Deals double damage to large creatures!
Cooldown: 1 minute
MP Cost: 2000
Daniel’s lips curved slightly.
Ignores all defenses and shields!
This skill might be invaluable for the upcoming quest.
And 1000% damage was no joke. Double damage against large creatures made it perfect for the Mountain God.
He learned the skill immediately and then crushed the quest scroll.
A brilliant light enveloped him.
When the world came into focus, Daniel was already at the foot of a towering mountain.
The sky was gray, clouds pressing low as if ready to collapse.
The entire mountain was shrouded in an eerie mist, faintly gray, flowing as if alive.
Animal bones littered the ground, some fresh with scraps of meat.
At the foot of the mountain stood a stone tablet, inscribed in blood-red letters:
[Trespassers Die!]
Daniel glanced at it casually and stepped into the mountain.
After only a few steps, the ground trembled.
Massive boulders began to roll, snapping together with a series of clicks, as if an invisible hand were assembling blocks.
Debris scattered, dust flying. Soon, tall stone figures began to rise!
They stood over three meters tall, bodies of rough stone, thick limbs, no facial features, only a faintly glowing crystal core in their chest.
[Mountain God’s Minion · Stone Golem · LV70 (Iron-grade Monster)]
The moment they fully formed, nearly a hundred stone golems charged at Daniel!
The ground shook with their roar, even trembling beneath his feet.
Daniel didn’t hold back. He raised his bow and fired.
Shattering Comet!
A streak of light shot into the sky, suddenly splitting into dozens of arrows trailing golden flames, raining down like a meteor shower.
Boom!
Arrows rained across the field, blasting stone golems apart.
Some had arms shattered, some had chests blown open, others disintegrated completely.
[Ding! You killed Stone Golem ×26! Gained 579,494 XP...]
"Indeed, Shattering Comet stacks with explosion effects..."
Although killing these stone men wasn’t difficult, Daniel noticed something.
These creatures were purely rock; explosions did reduced damage.
Sometimes two arrows were needed to destroy one.
Then, an idea came to him.
What if he combined Shattering Comet with Arrowstorm?
Arrowstorm covered a wide area, 200% damage per arrow with explosions.
Shattering Comet split into multiple arrows, wider coverage but slightly lower single-arrow damage.
Stacking the two effects onto one arrow—what would happen?
He decided to try.
Another wave of stone golems approached, footsteps shaking the mountain.
Daniel inhaled deeply and drew his bow.
He released!
The arrow soared, trailing interwoven golden and blue flames, climbing to the clouds.
At its peak, it halted.
Swish swish swish!!!
The arrow split into dozens of streams of light.
But unlike a normal Shattering Comet, each stream exploded again into palm-sized golden sparks.
The sparks densely filled the sky, like a shower of falling stars.
Then they began to descend.
Swoosh swoosh swoosh swoosh swoosh—
Boom boom boom boom boom!!!
Explosions roared almost simultaneously, the entire hillside engulfed in golden fire.
Like a cluster-bomb strike, nothing survived in its path.
Golems charging forward were instantly swallowed by the inferno.
The explosion happened in just an instant.
When the smoke cleared, not a single stone golem remained.
Only shattered rocks and smoking craters covered the slope, dense like the lunar surface.
[Ding! You killed Stone Golem ×154! Gained 3,379,494 XP...]
Daniel stared, momentarily stunned.
The power...
Although each arrow’s damage was lower than Arrowstorm, roughly 150%, the coverage was enormous, nearly unavoidable.
That previous wave covered at least 200 meters, wiping out over 150 golems.
And the best part—MP consumption.
Arrowstorm: 1000 MP. Shattering Comet: 1000 MP. But that single arrow only consumed 1500 MP!
Effectively, he expended 1.5x MP to achieve the combined effect of two skills. Damage was slightly lower, but range doubled!
Insufficient firepower?
No problem—he had overwhelming numbers.
Daniel grinned wildly.
A single archer equaled an entire artillery regiment!
He advanced further up the mountain.
The higher he climbed, the thicker the mist, reducing visibility.
Stone golems became rarer, but they evolved: some carried shields, some hurled stones, and two even merged into larger forms.
Still, none of them posed a threat—one arrow often cleared an entire ridge!
This was the power of a humanoid artillery corps!
Half an hour later, Daniel reached mid-mountain.
Then he froze.
The sight before him made his pupils constrict.
It was a mountain... no, the entire mountain was the BOSS!
A colossal, hundred-meter-tall mountain creature, its body fused with rock and soil, blending with the mountain range itself.
A faint human-like face could be seen at the summit: two massive caves for eyes, a deep fissure for a mouth.
Every breath made the mountain itself rise and fall slightly.
[Fallen Mountain God · LV75 (Blackgold-grade BOSS)]
Daniel stood at its base, tiny as an ant.
He could even see the patterns on its rocky skin.
Traces left over countless years—the history of the entire mountain.
And now, within those patterns, a faint, sinister black glow pulsed.

chapters.title: Chapter 29 -29-Corrupted Angel
paragraphs: The Mountain God seemed to sense his presence.
The blurred face drooped slightly, its massive "eyes" fixed on him.
Then, it slowly raised a foot.
A foot composed of the entire mountain itself—the toes alone were the size of buildings.
Boom!!!
The entire ground shook violently!
The spot where Daniel had just stood was crushed into a ten-meter-wide crater, debris flying, dust rising in clouds.
Daniel landed on a massive rock fifty meters away.
He immediately raised his hand and fired.
Explosive Arrow!
The arrow struck the Mountain God’s leg, only creating a small dent. Its HP barely changed.
Daniel twitched.
A thousand damage—against the Mountain God’s absurdly massive HP, probably less than 0.01%.
But the Mountain God was enraged by even that single arrow.
"Damn insect!"
"Die for me!"
It let out a deep roar, a sound resonating from deep within the mountain itself, shaking hearts with fear.
Then it raised its massive hands and slammed them into the ground!
Boom!!!
A shockwave radiated outward from its impact. The ground cracked, boulders flew.
Daniel was thrown into the air, somersaulting before stabilizing. He lost 800 HP.
Regaining his stance, his eyes cooled.
He inhaled deeply and drew his silver bow to full draw.
Aetherlance!
Golden light spread along the bow, up his arms, and over his body. In the blink of an eye, Daniel was like a blazing golden torch.
As the bowstring reached its limit, a massive golden spear formed on the bow, its tip emitting a blinding glow.
Bang!
The golden spear tore through the sky, leaving a trail of golden light, and pierced straight into the Mountain God’s chest!
Boom—!
The Mountain God staggered.
Focusing, Daniel saw a door-sized hole blown open in its chest, stones raining down, golden light spilling from the cavity.
The red critical hit indicator flashed—Mountain God’s HP visibly dropped.
Daniel’s eyes brightened.
This skill packs some serious punch!
Daniel used God Speed to dodge the Mountain God’s furious attacks while waiting for Aetherlance to cool down.
Meanwhile, countless explosive arrow volleys pounded the Mountain God, dislodging rocks in showers.
A minute later, he fired another Aetherlance.
Another minute later, a third.
After three shots, the Mountain God’s HP dropped by one-third.
But it had entered a full berserk state.
The Mountain God roared to the sky, the entire mountain trembling violently.
Boulders cascaded from the peak, crashing down, forming craters in the terrain.
It raised its hands again and slammed down—
This time, it wasn’t a mere shockwave. It was an actual landslide.
Countless fissures cracked the earth, plunging into bottomless depths. One misstep and you would fall in.
Daniel activated God Speed, weaving through falling rocks, jumping along fissure edges.
Several times, he narrowly avoided being crushed.
At an opening, he fired another Aetherlance directly at the core!
Boom!
The Mountain God’s chest exploded, forming another massive cavity, golden light pouring out.
After this hit, its HP fell to roughly one-third!
Daniel’s eyes narrowed—was this a weak-point critical hit?
He had heard that Mountain Gods were incredibly difficult to kill.
But if you could locate their weak point, they became far easier to defeat.
Of course, the weak point was also the most heavily fortified area!
But Daniel’s Aetherlance ignored defenses and shields.
Cracks spread across the Mountain God’s body, black light intensifying.
Without hesitation, Daniel seized the Mountain God’s moment of rage and fired Aetherlance again into its chest cavity!
Boom!
HP dropped to zero.
The Mountain God’s enormous body began to collapse, dust billowing everywhere.
The entire mountain disintegrated with deafening crashes.
[Ding! You have slain Fallen Mountain God (Blackgold-grade BOSS)]
[Rewards: Mountain God Essence ×1, Earth Armguards (Blackgold-grade), Boulder Shield (Blackgold-grade), 500 gold coins, Contribution Points +100, 2,569,000 XP...]
Daniel stared at the door-sized hole in the Mountain God’s chest—the mark left by Aetherlance.
Inside lay the quest item: Heart of Mountain.
But as he gazed at the Mountain God’s immense body, a sense of awe struck him.
Despite its size, this was merely a young Mountain God.
He had witnessed, centuries later on the endgame battlefield, Mountain Gods over ten thousand meters tall.
One punch could tear the ground apart, and even the most powerful skills hitting them were like scratching an itch.
This Mountain God had slept for countless years, awakening only due to the Elven Queen’s summons to confront the Dark God.
The Mountain God race also went by another name—the Children of the Earth.
They were the closest offspring of the land itself, all Strength tied to the world, lacking souls.
Their only weakness: Heart of Mountain.
This also meant they were immune to mental control and corruption by the Dark God’s whispers.
Yet this one had fallen into a completely irrational rage.
With that in mind, Daniel charged directly into the chest cavity.
Inside, it was pitch black.
The next moment, Black Dragon King’s Protection activated behind him, red light illuminating the surroundings.
He entered a massive chest cavity.
Thick ribs surrounded him, each wide enough to be hugged by several people—like a natural prison.
The ribs were covered with cracks, constantly shedding fragments.
In front of him, a massive gemstone floated in midair.
[Heart of Mountain (Epic-grade Material)]
It was roughly the size of an adult man, crystal-clear, with faint golden light swirling within.
The light pulsed rhythmically, like a heartbeat.
But what caught Daniel’s attention wasn’t the gemstone—it was what was sealed inside.
Inside floated a person—a winged being!
Silver hair, near-perfect facial features, six white wings folded tightly behind him.
His eyes were closed, expression calm, as if sleeping.
Yet along the wing edges, black veins were spreading.
The veins crawled like blood vessels, slowly corrupting the white feathers.
Daniel’s pupils constricted.
[Ding! Hidden BOSS detected, awakening...]
Crack!
The Heart of Mountain suddenly fractured.
Fissures spread from the center, golden light dimming, replaced by a sinister black mist.
The black mist surged from the cracks, carrying a stench of decay and despair.
Crack—
The Heart of Mountain shattered completely.
Shards exploded outward; Daniel dodged several flying fragments.
When he looked again, the figure inside hovered midair, eyes now open!
No whites in the eyes—only dark red pupils, like smoldering embers.
He slowly spread the six wings behind him.
Every feather was veined with black, as if soaked in ink.
The veins wriggled, and black liquid dripped from the edges, corroding the ground.
[Corrupted Angel · Aeryel Dawnstar · LV75 (Epic-grade BOSS)]

HP dropped to zero.
The Mountain God’s enormous body began to collapse, dust billowing everywhere.
The entire mountain disintegrated with deafening crashes.
[Ding!
You have slain Fallen Mountain God (Blackgold-grade BOSS)]
[Rewards: Mountain God Essence ×1, Earth Armguards (Blackgold-grade), Boulder Shield (Blackgold-grade), 500 gold coins, Contribution Points +100, 2,569,000 XP...]
Daniel stared at the door-sized hole in the Mountain God’s chest—the mark left by Aetherlance.
Inside lay the quest item: Heart of Mountain.
But as he gazed at the Mountain God’s immense body, a sense of awe struck him.
Despite its size, this was merely a young Mountain God.
He had witnessed, centuries later on the endgame battlefield, Mountain Gods over ten thousand meters tall.
One punch could tear the ground apart, and even the most powerful skills hitting them were like scratching an itch.
This Mountain God had slept for countless years, awakening only due to the Elven Queen’s summons to confront the Dark God.
The Mountain God race also went by another name—the Children of the Earth.
They were the closest offspring of the land itself, all Strength tied to the world, lacking souls.
Their only weakness: Heart of Mountain.
This also meant they were immune to mental control and corruption by the Dark God’s whispers.
Yet this one had fallen into a completely irrational rage.
With that in mind, Daniel charged directly into the chest cavity.
Inside, it was pitch black.
The next moment, Black Dragon King’s Protection activated behind him, red light illuminating the surroundings.
He entered a massive chest cavity.
Thick ribs surrounded him, each wide enough to be hugged by several people—like a natural prison.
The ribs were covered with cracks, constantly shedding fragments.
In front of him, a massive gemstone floated in midair.
[Heart of Mountain (Epic-grade Material)]
It was roughly the size of an adult man, crystal-clear, with faint golden light swirling within.
The light pulsed rhythmically, like a heartbeat.
But what caught Daniel’s attention wasn’t the gemstone—it was what was sealed inside.
Inside floated a person—a winged being!
Silver hair, near-perfect facial features, six white wings folded tightly behind him.
His eyes were closed, expression calm, as if sleeping.
Yet along the wing edges, black veins were spreading.
The veins crawled like blood vessels, slowly corrupting the white feathers.
Daniel’s pupils constricted.
[Ding!
Hidden BOSS detected, awakening...]
Crack!
The Heart of Mountain suddenly fractured.
Fissures spread from the center, golden light dimming, replaced by a sinister black mist.
The black mist surged from the cracks, carrying a stench of decay and despair.
Crack—
The Heart of Mountain shattered completely.
Shards exploded outward; Daniel dodged several flying fragments.
When he looked again, the figure inside hovered midair, eyes now open!
No whites in the eyes—only dark red pupils, like smoldering embers.
He slowly spread the six wings behind him.
Every feather was veined with black, as if soaked in ink.
The veins wriggled, and black liquid dripped from the edges, corroding the ground.
[Corrupted Angel · Aeryel Dawnstar · LV75 (Epic-grade BOSS)]

chapters.title: Chapter 30 -30-Archangel’s Crown, Vengeance Mark
paragraphs: [Corrupted Angel · Aeryel · LV75 (Epic-grade BOSS)]
A blood-red alert appeared.
Daniel’s mind tightened, and he immediately put some distance between them.
But the Corrupted Angel did not attack at once.
It hovered in midair, gazing down at the shattered fragments of the Heart of Mountain, watching the remaining pieces flicker with their last traces of faint golden light.
Then it let out a low, sorrowful wail.
The sound was both crying and rage.
Within the small chest cavity, debris cascaded down.
[Ding! Hidden Story Triggered: Corrupted Angel · Aeryel!]

Aeryel was a prince of the angel race. At his birth, the Dark Acolyte had already betrayed the angels. After failing, the Dark Acolyte placed a Dark God’s curse upon the infant, attempting to blackmail the Angel King.

Faced with orders to eliminate the fallen heir, the Angel King could not bring himself to kill his child, entrusting him secretly to a trusted Mountain God, hoping that its purifying power would gradually dispel the curse.
However, the curse was far stronger than expected. Twenty years later, Aeryel’s will was thoroughly corrupted, and even the Mountain God fell into madness under the Dark God’s whispers.
Daniel read the description, understanding immediately.
No wonder the gentle Mountain God had gone berserk.
No wonder this mountain had become a life-forbidden zone.
He had no time to dwell, as the chest cavity began to tremble violently. Cracks appeared across the thick ribs.
The Mountain God was dead. The cavity was collapsing!
At the same time, the figure moved.
Six black wings unfurled explosively. The Corrupted Angel transformed into a streak of black light, charging at him!
The speed was astonishing.
Daniel instinctively activated God Speed, dodging behind a rib.
Boom!
The angel’s claw shredded the rib behind him, debris flying and striking Daniel painfully.
Before he could react further, a second strike came!
Daniel gritted his teeth, manipulating his Dragon Wings to dodge within the confined space.
The ribs restricted his movement, and he narrowly avoided being hit several times.
The angel’s claws grazed his cheek, leaving a slash of blood.
Black wings swept across, breaking nearby ribs, nearly crushing him.
He seized an opening and drew his bow.
Aetherlance!
The golden spear shot forth at close range, piercing the angel’s chest instantly.
The angel screamed, losing 15% HP.
But instead of retreating, it became even more frenzied.
Daniel dodged with God Speed, firing arrows as he moved.
He avoided using explosive damage in this confined space—too much would collapse the chest prematurely.
Two more Aetherlance strikes hit, reducing Aeryel’s HP to 50%.
The Corrupted Angel’s movements grew faster, black mist thickening around it.
The suffocating black aura made Daniel shiver in disgust.
At the moment of his fifth Aetherlance, Aeryel suddenly halted.
He hovered midair, six black wings drooping, red light in his eyes flickering.
In that critical moment, the golden spear pierced his heart!
HP instantly dropped to zero.
Yet he did not fall.
He hovered, gazing down at the gaping wound in his chest, the black liquid still dripping.
Then he lifted his head.
The red light in his eyes vanished.
In its place were clear, pale golden eyes.
"You... who are you?"
His voice was hoarse and weak, like someone awakening after centuries of slumber.
Daniel said nothing, remaining alert.
Aeryel struggled to land on a relatively intact rib.
He looked at his ruined black wings, at the creeping black veins, and smiled bitterly.
"Indeed... I couldn’t hold on."
"And I dragged Mountain God Grandpa down with me."
He looked up at Daniel.
"My name is Aeryel, prince of the angel race."
He paused, as if recalling a distant memory.
Then he reached out to touch a thick rib beside him.
"Mountain God Grandpa accompanied me for twenty years. To suppress my curse, his Strength was consumed continuously, until in the end, even he was corrupted."
His voice trembled.
Debris continued to fall from above; the chest cavity collapsed faster and faster.
Aeryel looked at Daniel.
"You killed Mountain God Grandpa... and freed me. I owe you my life."
Struggling, he removed the golden crown from his head and handed it directly to Daniel.
"This... is for you."
[Ding! Corrupted Angel · Aeryel grants you: Archangel’s Crown (Legendary-grade)]
[Archangel’s Crown (Legendary-grade)]
Effect 1 — Archangel’s Holy Light: Immune to all angel-class magic and physical attacks; damage to angel-class enemies +800%!
Effect 2 — Power of Judgment: Damage to dark or evil-aligned enemies +1000%!
Effect 3 — Holy Blessing: Four core attributes +200; Mental Resistance +1000%!
Description: Legacy relic of the angel prince, containing the last will of a legendary archangel.
Daniel took the crown, looking at the weakened angel prince before him.
Aeryel gave a faint, weary smile.
"The Dark Acolyte... betrayed the angel race. My father... may have been deceived as well."
His voice weakened as his body turned into countless golden light particles, dissipating.
"I’m sorry..."
With the final word, he transformed completely into sparkling golden fragments, vanishing within the chest cavity.
[Ding! You have slain Corrupted Angel · Aeryel (Epic-grade BOSS)]
[Rewards: 3,500,000 XP, Holy Wing Guardian (Epic-grade) ×1, Angel’s Tear (Special) ×1, 8,000 gold coins, Contribution Points +800!]
[Ding! XP overflow detected. Current Level: 70 (Cap)]
Daniel hadn’t even checked the new equipment before a burning sensation flared across his chest.
Looking down, a golden rune slowly emerged on his chest, faintly glowing.
The rune was complex, subtly forming the shape of a pair of wings.
[Ding! You have received the Angelic Vengeance Mark!]
Effect: Angelic race members can sense your presence at close range. While marked, your location will be revealed automatically when entering angel territories.
Duration: Permanent (removable only by special means)
Daniel frowned.
Vengeance Mark?
He looked toward the place where Aeryel had disappeared; the golden particles had completely dissipated.
No wonder the angel had apologized in the end—now it made sense.
At that moment, the system alarm blared:
[Warning!!! Detection: powerful lifeform locking onto this location!!!]
[Warning!!! Evacuate immediately!!!]
A terrifying presence descended from the sky at incredible speed.
A pressure so immense it seemed to freeze the surrounding space.
Daniel didn’t hesitate and activated God Speed.
Destination: Luminara!
The next moment, he vanished.
Almost simultaneously, a golden light appeared above the Broken Spine Mountains.
A colossal angel nearly ten meters tall, twelve golden wings blotting out the sky, each feather ablaze with holy flame.
His expression was both majestic and sorrowful, gazing down at the collapsed mountains, the shattered remains of the Mountain God, and the last lingering particles of light in the air.
The king of the angel race.
"Damn you! Even if you flee to the ends of the world, I will bring your head back to honor the fallen!"
He let out a thunderous roar.
The voice carried endless sorrow and overwhelming killing intent.
Boom—!!!
Golden light erupted from him, flattening the surrounding mountains across hundreds of miles in an instant.

chapters.title: Chapter 31 -31-Supreme‐Grade Windstrider Set
paragraphs: [World Channel]
"Holy shit! Did anyone else feel that? The ground... it felt like it was shaking!"
"I was outside doing a quest! I thought it was an earthquake!"
"Something must have exploded to the west, right?"
"I saw a golden flash! So bright!"
"Could it be Faustus causing trouble again?"
"Don’t blame everything on Faustus. He’s a human, not a god!"
"Are you sure he’s human?"
Luminara, Archer Guild.
A streak of white light flashed, and Daniel’s figure appeared in the guild hall.
He rubbed his nose while glancing at the World Channel chat.
Though this was a form of indirect praise, seeing it all laid out like this still felt... odd.
"Back already?"
Shadow Song’s voice came from ahead, lazy and unhurried. "How did the quest go... hmm?"
Her words abruptly stopped.
Those deep, piercing eyes fixed on Daniel, her pupils narrowing slightly.
"You carry the aura of the Angels... and that of the royal line, no less."
Daniel gave a wry smile. "It’s a long story."
He submitted the quest item—the shattered fragment of the Mountain God’s Heart of Mountain—and briefly explained the Mountain God’s descent into madness.
Shadow Song took the fragment and, after listening to Daniel’s brief explanation, paused for three seconds in silence. Then she lifted her head and looked at him as though he were a monster.
"The Mountain God is a level 75 Blackgold‐grade BOSS. How long did it take you to complete this quest?"
"About... an hour?"
Shadow Song twitched at the corner of her mouth.

In her expectations, a normal completion would require at least fifty level‐100 mercenaries working in perfect coordination. As for a solo run... she admitted that the world occasionally produced astonishing individuals—but she hadn’t expected there to be one among the adventurers.
She paused, her tone complicated. "You’ve done what many wouldn’t even dare to dream of doing alone."
Daniel smiled. "Just lucky, I guess."
"Lucky?"
Shadow Song took a deep breath, as if trying to calm herself. "You call this luck?"
She shook her head and gestured in the air.
[Ding! Congratulations on completing the SSS‐Rank Star Ascension Quest — Fallen Mountain God]
[Class Star Rating: ★★ → ★★★]
[Maximum Level Cap Unlocked: 100]
[Reward: 150 Attribute Points (freely assignable)]
[New Class Skill Unlocked: Voidstride (SSS‐Rank)]
[Quest Rewards: 5,000 Contribution Points, 20,000 Gold Coins!]
Daniel’s eyes lit up as he eagerly clicked to view the new skill details.
[Voidstride (SSS‐Rank) — Exclusive Archer Class Skill]
Type: Active / Defensive / Mobility
Void Concealment (Core Effect)
Upon activation, the user instantly slips into the void layer, entering an invincible state for 3 seconds.
While in the void, the user cannot be targeted or harmed by any skill, attack, or effect (including true damage, instant death, or causal attacks).
Free movement is allowed, but attacking enemies is disabled until exiting the void.
Void Reversal: During Void Concealment, the user can mark a location (max distance 50m). Upon exiting, choose to teleport to the marked location or return to the original spot.
If teleporting, all damage taken in the next 2 seconds is reduced by 80%.

Void Perception: While in the void, the user can detect all creatures within 200 meters, including their level and approximate strength. This perception cannot be blocked (including stealth, invisibility, or disguise).
Cooldown: 5 minutes
MP Cost: 3,000
Class Restriction: Special Archer Class

Skill Description: Legends say that the ancient Arrow God once evaded a lethal strike by slipping into a void seam, escaping certain death. The insight gained in that instant became this supreme-grade legacy skill: The void‐walker is impervious to all.
"By the way... there’s this too."
Shadow Song retrieved a delicate box from beneath the counter.
The box was silver-white, engraved with intricate Elven patterns, with seven gemstones of different colors set into the corners, each glowing faintly.
"This is your reward."
She pushed the box toward him. "A full set of Blackgold‐grade exclusive Archer equipment — the Windchaser Set. Given your outstanding performance, it’s yours."
Daniel’s eyes brightened.
He opened the box. Seven pieces of the set were neatly arranged, each radiating a soft silver glow.
There was no doubt: the value of this series rivaled even epic-grade gear.
The collective bonus for equipping the full set far exceeded that of individual pieces.
Without hesitation, Daniel sold the Windchaser Set to the Doom Guild.
[Ding! Host successfully sold the Windchaser Set. Received 1 Copper Coin. Please choose: Quantity Boost / Quality Boost!]
"Quality boost!"
[Millionfold Boost in progress... Congratulations! Host received 1 Gold Coin and acquired the Supreme-Grade Archer Set — Windstrider!]
In the next moment, Daniel’s inventory was filled with seven pieces of crimson-red gear.
[Windstrider Scarf (Supreme-Grade)]
Agility: +150
Eagle Eye: Vision range +200%, dynamic vision enhanced to track fast-moving targets.
Focus: Regenerates 10 stamina per second in combat.
Requirements: Level 90+, Agility 1,000+
[Windstrider Robe (Supreme-Grade)]
Constitution: +120
Agility: +120
Blessing of the Wind: 50% chance to completely evade incoming attacks.
Lightness: Movement speed +30%, jump height +50%
[Windstrider Gauntlets (Supreme-Grade)]
Agility: +150
Rapid Fire: Attack speed +35%
Precision: Arrow spread -50%, hit rate greatly increased
[Windstrider Pants (Supreme-Grade)]
Constitution: +110
Agility: +150
Wind’s Protection: All damage received -15%
Endurance: Stamina consumption -30%
[Windstrider Boots (Supreme-Grade)]
Agility: +150
Gale Step: Movement speed +40% in combat, +100% out of combat
Airborne Maneuver: Three mid-air directional adjustments
[Windstrider Emblem (Supreme-Grade)]
Agility: +150
Wrath of the Wind: Critical damage +80%
Soul of the Wind: All Archer Class skill effects +50%
[Windstrider Pendant (Supreme-Grade)]
Four Core Attributes: +150
Set Resonance: Doubles effects of all Windstrider gear for 30 seconds. Cooldown: 24 hours
Wind Sovereign: After using a mobility skill, the next attack within 3 seconds deals +200% damage
Description: Forged by legendary Elven artisans, the Windstrider set is a supreme treasure. Equip all seven pieces, and you become the embodiment of the wind!
Daniel took a deep breath.
A full Supreme-Grade set!
The combined Agility bonus alone totaled 1,020 points—plus the core attribute bonuses and other effects...
Without hesitation, he equipped it.
A golden light burst from his body, then quickly faded.
At that moment, the system alerted him again:
[Ding! Detected massive overflow in your EXP pool. Auto-leveling in progress...]
Golden flashes erupted from Daniel, one after another, like fireworks.
The guild hall of the Archer Guild was bathed in dazzling golden light.
Every NPC turned in unison, jaws dropping wide open.
Shadow Song stood to the side, her normally cold expression finally breaking.
When Daniel completed his first Star Ascension Quest, he had instantly reached the level 70 cap. Now, with the cap lifted, he surged straight to the maximum level again!
Combined with his terrifying performance on the SSS quest... could he really be a hidden top-tier magical beast among humans?

Gale Step: Movement speed +40% in combat, +100% out of combat
Airborne Maneuver: Three mid-air directional adjustments
[Windstrider Emblem (Supreme-Grade)]
Agility: +150
Wrath of the Wind: Critical damage +80%
Soul of the Wind: All Archer Class skill effects +50%
[Windstrider Pendant (Supreme-Grade)]
Four Core Attributes: +150
Set Resonance: Doubles effects of all Windstrider gear for 30 seconds.
Cooldown: 24 hours
Wind Sovereign: After using a mobility skill, the next attack within 3 seconds deals +200% damage
Description: Forged by legendary Elven artisans, the Windstrider set is a supreme treasure.
Equip all seven pieces, and you become the embodiment of the wind!
Daniel took a deep breath.
A full Supreme-Grade set!
The combined Agility bonus alone totaled 1,020 points—plus the core attribute bonuses and other effects...
Without hesitation, he equipped it.
A golden light burst from his body, then quickly faded.
At that moment, the system alerted him again:
[Ding!
Detected massive overflow in your EXP pool.
Auto-leveling in progress...]
Golden flashes erupted from Daniel, one after another, like fireworks.
The guild hall of the Archer Guild was bathed in dazzling golden light.
Every NPC turned in unison, jaws dropping wide open.
Shadow Song stood to the side, her normally cold expression finally breaking.
When Daniel completed his first Star Ascension Quest, he had instantly reached the level 70 cap.
Now, with the cap lifted, he surged straight to the maximum level again!
Combined with his terrifying performance on the SSS quest... could he really be a hidden top-tier magical beast among humans?

chapters.title: Chapter 32 -32-Insecure, Obsessed with Clearing Maps
paragraphs: "How exactly did you do it?"
Shadow Song couldn’t help but ask aloud.
The golden light faded, and Daniel opened his panel.
[Current Level: 100 (Max)]
[You must complete the next Star Ascension Quest to continue leveling.]
He nodded in satisfaction, then turned to Shadow Song.
"It’s just... when I do quests, I tend to feel insecure, so I like to clear the map thoroughly. Not even a single worm is spared..."
Shadow Song’s pupils constricted.
Unbelievable. Impressive. Astonishing.
"You’re one of the most unique people I’ve ever met!"
Daniel chuckled. "As long as I’m not a weirdo, that’s fine."
Shadow Song waved her hand as if giving up on reasoning.
"Who’s to say you aren’t?"
"Hm?"
She leaned against the counter, her gaze complicated.
"I’ve been an instructor for twenty years, seen countless geniuses, but someone like you... honestly, this is a first."
"First day you were level 50, second day already level 100."
She shook her head. "If you keep this pace, in less than a month you’d surpass me."
Daniel asked with a smile, "Instructor, what’s your level?"
"Level 220."
"Then I’m close."
Shadow Song rolled her eyes.
Level 100!
In his previous life, it had taken him over a month to reach this level—now it only took two days.
And he knew... this wasn’t even the limit.
He opened the system panel and looked at a crucial option.
[Use Free Attribute Reset? (One-time only)]
[Hint: Resetting will grant all attribute points from levels 1–100, allowing full redistribution.]
Players received a one-time free reset upon reaching level 50. This was the game’s gift to them.
But Daniel, with the Heart of Balance, didn’t even need to think—just max it out!
[Ding! Resetting attribute points...]
[Reset Complete! Total Attribute Points: 2,250]
(Levels 1–20: 10 points per level, 200 total; Levels 21–100: 20 points per level, 1,600 total; Bonus points: 450)
2,250 points!
Daniel took a deep breath and didn’t hesitate—he poured everything into Agility.
[Agility: 2,250!]
But it wasn’t over.
He glanced at the [Heart of Balance] in his equipment.
This supreme-grade gear had the effect of permanently raising all four core attributes to the value of his current highest attribute.
His highest attribute? Agility—2,250!
[Ding! Heart of Balance activated!]
[Recalculating attributes...]
Strength: 2,250
Intelligence: 2,250
Agility: 2,250 (unchanged)
Constitution: 2,250
A faint golden light burst from Daniel’s body, then instantly receded.
He opened the detailed panel.
[Player: Faustus]
[Level: 100]
[Base Attributes (including equipment):]
Strength: 2,250 (+500 Black Dragon King’s Protection +200 Archangel’s Crown +150 Windstrider Pendant +20 Military Merit Medal) = 3,120
Intelligence: 2,250 (+500 Black Dragon King’s Protection ...) = 3,120
Agility: 2,250 (+500 Black Dragon King’s Protection ... +1,020 Windstrider Set) = 4,040
Constitution: 2,250 (+500 Black Dragon King’s Protection ...) = 3,170
Equipment bonuses aside, Daniel stared at the numbers in silence for ten full seconds.
4,040 Agility!
What did this mean?
His Arrowstorm now fired 100 arrows per 100 Agility—he could shoot 4,040 arrows at once!
It meant his movement speed, attack speed, and evasion rate had reached terrifying heights.
His attribute panel now surpassed most fully geared level 300 players.
Even more terrifying—all his core stats were now above 3,000.
He was no longer the fragile archer of tradition.
He had become a near-perfect hexagonal warrior.
Daniel clenched his fist, feeling the surging Strength within him.
Even a level 200 BOSS would pose no threat now.
Shadow Song was still frozen behind the counter. When Daniel glanced at her, she flinched.
"What are you planning now?"
"I want to take on a quest."
Daniel stepped forward. "The next Star Ascension Quest."
Shadow Song looked at him strangely.
"You just hit level 100... don’t you need a break?"
"Do I look like I need a break?"
Daniel shook his head. "Just give me the quest."
Shadow Song studied him for a few seconds, then smiled.
"Interesting."
She pulled a scroll from beneath the counter and handed it to Daniel.
[Star Ascension Quest: Worldwept (SSS-Rank)]

[Quest Description: On the day of the world-line convergence, the war of all realms will erupt again. You must earn enough World Points during the great battle to exchange for the required item — Primordial Crystal!]
[Quest Objective: Obtain 1,000,000 World Points in the World-Line Convergence event to exchange for 1 Primordial Crystal]
[Current World Points: 0 / 1,000,000]
[Quest Rewards: Class Star Rating +1, Attribute Points +300, Unlock new Class Skill, Unlock Level Cap!]
[Note: This quest will only be available once the World-Line Convergence event begins!]
Daniel frowned slightly.
World-Line Convergence?
In his previous life, he had experienced it four times and knew the scale of the battle.
It was a massive cross-world event, where World Points could be exchanged for rare items.
But 1,000,000 World Points...
He recalled that even the top guilds, using their entire membership, barely earned just over a million points.
For one person to get a million... nearly impossible.
Yet Daniel hesitated for only a second before accepting.
Shadow Song looked surprised.
"You’re sure?"
"This quest will take a long time and is extremely difficult. I could recommend an SS-rank quest instead. The reward is lower but you could do it immediately."
"No need."
Daniel shook his head. "SSS-rank fixed rewards—if I miss it, it’s gone forever."
Shadow Song’s eyes reflected a flicker of admiration.
"Bold."
She paused. "But are you really capable of waiting that long?"
Daniel smiled.
"My strength is far greater than you think!"
At that moment, the system pinged.
[Ding! Hidden Quest Detected Completed: Redemption of the Corrupted Angel!]
[Quest Rating: SSS-Rank]
[Rewards: 5,000 Contribution Points, 100,000 Gold Coins, Secret Chest ×1]
Daniel was stunned.
Redemption of the Corrupted Angel?
He remembered the angel prince who had finally regained consciousness, his clear golden eyes, and his smile as he faded away.
So this hidden quest came with extra rewards.
He opened his inventory and looked at the suddenly appeared treasure chest.
