chapters.title: Chapter 33 -33-Resurrection Item: Seraphic Revival
paragraphs: [Secret Chest (Special)]
Description: A chest imbued with mysterious Strength. Legends say only heroes who complete the highest-difficulty hidden quests can obtain it.
He opened it.
A golden flash appeared, revealing an ancient-looking scroll quietly resting at the bottom.
[Revival Scroll (Epic-Grade / One-Time Use)]
Effect: Can be used on an NPC who has been dead for no more than 24 hours, with a 30% chance to resurrect them.
Restriction: Only usable on NPCs; cannot affect players.

Description: The last hope left by the Angel King and the Mountain God for Aeryel Dawnstar. If purification failed, this scroll could revive him. Unfortunately, this hope was never used on the right person.
Daniel stared at the description for a few seconds.
He remembered the fading angel prince.
Even if this scroll had been used at that time, he wasn’t sure if it could have cleansed all negative statuses.
He fully understood the intention behind the Angel King and Mountain God. After all, a 30% chance is far too low!
This scroll was not to be used unless absolutely necessary.
The only miscalculation was that even the Mountain God had been directly corrupted by that Strength.
He shook his head, pushing the thought aside.
Then he opened the guild storage and placed the scroll inside.
[Ding! You sold an item to Doom Guild: Revival Scroll (Epic-Grade) for 1 Copper Coin. Millionfold Boost triggered!]
[Item is a special consumable. Choose: Quantity Boost / Quality Boost?]
"Quality boost!"
[Congratulations! You obtained: Seraphic Revival (Supreme-Grade)]
[Seraphic Revival (Supreme-Grade / Forbidden Art)]
Effect: Sacrifice a massive amount of gold coins to resurrect any deceased NPC.
Cost: Dynamically calculated based on the target’s level, race, power, time of death, etc. (Minimum: 1,000,000 Gold Coins).
Restriction 1: The resurrected unit will form a soul contract with you, binding their life and death to your control!
Restriction 2: Cannot resurrect NPCs who died of natural old age.
Cooldown: None
Description: A forbidden Supreme-Grade technique of the Angels. It binds the dead with contract chains. Some see it as sacrilege, others as a blessing.
Daniel’s pupils constricted slightly as he read the skill description.
Resurrect NPCs!
And after resurrection, they are permanently bound to him!
What did this mean?
It meant that, if he wanted, he could assemble an army of top-tier NPCs!
All the greats who had perished in history, all the heroes who had fallen for various reasons—so long as he had the gold, he could bring them back!
And money was the one thing he now had in abundance.
Even better, the skill had only one restriction—it couldn’t revive the naturally deceased.
This meant any who died in battle, were slain, or died unexpectedly could all be resurrected!
Daniel took a deep breath and didn’t hesitate to learn the skill.
[Ding! You have learned: Seraphic Revival (Supreme-Grade)]
A golden cross icon appeared in his skill bar.
He tried to view the skill details, and countless images flooded his mind.
All the historically renowned warriors, the heroes fallen in wars, the gods slain by dark deities...
As long as he wished, and had enough gold, he could make them rise again!
Of course, the prerequisite was that he could locate their corpses or soul fragments.
Daniel suppressed his excitement, silently filing this away in his mind.
An NPC army to confront enemies from other worlds, to fight alien races, to oppose dark gods...
This idea was enormous, requiring careful planning.
But at least now, it was possible.
At 11 PM, Daniel sat up in the gaming pod.
Outside, night had fallen, and the city lights twinkled in the distance.
He stretched his neck and picked up his phone.
Bank notifications still flooded in—numbers in the billions that made one dizzy.
But now? He didn’t even feel it.
Money? Just a string of numbers.
Leaning against his headboard, he closed his eyes and reviewed the day’s gains in his mind.
Level 100. Core attributes exploded. Full Supreme-Grade equipment. Supreme-Grade skills...
Everything was progressing according to plan—hundreds or even thousands of times faster than before his reincarnation.
Yet the appearance of the Angel King had sounded a warning.
A twelve-winged angel, at least level 300, possibly even a Legendary-Grade BOSS.
With his current power, confronting such an enemy would only result in instant death.
And the mark of vengeance...
Although not an immediate threat, stepping into Angelic territory would automatically reveal his position.
Meaning he must avoid all Angel-related maps for the time being.
"Troublesome..."
Daniel rubbed his brow.
Then he thought: maybe it was an opportunity.
The Angels were one of the strongest races in this world. Their territories held countless treasures and secrets.
If he could find a way to remove the mark—or even use it to his advantage...
He shook his head, bringing his thoughts back to reality.
Now was too early to think about that.
The immediate priority: continue strengthening himself, expand his power, and prepare for the upcoming World-Line Convergence.
Plus, he needed to keep an eye on fortress construction in the real world.
He opened his phone to check progress.
The construction site in the Alpine region had begun, with thousands of workers laboring day and night.
The underground fortress framework was already up, with the main structure expected to finish in two months.
Taking advantage of the time, Daniel purchased a batch of extremely rare materials to strengthen the construction, aiming for absolute structural integrity.
Everything was proceeding according to plan!
The next morning at 8 AM, Daniel logged in on time.
A flash of white light, and he appeared in the central plaza of Luminara.
The crowd was several times larger than yesterday—bustling with activity.
Some were teleporting between portals, some calling for parties, some selling items.
Daniel ignored them all and opened his pet space.
A rocky head peeked out, two yellow crystal-like eyes blinking, then the entire body leapt out.
[Earthmount Dragon (Ancient Dragon · LV15)]
Status: Awake
Affinity: 100 (Max)
The little stone dragon climbed onto his shoulder, nudging his face with its head, emitting affectionate coos.
Daniel laughed, patting its head, then opened its attribute panel.
[Earthmount Dragon (Legendary-Grade)]
Level: 1
Base Attributes:
Strength: 500 (+ per-level growth)
Constitution: 500
Agility: 100
Intelligence: 100
Skills: Crystal Breath, Stonehide, Terra Force, Immortal
Daniel’s eyes brightened.
Even at base stats, this pet rivaled mid-level players. With per-level growth in all four core attributes, it was a tank among tanks.

chapters.title: Chapter 34 -34-Legendary-Grade? Pet Rankings Activated
paragraphs: Daniel glanced at the massive overflow of experience in his EXP pool and didn’t hesitate—he shared it.
[Ding! You shared experience with your pet "Earthmount Dragon"...]
Golden light flashed around the little stone dragon for quite some time.
Then it leapt from Daniel’s shoulder, its body rapidly expanding in the golden glow.
Once only the size of a small puppy, it instantly grew over three meters long and more than two meters tall.
Its rough rocky skin became even tougher, the scale-like patterns more distinct.
A row of stone spikes appeared along its spine, and its tail thickened and strengthened.
Its yellow crystal-like eyes glimmered brightly, radiating authority.
[Earthmount Dragon (Ancient Dragon · LV77)]
[Current Actual Attributes:]
Strength: 2,040
Constitution: 2,040
Agility: 870
Intelligence: 870
Daniel nodded in satisfaction.
2,040 Strength and Constitution alone already surpassed many level-100 tank players.
And it had four powerful skills—especially the insanely overpowered Immortal, which made it unkillable as long as it touched the ground.
The little stone dragon... or rather, now a "big stone dragon," nudged Daniel before shrinking back.
Within seconds, it returned to its puppy size, flapping its wings as it flew back to Daniel’s shoulder and settled into a comfortable position.
Daniel chuckled.
This little guy really knew how to enjoy life.
At that moment, a system announcement echoed throughout the Stellar World.
[Ding! Global Announcement!!!]
[The number of players owning pets has reached 10. The Pet System is officially live, and the Pet Rankings are now open!]
[Rankings will update in real time with all players’ pet information!]
[Top-ranked players will receive generous rewards!]
The World Channel erupted instantly.
"The pet system is live?!"
"Check the rankings! What pets are out there?!"
"Let’s see Faustus’s Blackgold-Grade pet... Holy shit?!"
"Legendary-grade?! Are you kidding me?!"
[Pet Rankings]
Earthmount Dragon (Legendary-Grade) — Owner: Faustus
Shadow Demon Wolf (Blackgold-Grade) — Owner: Crimson Soul
Ironwall Guardian (Silver-Grade) — Owner: Digital Phantom
Flame Warhorse (Iron-Grade) — Owner: ...
"Legendary-grade??? I didn’t misread that, right??"
"Faustus! Are you kidding? That’s a legendary-grade pet!"
"Wait, didn’t he get a Blackgold-Grade companion egg? Am I remembering wrong?"
"Earthmount Dragon, Ancient Dragon... that’s a freaking dragon!"
"I just got a Bronze-Grade wild boar pet, and he already has a dragon???"
"No way, did Faustus steal a dragon’s lair?"
"Impossible! A dragon’s nest is a top-tier map, level 300+!"
"How did he even get it? I want a dragon too!"
"Yeah, that’s so cool... it’s a dragon!"
"Who’s the second place, Crimson Soul? Level 22 and already has a Blackgold-Grade pet?"
"Wait, level 22 and a Blackgold-Grade companion egg??? What kind of luck is that?!"
"The third-ranked pet is only Silver-Grade, way below Blackgold-Grade... and after that, mostly Iron and Bronze—what a gap!"
"I don’t accept this! Why can a level 22 newbie get a Blackgold-Grade pet?"
"They’ve got the skills for it. You do it if you can."
"Forget Faustus, what’s the deal with Crimson Soul?"
"I think I saw her the day before yesterday, a female player, hunting boars in Starter Village."
"Wait, Faustus gave her a Blackgold-Grade companion egg... could there be a connection?"
"Hard to say... I wouldn’t dare."
"I’m jealous. Seriously jealous..."
[Rhine Guild · Core Channel]
"Got it."
Vice Guildmaster North Wind’s voice spoke.
"Crimson Soul’s real identity: the eldest daughter of the Violet Consortium, a Mage class. She just founded Violet Guild yesterday..."
"Where did she get her pet?"
"From Faustus."
The channel went silent for a second.
"Bought it? As expected from a Violet Consortium heiress—so extravagant!"
"No, she only spent 10,000 Gold Coins."
"What? 10,000 Gold Coins?! A Blackgold-Grade pet for just 10,000?!"
"What’s Faustus thinking? Selling to Crimson Soul for 10,000, but even if we offered a million, he wouldn’t sell!"
Guildmaster Rhine Watcher fell silent for a moment before speaking slowly.
"There are two possibilities."
"First, he may have some private deal with the Violet family that we don’t know about."
"Second, he just likes Crimson Soul."
"Guildmaster, which do you think?"
"First one."
"Why?"
"Because he is Faustus!"
The channel fell silent again.
"I don’t believe such a god-tier player is just a lone wolf with no backing."
[Stormbound Guild · Encrypted Channel]
"Guildmaster, this Crimson Soul..."
"Find out her real identity!"
"Done. She’s the eldest daughter of the Violet Consortium, not to be trifled with."
Vantheon narrowed his eyes, a hint of greed flashing.
"Violet Consortium... tricky, but they don’t care much about the virtual industry, right?"
"So should we..."
"Not yet."
Vantheon waved.
"Watch her first. Wait for the right moment."
The Violet Consortium was one of the top ten richest families in the world, with wealth rivaling nations.
Even the conglomerates behind the scenes would defer to them.
Daniel watched the chaos in World Channel and smirked slightly.
He looked at the second-ranked player on the pet leaderboard—Crimson Soul’s name stood out.
Level 22, Blackgold-Grade pet.
She was impressive—already hatched a powerful companion this fast.
He opened a private message and sent her a note:
"Congratulations on ranking!"
A few seconds later, she replied:
"!!! Faustus, you actually messaged me!"
"Thanks! All thanks to you!"
"Yeah, train well. Don’t waste that companion egg."
She paused for a few seconds, then replied:
"I will! Thank you, Faustus!"
Daniel closed the chat, feeling pleased.
One of the top ten human heroes from his past life was now tied to him via a companion egg.
This transaction—worth it.
Crimson Soul also felt a mix of emotions.
Her companion egg had hatched into a powerful pet, strong enough at level one to handle many monsters.
As her level increased, the Shadow Demon Wolf grew stronger too. In less than an hour, it had already leveled three times!
She was grateful for Faustus’s generosity.
As for his legendary-grade pet... while she envied it, her feelings were more admiration than jealousy.
At the same time, her curiosity about Faustus deepened.
How did he accomplish all this single-handedly?
[Ding! Pet Rankings Settling...]
A system notification rang in Daniel’s ear.

chapters.title: Chapter 35 -35-Twin Link: Skill Sharing!
paragraphs: [Ding! Pet Rankings Settling...]
A system notification rang in Daniel’s ear.
[Congratulations! Your pet ranked #1 on the leaderboard!]
[Rewards are being issued...]
[You received: S-Rank Pet Mastery Skillbook — Cooperative Combat!]
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
A free S-Rank skillbook?
He opened his inventory. A skillbook, glowing faintly, rested quietly in the slot.
The skill effect: the owner can unilaterally share 10% of their attribute points with their pet. Not bad!
But Daniel’s focus was on whether it was bound. Checking bindings had become second nature to him.
Seeing it was unbound, he didn’t hesitate—he sold it.
[Ding! You sold Skillbook: Cooperative Combat (S-Rank) to Doom Guild for 1 Copper Coin. Millionfold Boost triggered!]
[Choose: Quantity Boost / Quality Boost!]
"Quality boost!"
[Ding! Millionfold Boost reward... Congratulations! You received 1 Gold Coin! You have also acquired a Pet Mastery-exclusive skill — Twin Link (SSS-Rank)!]
[Twin Link (SSS-Rank)]
Effect: Establish a deep soul link with your pet, granting the following abilities:
Skill Sharing: Use all skills of your pet (cooldowns calculated independently).
Trait Sharing: Temporarily (30 seconds) adopt your pet’s core racial traits (Cooldown: 1 hour).
Attribute Resonance: When the pet is nearby, both gain +10% to all attributes.
Life Link: You may redirect damage you receive to your pet (requires pet consent).
Description: The ultimate bond between human and pet, allowing your combat power to exceed the sum of its parts — 1+1>2!
Daniel took a deep breath.
This was a god-tier skill for pets!
In his previous lives, he had seen this skillbook once—an ordinary player accidentally obtained it, and it sold for a fortune at the auction house.
Its effect was insanely practical.
1+1>2? Not a single exaggeration.
He glanced at the little stone dragon on his shoulder and immediately decided to learn it.
[Ding! You have learned: Twin Link (SSS-Rank)]
[Select a pet to link: Earthmount Dragon]
"Confirm!"
A golden chain of light extended from his chest, connecting to the little stone dragon.
The dragon lifted its head, blinked, and nuzzled his face affectionately.
[Ding! Link Successful!]
[You can now use your pet’s skills: Crystal Breath, Stonehide, Terra Force!]
Daniel’s grin widened insanely.
Crystal Breath — Attack +10,000%!
Stonehide — Immune to 50% physical damage, HP recovery +200%!
Terra Force — Control the earth itself!
— As long as it touches the ground, it cannot die!
Though Earthmount Dragon’s Immortal trait shared for only 30 seconds, using it at a critical moment could absolutely turn the tide of battle.
He looked at the little dragon on his shoulder and liked it more with each glance.
The creature seemed to sense its owner’s mood, emitting soft coos and settling back down to sleep.
After handling his pet, Daniel opened the system panel and checked his quest list.
The SSS-Rank Worldwept quest still wouldn’t unlock for a while.
But he couldn’t sit idle.
There were many things to do: expand his enterprises, increase his strength, prepare for the upcoming war...
And that angelic mark of vengeance...
Suddenly, a spark went off in his mind—titles!
In the Stellar World, titles represented identity, status, and privileges.
A titled player could enjoy various benefits within human territories: hire higher-level NPCs, purchase rarer resources, accept higher-difficulty quests, and even own land!
All these advantages could accelerate his plans.
In his previous lives, Daniel had never gone this route—the threshold for joining NPC circles was too high.
But now? Everything was possible.
"Looks like it’s time to visit the City Lord’s Mansion."
Daniel stood and made his way to the center of Luminara.
The Luminara City Lord’s Mansion stood at the city’s heart—a magnificent Gothic building.
Tall spires, stained glass windows, exquisite stone carvings—all radiating authority and splendor.
At the entrance stood two lines of fully armed guards, swords at the ready, eyes unwavering.
Daniel approached. A guard stepped forward.
"Stop! This is the City Lord’s Mansion. No entry for idlers!"
Daniel didn’t speak, merely displaying his Pioneer of Creation title.
The guard’s pupils contracted. He immediately stood at attention and saluted respectfully.
"Ah! Honorable Adventurer! Please, enter!"
Daniel nodded and strode into the mansion.
A guard immediately sent a magical letter to report his arrival...
Walking down a long corridor, he arrived at a large oak door.
It opened automatically, revealing a spacious reception hall.
A middle-aged man in luxurious robes sat at the main seat, sipping tea.
His hair was gray, his expression authoritative, exuding a subtle aura of pressure.
[Luminara City Lord · Augusta (LV299)]
Daniel blinked.
Level 299!
Wasn’t Augusta the legendary level-300+ Greatsword Master?
He quickly remembered—his memory was based on normal progression several months ahead.
At this point, Augusta hadn’t yet reached that level. Still, this was the highest-level NPC Daniel had seen so far.
Augusta looked up at him, a flicker of surprise in his deep eyes.
"Oh? A level 100 adventurer?"
"And a legendary-grade dragon as a companion... Interesting."
Daniel opened his mouth to speak, but Augusta waved him off.
"No need to introduce yourself. I already know you!"
He stood, walking up to Daniel, eyes scanning him from head to toe.
"Faustus, Pioneer of Creation, Honorary Citizen of Nine Cities, Level 2 Honor Medal holder, first player to found a guild, first to slay a Gold-Grade BOSS, first to enter a main city..."
He recited the long list of titles in one breath, lips curling slightly.
"Honestly, I’ve never seen such an exceptional adventurer before."
Daniel smiled.
"Your Lordship is too kind."
"Kind? No, I speak the truth."
Augusta returned to his seat, gesturing for Daniel to sit.
"I’ve experienced the teleportation network you built. Very convenient, very stable—far better than Harold’s."
Daniel twitched his mouth.
If Harold heard that, he’d probably cry.
Augusta regarded him carefully.
"Why have you come today?"
"I want to purchase a title."
Since Augusta was straightforward, Daniel told him the truth.
"You want to buy a title?"
A hint of surprise crossed Augusta’s eyes.
"Yes."
"Hm... Normally, purchasing a basic title requires 10,000 Contribution Points, 5 million Gold Coins, and proof of merit."
He paused.
"But for you, none of that is an issue."
He walked to the window, back to Daniel.
"The teleportation networks you built across the Nine Main Cities have contributed greatly to all of humanity."
"By imperial decree, you are being granted the title of Viscount as a special reward."
He turned back, smiling.
"How’s that? A surprise?"
Daniel froze.
He had come to buy a title, but the emperor was just giving it to him?
At that moment, the system pinged.
[Ding! Global Announcement!!!]
[Player "Faustus" has been granted the title of Viscount by imperial decree for outstanding contributions to humanity!]
[As the first player to receive a title, you also gain:]
Contribution Points +10,000
Gold Coins +50,000
Honorary Title: Rising Star of the Empire!
[This achievement has been recorded in the Stellar Chronicles for all time!]
The World Channel erupted.
"What??? A title???"
"Viscount? This game even has a nobility system?"
"Who is Faustus exactly? How does he get all the good things?!"
"I just entered a main city, and he’s already nobility!"
"No way, the gap is too huge!"
"I don’t accept this! Why him?"
"Because he built the teleportation networks across the Nine Main Cities. What have you done?"
"I... I built... style..."
"Shut up!"

chapters.title: Chapter 36 -36-Promoted to Count
paragraphs: Daniel stared at the system notification, a flicker of surprise crossing his mind.
But he quickly composed himself.
Being promoted to Viscount was indeed unexpected, yet it was far from enough. His ambitions reached far beyond that.
"Lord of the City," he said, lifting his gaze to meet Augusta’s eyes. "I want to continue advancing my noble rank."
Augusta raised an eyebrow. "Oh? And which rank do you wish to attain?"
"Count."
"Count?!"

A hint of surprise flashed across Augusta’s eyes. "From Viscount to Count is just one step. All you need is to make a bit more contribution to the Empire, and the promotion will go through smoothly. Are you sure you’re willing to pay the extra price to rise further?"
"I’m sure."
Daniel nodded. "How many gold coins will it cost?"
Augusta was silent for a few seconds before smiling. "Looks like someone isn’t short on money."
He returned to his seat and began calculating.
"Under normal circumstances, to rise from no title to Count, you would need to meet the following conditions:"
"Contribution Points: over 50,000, proof of achievements, and... 50 million gold coins."

"But since you already hold the rank of Viscount, your Contribution Points are slightly lacking, yet you possess the Second-Level Honor Medal. Your proofs of achievement can also be substituted through the teleportation network."
She looked up at Daniel. "So all you need to do is pay 30 million gold coins to become a Count!"
Without hesitation, Daniel opened the transaction interface.
[You have transferred 30,000,000 gold coins to the official Luminara account!]
Augusta’s pupils constricted slightly as she watched the number settle.
Thirty million gold coins... just like that?
If she remembered correctly, Daniel had just yesterday bought up all the commercial properties across the nine main cities.
This adventurer... how rich was he, exactly?
Yet she didn’t ask further, simply nodding.
"Very well. From this moment onward, Lord Daniel, you are a Count of the Empire!"
A burst of golden light erupted from Daniel.
[Ding! Congratulations on your promotion to Count!]
[You have obtained the following privileges:]

[1. Immunity: Within human territories, certain crimes can be pardoned, and in some cases, even if you yourself break certain laws, partial immunity may apply (except for high crimes such as treason or murder).]
[2. Decree Power: You may issue corresponding quests for players or NPCs to undertake.]
[3. Domain Rights: You may purchase territories, levy taxes, manage industries, and recruit troops within your domain.]
[4. Priority Privileges: Receive a 20% discount at NPC stores and have priority access to quests.]
[6. Political Participation: You may attend the Imperial Assembly and vote on major decisions.]
[Contribution Points +20,000]
[Gold Coins +100,000]
Daniel’s lips curled into a slight smile as he scanned the long list of privileges. These were exactly what he had wanted.
The simplest advantage: should he ever get a red name in the city—kill another player—his Count status could help mitigate punishment.
And even the punishment itself would be adjudicated jointly by City Lord Augusta and the Chief Justice!
Honestly, if not for the complications and enormous costs of promoting to Marquis, Duke, or Grand Duke, he would have moved up without hesitation.
Alas, beyond Count, unless one had enormous achievements and royal blood, further promotions were simply unimaginable.
As for Duke or Grand Duke, the costs players would need to pay were beyond comprehension.
Take City Lord Augusta, for example. As the lord of one of the nine main cities, he was a Grand Duke with royal blood, a status of unmatched prestige.
"Now that you are a Count, it’s time to consider your domain, isn’t it?" Augusta asked with a smile. "Would you like me to recommend some good locations?"
Daniel nodded with a smile.
A domain of his own—this was exactly what he needed.
He waved his hand, and a massive light-and-shadow map unfolded before him, detailing the entire Empire.
Daniel scanned the map, which was densely labeled with countless place names, each region marked in a different color.
"Before that, I need to explain the Empire’s territory grading system," Augusta said, tapping lightly. Lines of text appeared next to the map.
"According to Article 12, Volume III of the Imperial Code, all Imperial territories are divided into seven grades, each corresponding to specific specifications, privileges, and purchase conditions."

"Level One is the village, the lowest-level territorial unit, primarily agricultural production... Then comes the town, larger in size, with more population, and equipped with systematic agriculture and industry..."
After that come basic city, intermediate city, advanced city, the nine main cities, and at the center, the Imperial Capital.
As a Count, Daniel could currently manage territories up to the basic city level.
Hearing the explanation, Daniel quickly decided what he needed.
"I want a territory of basic city grade."
Augusta smiled knowingly, pointing to a blue patch on the map.
"Here, see this? The Emerald Plains to the east of Luminara. Fertile land, rich resources—perfect for agricultural development."
"Then there’s the Emerald Coast to the south. Beautiful scenery, abundant pearls and corals, great for tourism."
"Or here, the Ironspine Mountains to the west. Rich in minerals, ideal for mining."
She explained each territory, all prime locations brimming with potential.
No one would believe that Augusta had no personal motives in making such recommendations.
In truth, Augusta had noticed Daniel’s talent and also had immense confidence in his potential.
In just a few days, he had reached level 100, held the title of legendary-grade engineer, and even had a juvenile dragon as a pet...
Any one of these alone would attract attention.
These wealthy territories were like fat sheep, with extremely high annual tax revenue. Even if Daniel contributed nothing, the taxes alone would greatly increase his merit.
If Daniel could make a few more contributions to the Empire and govern his domain effectively, a promotion to Marquis within a few years would be entirely possible.
Territories were usually tightly held, yet Augusta was willing to allocate some to Daniel—it was, essentially, an investment in him.
He saw limitless potential in Daniel.
But Daniel paid no attention to these fertile lands. His gaze fell on the northernmost region of the map, a gray area marked with small letters:
[Polaris City – Adjacent to the Otherworld Abyss, Danger Level: S]
"Polaris City?"
Daniel pointed at the location.
Augusta’s smile stiffened.
"It’s close to the Abyss, and occasionally small-scale demon incursions occur... You don’t intend to go there, do you?"
"Mm."
"You’re sure?"
Augusta’s expression turned serious. "That’s not a good choice. Being adjacent to the Otherworld Abyss, even if the attacks are minor for now, Polaris City will be the first to bear the brunt."
"Moreover, the climate is harsh, the soil barren, almost no production. Becoming the lord there... forget profit, just surviving will be a challenge."
She fixed her gaze on Daniel and asked in a deep voice, "Are you certain you want to go there?"
Daniel nodded again. "I’m sure."
Augusta fell silent for a few seconds before suddenly smiling.
"I see..."

chapters.title: Chapter 37 -37-Purchasing Polaris City and Hiring Top-Tier NPCs
paragraphs: Developing a domain safely in the heartland would take at least several years before one could accumulate enough merit to be promoted to Marquis.
But the frontier was different!
As long as you could fend off invasions from other races, your merit would skyrocket! Even long-established Marquises and Dukes mostly held domains in the borderlands.
For them, the other races were both a threat and a source of glory.
Augusta, however, shook his head. "Young man, having courage is admirable, but the frontier is no easy place. You could lose your life at any moment."
Daniel smiled. "I know."
A flicker of admiration crossed Augusta’s eyes.
"Alright, since you’ve made up your mind, I won’t stop you."
He tapped on the map, and the territory of Polaris City immediately lit up.
[Polaris City (Basic City)]
[Area: ~500 square kilometers]
[Population: ~30,000 (Humans)]
[Current Status: Normal]
[Purchase Price: 100 million gold coins (10% discount for Counts)]
[Lord Rights: Collect taxes within the domain (up to 10%), manage industries, recruit armies (up to 5,000 troops), issue quests, etc.]
Daniel paid immediately.
[Gold Coins -90,000,000]
[Ding! Congratulations! You are now the Lord of Polaris City!]
[Current Territory: Polaris City and surrounding areas]
[Lord Rank: Count]
[Term: Lifetime (non-hereditary)]
Daniel exhaled deeply after reviewing the territory information.
With the status of Count and his own domain, many things would now become much easier!
At that moment, Augusta also closed the map. After a brief hesitation, he looked at Daniel.
"By the way, there’s something I’d like to ask you for help with."
Daniel raised an eyebrow. "Go ahead."
"Luminara has run into some trouble recently."
Augusta paused. "The Intelligence Bureau discovered some anomalies while investigating the other races. But we’re short on manpower, and need someone to assist."
He looked at Daniel. "Are you interested?"
[Ding! Special Quest Triggered: Augusta’s Commission]
[Quest Objective: Report to the Intelligence Bureau for detailed instructions]
[Accept?]
Daniel’s heart stirred.
Information on the other races? Judging by Augusta’s hesitant expression, if his status and rank hadn’t just been elevated, he would never have been entrusted with such a sensitive mission.
And naturally, for a mission of such significance, the rewards would surely be considerable.
"I’ll take this quest!" he said.
After leaving the Lord’s Manor, Daniel didn’t rush to the Intelligence Bureau.
There was something more important he needed to handle first.
The Commercial Management Office.
It was a refined two-story building next to the Lord’s Manor. Pushing open the door, Daniel entered a tastefully decorated space with redwood floors and oil paintings on the walls.
A middle-aged man in a well-tailored suit stood behind the counter, smiling at him.
[Stephen, Chief of Luminara Commercial Management (Epic-Grade NPC)]
"Welcome, Your Grace," Stephen greeted respectfully. "How may I assist you today?"
Daniel withdrew his thoughts and spoke directly.
"I want to hire NPCs."
"Very well. What rank of NPCs do you require?"
"The top-tier."
Stephen’s eyes widened slightly. "Top-tier NPCs? Your Grace, hiring top-tier NPCs is... not inexpensive..."
"Money isn’t an issue," Daniel interrupted. "I need the following types: Commercial Management, Financial Auditing, Store Operations, Logistics Coordination, and City Construction."
"At least ten NPCs in each category—all top-tier."
Stephen froze for three seconds, then took a deep breath.
"Your Grace, are you certain?"
"Certain."
"Then... please wait a moment."
He turned and went into a back room. A few minutes later, he returned holding a thick stack of documents.
"This is the current list of available top-tier NPCs—127 in total. Their hiring costs vary, but on average, each requires about 100,000 gold coins per month."
127 NPCs at 100,000 each—a total of 12.7 million gold coins per month.
Stephen expected Daniel to be intimidated by the number.
But Daniel simply nodded. "Hire them all."
"All... all of them?!"
Stephen’s hand shook so much that the stack of papers nearly fell.
"Your Grace... are you sure it’s all of them?"
"Absolutely."
Daniel opened the transaction interface and transferred the funds.
[You have transferred 15,000,000 gold coins to the Luminara Commercial Management Office (including deposit).]
Stephen stared at the string of zeros on the screen, utterly dumbfounded.
He had been Chief of Commercial Management for ten years and had seen countless wealthy individuals.
But someone spending like this—this was a first.
"Your Grace... what exactly are you planning?"
Daniel smiled. "To be a relaxed boss."
"A relaxed... boss?"
"Yes."
Daniel stood up. "All the player-run shops in the nine main cities require management. I have neither the time nor the patience to handle them myself."
"These top-tier NPCs will manage them for me."
He paused. "Additionally, I need you to recruit NPCs willing to develop Polaris City. Top-tier, of course."
"Engineers for city construction, merchants for commercial development, soldiers for security... at least twenty in each category, with generous compensation."
Stephen opened his mouth, then closed it, finally squeezing out:
"Your Grace, are you planning to build Polaris City from the ground up?"
Daniel smiled. "Something like that."
Over the next half hour, Stephen, in a state of stunned numbness, helped Daniel complete all the hiring procedures.
127 top-tier commercial NPCs, all signed five-year contracts.
60 city construction NPCs, signed three-year contracts.
50 security NPCs, signed five-year contracts.
30 agricultural and mining NPCs, signed three-year contracts.
A total of 267 top-tier NPCs, with a monthly payroll exceeding 20 million gold coins!
After signing the last contract, Stephen’s hands were still trembling.
"Your Grace... you’re... extraordinarily generous."
"Of course!"
Daniel smiled, putting away all the contracts.
Each of these top-tier NPCs was priceless.
Crucially, these top-tier NPCs were not easily hired.
If he were an ordinary person without a title, no matter how many Contribution Points he had, the NPCs would at most treat him politely.
But hiring them to work for him? Sorry, these individuals serve nobles exclusively.
This was one of the reasons Daniel had sought to elevate his rank.
With status and rank, he could call upon the best talent. As his noble rank rose further, these top-tier NPCs would even compete to serve him!
Above them, there were epic-grade and legendary-grade NPCs—each possessing extraordinarily specialized skills.
Stephen before him was an epic-grade NPC, overseeing all commercial operations in Luminara.
Epic-grade NPCs were common in Luminara’s main cities.
This was the hidden power of a main city. Many NPCs players see every day were actually top-tier talents that most players could never approach.
Even so, the NPCs Daniel had hired were far more capable than normal NPCs and could handle extremely complex tasks independently.
With them, managing the commercial operations of the nine main cities was no problem.
With them, building Polaris City was secure.
All Daniel had to do was set the objectives and rules, let them execute, and simply collect the rewards.

chapters.title: Chapter 38 -38-The Intelligence Bureau Mission
paragraphs: [World Channel]
"Guys, check the leaderboard! Faustus is level 100!"
"What?? Yesterday he was only 70! How is he already 100?!"
"He’s hacking, right? He must be hacking! Let’s see how you diehard fans explain this one!"
"Exactly! Second place is only level 43, and he’s 100—does that make sense?"
"It doesn’t, but it happened."
"Wait, look at his title! Count!!!"
"Count??? When did that happen???"
"It was just the server-wide announcement! He was given Viscount out of turn, and then he promoted himself to Count!"
"From Viscount to Count... how did he skip over the normal procedure?"
"Money talks, that’s how."
"No, even with money, there should be other restrictions, right?"
"I checked at Lord’s Manor. To promote to Baron, you need Contribution Points and achievements. Now I’m curious—how many Contribution Points does he have to reach Count?"
"No one knows, but the conservative estimate is over 20,000..."
"20,000 Contribution Points??? I only have 200!"
"Faustus is unbeatable..."
[Eternal Eagle Guild]
"Level 100."
Guild Master Whitehead Falcon’s voice was low and grave. "Our highest-level member is only 43, and he’s already 100."
"Count rank... we haven’t even reached the Baron threshold."
"Legendary-grade pet... we don’t even have a few Bronze-grade ones."
"And his power... it’s unimaginable..."
He fell silent for a few seconds, then spoke slowly.
"This man cannot be measured by normal standards."
The Vice Master asked cautiously, "Master, should we continue trying to recruit him?"
"Recruit him?" Whitehead Falcon scoffed. "Do you think we have anything to offer him?"
"Money? You think he lacks money?"
"Equipment? Connections? Luxury cars and beauties?"
The channel fell completely silent.
After a long pause, a voice came from the corner.
"Investigate and clarify exactly what his relationship is with the Violet Consortium family!"
"Everything about him must be investigated thoroughly, especially in the real world. Step up efforts, and if necessary, involve the A-country intelligence agency!"
"I refuse to believe there’s anyone Morgan Consortium cannot find!"
[Stormbound Guild]
Vantheon stared at the name on the leaderboard, his face turning pale.
Level 100.
Count!
Legendary-grade pet!
Each word hit him like a slap to the face.
A subordinate cautiously asked, "Master, should we continue targeting him?"
Vantheon remained silent for a long while. Then, gritting his teeth, he managed to say,
"Pause... for now."
"Pause?"
"Can’t you understand human language? Pause!"
He smashed the cup in his hand. "We’ll deal with him when the opportunity comes!"
The subordinate exhaled in relief. No more suicide missions... at least for now.
Daniel closed the World Channel, a faint smile on his lips.
Their reactions were exactly what he had expected.
But it didn’t matter.
He no longer cared about others’ opinions.
Now, the only thing on his mind was strength.
Only that Final Catastrophe!
Once he dealt with that guy, he could leisurely enjoy life afterward.
He took a deep breath and headed toward the Intelligence Bureau.
The Intelligence Bureau was located in the northern district of Luminara, a heavy stone building.
A massive shield emblem hung over the entrance, flanked by fully armed guards.
Daniel entered through the gates into a spacious hall.
Maps and intelligence reports lined the walls, while several officer-looking figures spoke in low tones.
A tall, slender middle-aged man stood in the center, examining a huge sand table.
[Rex, Head of Luminara Intelligence Bureau (LV260)]
Daniel approached.
"Director Rex, I’m here to receive the mission."
Rex looked up and glanced at him.
"Oh? The Count himself has arrived?"
His voice was calm and firm, carrying the crisp decisiveness of a soldier.
"The City Lord has briefed me—there is a mission assigned to you."
He picked up a scroll and handed it to Daniel.
[Intelligence Bureau Commission: Investigation of Savage Stone Settlement (S-Rank)]

[Mission Description: Recently, our scouts in the Savage Stone Mountains have detected abnormal activity. The Beastfolk and Goblin tribes have been frequently contacting each other, suggesting a possible conspiracy. Investigate the Savage Stone Settlement to collect evidence of collusion between the two tribes.]
[Objectives: Collect at least three valid pieces of evidence (secret letters, treaties, meeting records, etc.)]
[Difficulty: S-Rank]
[Recommended Level: 100+]
[Time Limit: 7 days]
[Rewards: Contribution Points +5,000; Merit Points +3,000; Gold Coins +100,000; Intelligence Bureau Treasure Chest ×1]
Daniel read the mission description, and memories of past lives flickered through his mind.
During the early stages of previous server openings, these two races had always been hostile toward each other.
Beastfolk looked down on Goblins, considering them inferior.
Goblins feared Beastfolk and fled whenever they appeared.
But one day, without warning, they suddenly united, causing massive losses for the Humans.
That battle saw countless players and NPCs perish, and several frontier cities were breached.
Had it not been for the combined counterattack of the major main cities, the consequences would have been disastrous.
Could it be that all of this began with this very conspiracy?
If he could preemptively dismantle this plot...
"Leave the mission to me."
Rex nodded. "Good. I’ll be waiting for your report, Count."
He paused, his expression serious.
"By the way, the Savage Stone Settlement is deep in Beastfolk territory. The danger level is extremely high."
"If anything seems off, retreat immediately!"
Daniel smiled. "Don’t worry."
He turned and exited the Intelligence Bureau, disappearing into the crowd.
Behind him, Rex watched his back thoughtfully.
"Level 100 adventurer... legendary-grade pet... no wonder the City Lord entrusted this mission to him."
He shook his head and returned to studying the intelligence in front of him.
Daniel looked up at the sky as he left the Bureau.
Savage Stone Mountains—the heart of Beastfolk territory.
With his current strength, he could face even a level 200 BOSS without worry.
And he still had so many trump cards.
He patted the little stone dragon on his shoulder.
The small creature was still asleep, softly snoring.
Daniel smiled and strode toward the portal.
Savage Stone Mountains
The sky was gray, clouds low and oppressive, and the air carried a wild, untamed scent.
A white flash appeared, and a figure materialized on the edge of the Savage Stone Mountains.
This location lay in the northwest corner of Human territory. Farther north stretched an endless, primeval forest.
Daniel checked his map for orientation.
Savage Stone Settlement—the main Wolfkin settlement—lay ahead, at the junction of plains and forest.
Once he understood the general direction, Daniel folded his map and sped toward the target.
Half an hour later, a settlement appeared in the distance.
It was a typical Beastfolk-style camp.
No walls, no fortifications—just hundreds of massive animal-skin tents scattered about. At the center was a huge fire pit plaza.
Between the tents, countless Wolfkin warriors patrolled back and forth, their vigilance extreme.

sentences.text: [World Channel]
"Guys, check the leaderboard!
Faustus is level 100!"
"What??
Yesterday he was only 70!
How is he already 100?!"
"He’s hacking, right?
He must be hacking!
Let’s see how you diehard fans explain this one!"
"Exactly!
Second place is only level 43, and he’s 100—does that make sense?"
"It doesn’t, but it happened."
"Wait, look at his title!
Count!!!"
"Count???
When did that happen???"
"It was just the server-wide announcement!
He was given Viscount out of turn, and then he promoted himself to Count!"
"From Viscount to Count... how did he skip over the normal procedure?"
"Money talks, that’s how."
"No, even with money, there should be other restrictions, right?"
"I checked at Lord’s Manor.
To promote to Baron, you need Contribution Points and achievements.
Now I’m curious—how many Contribution Points does he have to reach Count?"
"No one knows, but the conservative estimate is over 20,000..."
"20,000 Contribution Points???
I only have 200!"
"Faustus is unbeatable..."
[Eternal Eagle Guild]
"Level 100."
Guild Master Whitehead Falcon’s voice was low and grave.
"Our highest-level member is only 43, and he’s already 100."
"Count rank... we haven’t even reached the Baron threshold."
"Legendary-grade pet... we don’t even have a few Bronze-grade ones."
"And his power... it’s unimaginable..."
He fell silent for a few seconds, then spoke slowly.
"This man cannot be measured by normal standards."
The Vice Master asked cautiously, "Master, should we continue trying to recruit him?"
"Recruit him?" Whitehead Falcon scoffed.
"Do you think we have anything to offer him?"
"Money?
You think he lacks money?"
"Equipment?
Connections?
Luxury cars and beauties?"
The channel fell completely silent.
After a long pause, a voice came from the corner.
"Investigate and clarify exactly what his relationship is with the Violet Consortium family!"
"Everything about him must be investigated thoroughly, especially in the real world.
Step up efforts, and if necessary, involve the A-country intelligence agency!"
"I refuse to believe there’s anyone Morgan Consortium cannot find!"
[Stormbound Guild]
Vantheon stared at the name on the leaderboard, his face turning pale.
Level 100.
Count!
Legendary-grade pet!
Each word hit him like a slap to the face.
A subordinate cautiously asked, "Master, should we continue targeting him?"
Vantheon remained silent for a long while.
Then, gritting his teeth, he managed to say,
"Pause... for now."
"Pause?"
"Can’t you understand human language?
Pause!"
He smashed the cup in his hand.
"We’ll deal with him when the opportunity comes!"
The subordinate exhaled in relief.
No more suicide missions... at least for now.
Daniel closed the World Channel, a faint smile on his lips.
Their reactions were exactly what he had expected.
But it didn’t matter.
He no longer cared about others’ opinions.
Now, the only thing on his mind was strength.
Only that Final Catastrophe!
Once he dealt with that guy, he could leisurely enjoy life afterward.
He took a deep breath and headed toward the Intelligence Bureau.
The Intelligence Bureau was located in the northern district of Luminara, a heavy stone building.
A massive shield emblem hung over the entrance, flanked by fully armed guards.
Daniel entered through the gates into a spacious hall.
Maps and intelligence reports lined the walls, while several officer-looking figures spoke in low tones.
A tall, slender middle-aged man stood in the center, examining a huge sand table.
[Rex, Head of Luminara Intelligence Bureau (LV260)]
Daniel approached.
"Director Rex, I’m here to receive the mission."
Rex looked up and glanced at him.
"Oh?
The Count himself has arrived?"
His voice was calm and firm, carrying the crisp decisiveness of a soldier.
"The City Lord has briefed me—there is a mission assigned to you."
He picked up a scroll and handed it to Daniel.
[Intelligence Bureau Commission: Investigation of Savage Stone Settlement (S-Rank)]
[Mission Description: Recently, our scouts in the Savage Stone Mountains have detected abnormal activity.
The Beastfolk and Goblin tribes have been frequently contacting each other, suggesting a possible conspiracy.
Investigate the Savage Stone Settlement to collect evidence of collusion between the two tribes.]
[Objectives: Collect at least three valid pieces of evidence (secret letters, treaties, meeting records, etc.)]
[Difficulty: S-Rank]
[Recommended Level: 100+]
[Time Limit: 7 days]
[Rewards: Contribution Points +5,000; Merit Points +3,000; Gold Coins +100,000; Intelligence Bureau Treasure Chest ×1]
Daniel read the mission description, and memories of past lives flickered through his mind.
During the early stages of previous server openings, these two races had always been hostile toward each other.
Beastfolk looked down on Goblins, considering them inferior.
Goblins feared Beastfolk and fled whenever they appeared.
But one day, without warning, they suddenly united, causing massive losses for the Humans.
That battle saw countless players and NPCs perish, and several frontier cities were breached.
Had it not been for the combined counterattack of the major main cities, the consequences would have been disastrous.
Could it be that all of this began with this very conspiracy?
If he could preemptively dismantle this plot...
"Leave the mission to me."
Rex nodded.
"Good.
I’ll be waiting for your report, Count."
He paused, his expression serious.
"By the way, the Savage Stone Settlement is deep in Beastfolk territory.
The danger level is extremely high."
"If anything seems off, retreat immediately!"
Daniel smiled.
"Don’t worry."
He turned and exited the Intelligence Bureau, disappearing into the crowd.
Behind him, Rex watched his back thoughtfully.
"Level 100 adventurer... legendary-grade pet... no wonder the City Lord entrusted this mission to him."
He shook his head and returned to studying the intelligence in front of him.
Daniel looked up at the sky as he left the Bureau.
Savage Stone Mountains—the heart of Beastfolk territory.
With his current strength, he could face even a level 200 BOSS without worry.
And he still had so many trump cards.
He patted the little stone dragon on his shoulder.
The small creature was still asleep, softly snoring.
Daniel smiled and strode toward the portal.

chapters.title: Chapter 39 -39-The Letters Between the Wolfkin and the Goblins
paragraphs: Daniel carefully studied the Wolfkin.
They could be roughly divided into two types.
One type was the upright, intelligent Wolfkin. They were burly, averaging over two meters in height, covered in gray-brown fur, with wolf heads and humanoid bodies, eyes gleaming with intelligence.
They wore simple leather armor and carried spears, battle axes, and other weapons—clearly the warrior class of the settlement.
The other type were quadrupedal, primal wolf creatures.
These were true wolves, only two or three times the size of Earth wolves. Their shoulders stood over 1.5 meters high, muscles rippling across their bodies, fangs bared, eyes fierce.
They possessed no intelligence and followed the Wolfkin warriors’ commands completely. They were the Wolfkin’s most famous strategic asset—the mounts of the Wolf Cavalry.
Daniel narrowed his eyes.
Wolf Cavalry!
In his previous life, he had seen the destructive power of the Wolf Cavalry.
When deployed en masse, a Wolf Cavalry charge was a battlefield reaper.
Fast, explosive, and ferocious—the same number of human cavalry could not stand against them.
A thousand-strong Wolf Cavalry could even break a five-thousand-strong elite human army.
This was one of the most elite units of the Beastfolk, a strategic resource Humans had long coveted—of course, tamed.
Daniel shifted his gaze from the Wolf Cavalry and continued observing.
Besides Wolfkin, there were a few humans in the settlement.
Human merchants wove through the tents with goods, haggling with the Wolfkin. Some were trading ores, some furs, and a few were negotiating the price of Wolf Cavalry mounts.
Daniel was not surprised.
Though occasional friction occurred between Humans and Beastfolk, these were usually small-scale border skirmishes. On a larger scale, the two races had long conducted business together.
Humans needed top-tier strategic assets like Wolf Cavalry, while the Beastfolk needed human-made iron tools, food, and magical items.
Both sides got what they needed and maintained a surface-level peace—but only on the surface.
Daniel’s gaze settled on the largest tent at the edge of the settlement.
It was slightly larger than the others, flanked by two fully armed Wolfkin guards—clearly the chief’s residence.
According to the sentries’ intelligence, the Wolfkin had recently been in frequent contact with Goblins from the forest.
This was unusual.
Wolfkin had always looked down on Goblins, treating them as lowly creatures. When they met, they would kill them outright—there was no negotiating.
And yet now, they were cooperating peacefully?
Something was clearly going on.
Daniel gathered his thoughts and activated Voidstride.
His body instantly slipped into the interstice of the void, vanishing from sight.
Daniel moved silently through the void, approaching the largest tent.
The three-second invincibility of Voidstride had long passed, but the stealth effect remained.
As long as he didn’t attack or reveal himself, he could maintain this state indefinitely.
This was a trick he had discovered after obtaining the skill. Though it couldn’t be sustained forever, a brief period of concealment was more than sufficient.
He passed through the animal-skin walls and entered the interior.
Inside, three Wolfkin were seated around a rough wooden table.
The leader was particularly massive, silver-gray fur, wearing a necklace of bone teeth—each thumb-sized, taken from enemies he personally killed.
[Wolfkin Commander Greshkar (LV110, Gold-Grade BOSS)]
The other two Wolfkin were smaller but equally fierce, likely his personal guards.
Daniel silently moved into a corner, listening intently to their conversation.
"That group of green-skinned dwarves sent someone again," one guard spoke, his tone dripping with disgust.
"Seriously unlucky... just seeing their faces makes me want to vomit."
Greshkar chuckled lowly. "Bear it."
"Though I dislike them as much as you, this matter... isn’t simple."
"Commander, the Chieftain really intends to cooperate with them? What qualifications do those green-skinned dwarves have to stand equal with us?"
"Qualifications?" Greshkar’s eyes flashed coldly. "They have none. But this time, they have someone backing them."
"Who?"
"I don’t know. The Chieftain didn’t tell me."
Greshkar shook his head. "But for those cowards to risk their lives to deliver a message... whoever is behind them isn’t insignificant."
He paused, then continued, "Later, I’ve been ordered to send a small team into the forest to meet their messenger and see what they want."
The two guards exchanged a glance and fell silent.
Daniel’s mind stirred.
A message delivery?
This was his chance.
He silently exited the tent, finding a concealed spot to wait.

As the saying goes, "to catch a thief, follow the loot." Even if the humans suspected collusion between the Wolfkin and Goblins, until they had concrete evidence, they had to maintain a façade of peace.
Meanwhile, human intelligence agents had already withdrawn all merchants from the Wolfkin settlement.
This wasn’t a problem for the Wolfkin—especially at this critical time.
With the human merchants gone, operations were far easier!
By evening, a Wolfkin cavalry unit of over a hundred set out from the settlement, heading north toward the primeval forest.
But they didn’t notice a faint shadow trailing behind them.
At the forest edge, the Wolfkin cavalry halted.
A five-man squad ventured deeper into the woods.
Soon, a Wolfkin pulled a horn from its pouch and blew three short blasts and one long.
Immediately, rustling sounds arose from the trees.
A dozen green figures emerged—Goblins.
These creatures stood barely 1.2 meters tall, their skin a dark green, ears pointed, noses flat, teeth protruding. They wore tattered leather armor and carried crude short spears.
The lead Goblin was slightly taller, wearing a bone crown—clearly the leader.
It took a leather scroll from its pouch and presented it to the Wolfkin squad leader.
"Please... deliver this to Chief Bloodclaw," it croaked in a hoarse, servile voice. "It’s a personal letter from our High Priest—very important!"
The Wolfkin squad leader took the scroll, glancing at it with mild disdain before tossing it into his pouch.
"Understood. Now leave."
The Goblin leader nodded repeatedly, retreating into the forest with its subordinates.
Just as the Wolfkin squad prepared to return, a flash of silver light streaked through the air.
Thump! Thump! Thump! Thump! Thump!
Five muffled thuds rang almost simultaneously.
Five Wolfkin were pierced by arrows before they could react, collapsing instantly.
Daniel appeared from the void, walking to the fallen squad leader and retrieving the scroll from his pouch.
[Letter from the Goblin High Priest to Wolfkin Chief Bloodclaw]
The letter was long, but its essence was clear:
The Goblins were willing to pay a heavy price to request the Wolfkin to introduce them to the Beastfolk King, Lionheart.
If they could unite with Lionheart’s Beastfolk army, along with the Seafolk and Dark Elves...
Then there would be a chance!
At the end of the letter, the Goblin High Priest wrote almost in a pleading tone:
"As long as King Lionheart accepts us, the Goblins will dedicate all our resources!"
Daniel read the letter, his expression darkening.
Seafolk... Dark Elves...
In his previous-life memory, these two races had indeed participated in the Dark God coalition later.
He had assumed it was the Dark God’s manipulation, but it seemed these other races had begun their coalition much earlier than expected.
He tucked the letter into his backpack, preparing to leave, when a sudden roar erupted from behind:
"Human scum! Die!!!"

chapters.title: Chapter 40 -40-Irrefutable Evidence, Shattering the Wolfkin Spine
paragraphs: Daniel turned around.
In the distance, Greshkar rode a massive silver Wolf Cavalry, leading over a hundred Wolf Cavalry charging at full speed.
The earlier arrow had already alerted them.
"Kill him!!!"
Greshkar roared.
Over a hundred Wolf Cavalry let out a unified roar and surged forward like a tidal wave.
A faint smile curled on Daniel’s lips.
"Perfect timing."
Explosive Arrow Rain!
A barrage of arrows descended from above, blanketing the entire charging formation.
Boom!
Boom boom boom boom!
Explosions rang out continuously, smoke and dust billowing across the battlefield.
When the smoke cleared, more than thirty Wolf Cavalry at the front lay in mangled heaps, bodies torn apart.
The remaining Wolf Cavalry froze for a second, then charged even more frantically.
Daniel remained calm, drawing his bow and firing in rapid succession.
One arrow, one headshot.
The Wolf Cavalry could never get close—anyone entering fifty meters of him was immediately slain.
Occasionally, a stray arrow flew toward him, but with his current Agility, they crawled like turtles, easily avoided with a mere tilt of his head.
[Ding! You have killed Wolfkin Warriors ×47]
[Merit Points +470; Gained Experience...]
Greshkar, riding his silver Wolf Cavalry, watched his warriors fall one by one, his eyes blazing red.
"Damn humans! I’ll tear you apart!"
He dug his legs into the mount. The silver Wolf Cavalry became a streak of light, instantly charging toward Daniel.
Spear sweep!
Daniel activated God Speed, appearing ten meters away.
He casually tossed a reconnaissance skill.
[Wolfkin Commander·Greshkar (LV110·Gold-Grade BOSS)]
[Skills: Wolf Soul Roar, Frenzied Charge, Rending Claw, Dominion Power]
[Silvermoon Wolf Cavalry (LV100·Gold-Grade Mount)]
[Skills: Gale Dash, Rending Bite, Wolf Soul Guard]
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
A gold-grade commander paired with a gold-grade mount—fitting.
He stood still, not rushing to attack.
The Wolf Cavalry’s speed and explosive power were indeed terrifying—ordinary level-100 players could never react to a charge like that.
If he could arm his own Polaris City with such cavalry...
"What are you staring at?!"
Greshkar, furious, charged again.
Daniel sidestepped and shot an arrow into Silvermoon’s leg.
Howl—!
The mount screamed, speed immediately reduced.
"That all?"
Daniel shook his head.
Having finished his preliminary test, he drew the bow.
Aetherlance!
A golden spear tore through the air, instantly piercing Greshkar’s chest and exiting through Silvermoon’s body.
Boom—!
Both massive HP bars emptied simultaneously.
Greshkar looked down at the massive chest-sized hole in his body, disbelief in his eyes.
"You... you..."
Before he could finish, both he and Silvermoon were blown to pieces.
[Ding! You have killed Wolfkin Commander·Greshkar (Gold-Grade BOSS)]
[Merit Points +3,000]
[Obtained: Wolf Bone Necklace (Gold-Grade) ×1, Wolf Cavalry Training Manual (Special) ×1]
[Ding! You have killed Silvermoon Wolf Cavalry (Gold-Grade Mount)]
[Merit Points +900]
Daniel collected the loot and turned his gaze to the forest.
The Goblins had not gone far.
He vanished in an instant.
Three minutes later.
Deep in the forest, over a dozen Goblin corpses lay strewn about.
The lead Goblin widened its eyes, still clutching the letter it hadn’t yet delivered.
Daniel reached into its grasp and retrieved the reply, scanning it.
[Supplementary Notes on the Alliance Proposal]
The contents were similar to the previous letter, only more detailed, specifying alliance conditions and troop deployments.
Now the evidence was irrefutable—he could act without hesitation.
Pocketing the letter, Daniel activated God Speed again.
This time, he teleported directly into the center of the Wolfkin settlement.
Boom!
Explosive arrows rained down, covering the entire camp.
The detonations shook the ground, tents were blown away, Wolfkin warriors were shredded in confusion, and wolves scattered in panic.
In just three minutes, the combat power of the entire settlement was wiped out.
[Ding! You have killed Wolfkin Warriors ×427]
[Merit Points +5,670]
As the dust settled, a massive figure rose from the rubble.
A nearly four-meter-tall Wolfkin, dark-gold fur, muscles like stone.
He rode a massive black wolf and wielded an axe the size of a door.
[Wolfkin Chief·Bloodclaw (LV130·Blackgold-Grade BOSS)]
[Skills: Blood Frenzy, Ripper, Wolf God Possession, Death Charge...]
[Shadow Wolf Cavalry (LV120·Platinum-Grade Mount)]
[Skills: Shadow Warp, Deadly Bite, Shadow Shield]
Bloodclaw’s eyes were blood-red as he locked onto Daniel.
"Human!!! You shall die!!!"
He roared, his mount becoming a streak of black light, instantly appearing before Daniel.
The massive axe swung down!
Daniel dodged with God Speed.
Bloodclaw followed, warping through shadows with terrifying speed.
One rider, one mount, their attacks came like a raging storm!
But Daniel remained calm, observing while dodging.
Three minutes later, he nodded.
"Not bad... you’re capable."
Bloodclaw roared, "Are you mocking me?!"
"Something like that."
Daniel drew his bow.
Aetherlance!
The golden spear pierced Bloodclaw’s chest instantly and exited through Shadow.
Boom—!
Both massive HP bars vanished simultaneously.
Boom!
Bloodclaw and Shadow were shredded to pieces.
[Ding! You have killed Wolfkin Chief·Bloodclaw (Blackgold-Grade BOSS)]
[Merit Points +5,000]
[Obtained: Bloodclaw’s War Axe (Blackgold-Grade) ×1, Wolf God Totem (Epic-Grade) ×1]
[Ding! You have killed Shadow Wolf Cavalry (Platinum-Grade Mount)]
[Merit Points +1,500]
[Obtained: Shadow Wolf Cavalry Pup (Platinum-Grade Companion Egg) ×1]
Daniel collected the loot and surveyed his surroundings.
At the edge of the settlement, the surviving Wolfkin—elderly, weak, and women and children—cowered together, staring at him in terror.
No one dared resist.
Those who resisted... the fate of being torn to pieces lay right in front of them.
An old Wolfkin trembled forward and fell to his knees.
"P... please spare us, my lord!"
Daniel looked at him, silent for a few seconds.
"Submit, or die?"
The elder pounded the ground desperately. "Submit! We want to live! Please... let us live!"
"Good."
Daniel pulled a contract from his pocket.
[Servant Contract (Special)]
Effect: Upon signing, the signee becomes a permanent servant of the contract holder. Betrayal or resistance results in soul annihilation!
"Sign it, and take your people. Leave here forever, and go to Polaris City!"
"From now on, you are my servants."

[Skills: Wolf Soul Roar, Frenzied Charge, Rending Claw, Dominion Power]
[Silvermoon Wolf Cavalry (LV100·Gold-Grade Mount)]
[Skills: Gale Dash, Rending Bite, Wolf Soul Guard]
Daniel raised an eyebrow.
A gold-grade commander paired with a gold-grade mount—fitting.
He stood still, not rushing to attack.
The Wolf Cavalry’s speed and explosive power were indeed terrifying—ordinary level-100 players could never react to a charge like that.
If he could arm his own Polaris City with such cavalry...
"What are you staring at?!"
Greshkar, furious, charged again.
Daniel sidestepped and shot an arrow into Silvermoon’s leg.
Howl—!
The mount screamed, speed immediately reduced.
"That all?"
Daniel shook his head.
Having finished his preliminary test, he drew the bow.
Aetherlance!
A golden spear tore through the air, instantly piercing Greshkar’s chest and exiting through Silvermoon’s body.
Boom—!
Both massive HP bars emptied simultaneously.
Greshkar looked down at the massive chest-sized hole in his body, disbelief in his eyes.
"You... you..."
Before he could finish, both he and Silvermoon were blown to pieces.
[Ding!
You have killed Wolfkin Commander·Greshkar (Gold-Grade BOSS)]
[Merit Points +3,000]
[Obtained: Wolf Bone Necklace (Gold-Grade) ×1, Wolf Cavalry Training Manual (Special) ×1]
[Ding!
You have killed Silvermoon Wolf Cavalry (Gold-Grade Mount)]
[Merit Points +900]
Daniel collected the loot and turned his gaze to the forest.
The Goblins had not gone far.
He vanished in an instant.
Three minutes later.
Deep in the forest, over a dozen Goblin corpses lay strewn about.
The lead Goblin widened its eyes, still clutching the letter it hadn’t yet delivered.
Daniel reached into its grasp and retrieved the reply, scanning it.
[Supplementary Notes on the Alliance Proposal]
The contents were similar to the previous letter, only more detailed, specifying alliance conditions and troop deployments.
Now the evidence was irrefutable—he could act without hesitation.
Pocketing the letter, Daniel activated God Speed again.
This time, he teleported directly into the center of the Wolfkin settlement.
Boom!
Explosive arrows rained down, covering the entire camp.
The detonations shook the ground, tents were blown away, Wolfkin warriors were shredded in confusion, and wolves scattered in panic.
In just three minutes, the combat power of the entire settlement was wiped out.
[Ding!
You have killed Wolfkin Warriors ×427]
[Merit Points +5,670]
As the dust settled, a massive figure rose from the rubble.
A nearly four-meter-tall Wolfkin, dark-gold fur, muscles like stone.
He rode a massive black wolf and wielded an axe the size of a door.
[Wolfkin Chief·Bloodclaw (LV130·Blackgold-Grade BOSS)]
[Skills: Blood Frenzy, Ripper, Wolf God Possession, Death Charge...]
[Shadow Wolf Cavalry (LV120·Platinum-Grade Mount)]
[Skills: Shadow Warp, Deadly Bite, Shadow Shield]
Bloodclaw’s eyes were blood-red as he locked onto Daniel.
"Human!!!
You shall die!!!"
He roared, his mount becoming a streak of black light, instantly appearing before Daniel.
The massive axe swung down!
Daniel dodged with God Speed.
Bloodclaw followed, warping through shadows with terrifying speed.
One rider, one mount, their attacks came like a raging storm!
But Daniel remained calm, observing while dodging.
Three minutes later, he nodded.
"Not bad... you’re capable."
Bloodclaw roared, "Are you mocking me?!"
"Something like that."
Daniel drew his bow.
Aetherlance!
The golden spear pierced Bloodclaw’s chest instantly and exited through Shadow.
Boom—!
Both massive HP bars vanished simultaneously.
Boom!
Bloodclaw and Shadow were shredded to pieces.
[Ding!
You have killed Wolfkin Chief·Bloodclaw (Blackgold-Grade BOSS)]
[Merit Points +5,000]
[Obtained: Bloodclaw’s War Axe (Blackgold-Grade) ×1, Wolf God Totem (Epic-Grade) ×1]
[Ding!
You have killed Shadow Wolf Cavalry (Platinum-Grade Mount)]
[Merit Points +1,500]
[Obtained: Shadow Wolf Cavalry Pup (Platinum-Grade Companion Egg) ×1]
Daniel collected the loot and surveyed his surroundings.
At the edge of the settlement, the surviving Wolfkin—elderly, weak, and women and children—cowered together, staring at him in terror.
No one dared resist.
Those who resisted... the fate of being torn to pieces lay right in front of them.
An old Wolfkin trembled forward and fell to his knees.
"P... please spare us, my lord!"
Daniel looked at him, silent for a few seconds.
"Submit, or die?"
The elder pounded the ground desperately.
"Submit!
We want to live!
Please... let us live!"
"Good."
Daniel pulled a contract from his pocket.
[Servant Contract (Special)]
Effect: Upon signing, the signee becomes a permanent servant of the contract holder.
Betrayal or resistance results in soul annihilation!
"Sign it, and take your people.
Leave here forever, and go to Polaris City!"
"From now on, you are my servants."

chapters.title: Chapter 41 -41-Contracted Wolfkin
paragraphs: The old Wolfkin glanced at the remaining elders, women, and children, grief flickering across his eyes.
But in the end, trembling, he accepted the contract, signing it without even reading its contents.
Preserving the bloodline of the Wolfkin was already a tremendous mercy.
As for becoming a servant? Compared to death, it was meaningless.
The other surviving Wolfkin followed suit, signing one by one.
Over three hundred in total, mostly elders, women, and children, along with some young, underage Wolfkin.
Daniel pocketed the contracts, his gaze sweeping across the shivering Wolfkin.
"Go to Polaris City. Live differently, and train the Wolf Cavalry for me."
"I don’t care what you feel toward me—anger, hatred—I don’t care. But I’ll make this clear first!"
"If even one Wolfkin dares to betray me, the entire Wolfkin tribe will pay the price for your impulse!"
Faced with Daniel’s icy gaze, the Wolfkin lowered their heads.
Any previous thoughts or resentment vanished completely under this naked threat.
"However, rest assured—so long as you are loyal, I will never wrong you."
The old Wolfkin nodded repeatedly. "Yes! Yes! Yes! We will serve faithfully!"
Daniel nodded, activated God Speed, and vanished in an instant.
Luminara, Intelligence Bureau.
Daniel appeared silently in the main hall.
Rex was at his desk, studying something, and looked up at the sound.
"You’re back? Was there an... accident—"
His words cut off abruptly.
Daniel placed three items on the desk before him:
A handwritten letter from the Goblin High Priest.
A cooperation request from the Wolfkin Chief.
An identity token of the Wolfkin Chief.
"Evidence."
Daniel’s words were concise.
Rex froze for three seconds, then grabbed the letters, quickly scanning them.
The longer he read, the grimmer his expression became.
After finishing the last letter, he looked up at Daniel.
"Are you certain these are genuine?"
"I took them personally from the Goblin messenger and the Wolfkin."
Rex fell silent for a few seconds, then exhaled deeply.
"Good. Very good."
[Ding! Congratulations on completing the Intelligence Bureau Commission: Savage Stone Settlement Investigation (S-Rank)]
[Mission Rating: SSS (Overachieved)]
[Rewards: Contribution Points +8,000; Merit Points +5,000; Gold Coins +20,000]
Rex regarded him, admiration clear in his eyes.
"To be honest, I thought you’d need a week, perhaps even support."
"Yet you returned in a single day, with so much evidence."
He paused. "Count, you are the most capable adventurer I’ve ever seen."
Daniel smiled. "Is there a follow-up?"
"There is."
Rex pointed to an area on the map.
[Doomgreen Forest—Core Goblin Settlement]
"Since it’s confirmed that those wretched Goblins are conspiring, we cannot sit idly by."
"I have a new mission for you."
[Ding! Follow-Up Quest Triggered: Threat in Doomgreen Forest (SS-Rank)]
[Quest Description: Travel to Doomgreen Forest, investigate Goblin activities, and weaken their Strength as much as possible.]
[Objectives: Gather intelligence on Goblin intentions; Merit Points awarded per Goblin killed (1–100, depending on level)]
[Time Limit: Two months]
[Rewards: Determined by mission completion progress and kill count!]
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Killing Goblins earns Merit Points? This is basically a point-grinding opportunity!
But he didn’t immediately accept. Instead, he asked:
"Can I release this mission to other adventurers?"
Rex was momentarily stunned. "You?"
"I’m a Count. I have the authority to issue quests."
Daniel smiled. "Besides, there’s a limit to how many I can kill alone. If I mobilize all adventurers, the efficiency will be much higher."
Rex paused, then smiled.
"Clever. Alright, you may—but there’s a condition."
"First, you must submit a detailed operational plan. Execution requires the City Lord’s approval."
Daniel nodded. "No problem."
After leaving the Intelligence Bureau, Daniel went straight to the Lord’s Manor.
Augusta listened to his plan, thoughtful for a few seconds.
"Are you sure you want to do this?"
"Absolutely."
"Mobilize all adventurers to kill Goblins... do you understand the implications?"
"I do," Daniel said. "The Goblin tribe will come into open conflict with Humans, which may affect border security."
"But please trust that with adventurers’ Strength, we can defend the borders and protect all imperial citizens."
"And at the same time, this will greatly weaken the Goblin forces, improving border safety, trade security, and tax stability!"
"This benefits Luminara and the entire Empire."
Augusta stared at him for a moment, then smiled.
"You’ve got guts, I’ll give you that!"
He picked up his pen and signed the operational plan.
"Go ahead. I approve."
With approval secured, Daniel immediately began setting up the event.
[Event Name: Doomgreen Forest Purge Operation]

[Event Background: The Goblin tribe has recently exhibited unusual activity, suspected of colluding with hostile forces. To ensure border security, the Empire calls on all adventurers to investigate the Goblins’ true intentions and purge the tribe.]
[Participation: Pay 100 copper coins to accept the quest!]
[Event Duration: Effective immediately, two-month limit]
[Kill Rewards:]
Normal Goblin: 1–5 Merit Points
Goblin Warrior: 6–20 Merit Points
Goblin Leader: 30–100 Merit Points
Goblin Priest: 50–150 Merit Points
Goblin Commander: 50–200 Merit Points
[Merit Point Usage: Can be exchanged at the Intelligence Bureau Quartermaster for rare equipment, skill books, materials, etc.]

[Special Note: Event initiated by Doom Guild Leader and Count Faustus of Luminara. Three-tenths of all Merit Points gained from Goblins will automatically be given to the event initiator to offset costs.]
Daniel double-checked everything, then clicked "Publish."
The next second, the World Channel exploded.
"Holy shit?! What’s happening?!"
"Doomgreen Forest Purge Operation? Kill Goblins for Merit Points?!"
"Merit Points can be exchanged for what? Let me see... Holy shit! Even Gold-Grade equipment?!"
"This event was started by Faustus? He’s only level 100, how can he publish an event?!"
"He’s a Count, got it? Counts have the authority to issue quests!"
"I’m so salty... I’m seriously salty..."
"Team up! Anyone want to farm Goblins together?"
"Please take me! I’m only level 10, can I go?"
"Level 10 against Goblins is dangerous—better team up."
"Faustus is amazing! I love this event!"
"Three-tenths of Merit Points... cha-ching, free profit!"
"Well, he has to pay the event cost. Giving three-tenths is better than nothing."
"Sign me up! I’m farming Merit Points!"
